THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MAY 1, 1924

Certified Circulation

THE CHINA PRESS was founded in August, 1911, and has thus been in existence for rather under thirteen years, or sixty-one years less than that of its senior morning contemporary, the North-China Daily News.

Ten years after it had been established, THE CHINA PRESS published an audited statement showing that its gross average daily paid circulation totalled 4358, or exactly 150 more than the circulation shown by its contemporary in a statement published in May of the same year. This figure of 4358 was in no way the result of any special circulation campaign, but was for the month prior to that in which the much-discussed Automobile Show was held, which resulted in a further increase of circulation to THE CHINA PRESS.

In justice to its advertisers, THE CHINA PRESS will follow its former custom and publish audited returns, showing the gross average daily paid circulation, so soon as the suit brought against the Company by a former employee has been heard. In the meantime, however, advertisers may rest assured that they will be quite satisfied with the circulation attained by THE CHINA PRESS after its thirteen years of existence as compared to the latest returns exhibited this week by its seventy-four-year-old contemporary.

经核证发行量

《大陆报》创办于1911年8月，迄今存在尚不足十三年，比其资历更深的晨报同行《字林西报》少六十一年。

在该报创办十年后，《大陆报》公布了一份经审计的声明，显示其日均付费总发行量为4358份，恰好比其同行在同一年5月发布的声明中显示的发行量多出150份。这4358份的数字绝非任何特别发行推广活动的结果，而是出现在备受关注的汽车展举办前一个月的数据，该车展随后使《大陆报》的发行量进一步增加。

为了对广告商负责，《大陆报》将遵循以往惯例，在一名前雇员对公司提起的诉讼审理完毕后，尽快公布经审计的回执，显示日均付费总发行量。然而与此同时，广告商可以放心，相较于本周其七十四岁高龄的同行所展示的最新数据，《大陆报》在十三年的历程中所取得的发行量足以令他们满意。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS. WEDNESDAY, APRIL 30, 1924.

Our Certified Circulation—A Reply

In yesterday morning's correspondence there appeared a letter from one of our principal advertisers inquiring about the distribution of the "North-China Daily News" and the "North-China Herald." It is a fair question and one, we believe, that most advertisers and others would like to see answered by a certified statement such as we publish below.

This statement shows in brief that advertisers who only wish to appeal to Shanghai and the immediate neighbourhood will reach 4,200 subscribers by an announcement in the "North-China Daily News"; while those who desire to cover both Shanghai and the rest of China will reach 6,500 subscribers by advertising in both the "North-China Daily News" and the "North-China Herald." These two newspapers—the daily and the weekly—cover entirely different ground.

There is, it may be remarked, a considerable difference between the terms "subscriber" and "reader." Our newspapers are on file in most offices, in nearly all clubs, and we believe in all reading rooms and libraries not only in Shanghai but throughout China. Our readers, therefore, are probably two or three times the number of our subscribers as shown in the following statement.

Geographical Statement of Paid and Gross Circulation of North-China Daily News and North-China Herald during the month of March, 1924

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

Combined Paid Circulation in Shanghai, Outports, etc.
6,518

We have compared the above statement with the cash receipts, books and records of the North-China Daily News & Herald, Limited, and certify the same to be correct in accordance therewith.

THOMSON & Co., Chartered Accountants.

我们的经核证发行量——答复

在昨晨的通信栏目中，刊登了我们一位主要广告商的来信，询问《字林西报》和《北华捷报》的发行分布情况。这是一个合理的问题，我们相信大多数广告商及其他人士都希望看到如下文所示的经核证声明来予以回答。

该声明简要表明，仅希望覆盖上海及周边地区的广告商，通过在《字林西报》上刊登公告可触达4,200名订阅者；而希望同时覆盖上海及中国其他地区的广告商，通过在《字林西报》和《北华捷报》上同时刊登广告可触达6,500名订阅者。这两份报纸——日报和周报——覆盖的范围截然不同。

值得一提的是，“订阅者”和“读者”这两个术语之间存在相当大的差异。我们的报纸存档于大多数办公室、几乎所有俱乐部，并且我们相信不仅在上海，而且在整个中国的阅览室和图书馆中均有存档。因此，我们的读者数量可能是下文声明中所示订阅者数量的两到三倍。

The Far Eastern News Agency (遠東通訊社)
commenced to function on April 1, 1924. Its promoter
is Moh Kuh Ming (莫克明) who acts as manager of the
concern. The Editor is Yen Moh Sun (嚴謨聲). The
object of the Agency, as stated by Moh, is to foster
industry, and it has no political connections whatever.
The Capital is $20,000 of which, Moh States, he
contributed 50% and certain merchants and educationalists
the other 50%.

The Agency has six reporters in Shanghai and
between 20 to 30 in outports. Its expenses are
estimated at $1,000 per month, and its income is mainly
derived from the 600 subscribers to its service. Its
charges are $10 per month for local subscribers and $15
per month for outport subscribers.

Moh was educated in the Shanghai Baptist College
and in Tokyo where he took a commercial course, specialising
in Banking. During the past four years he has been in
Canton where he edited the Chinese newspaper "Bing Ming
Zuh Pao" (The Proletariat's Paper).

List of Foreign News Agencies which Supply
News to the Foreign and Chinese Press in Shanghai.
------------------
Reuter's, the well known British agency, No. 4 Avenue Edward VII.
Manager ; W. Turner, General Manager in the Far East,
Accountant ; A. H. C. Thompson.
This is probably the only news agency which offers
serious opposition in China to the Japanese and Chinese
agencies, but unlike the services of the two latter nationalities
which are subsidized, it appears to depend upon its earnings
for its upkeep. Reuter's service in China is partial to
Great Britain and the United States.

Rosta News Agency
The Rosta is the official agency of the Moscow Soviet
Government. It brings a service by telegraph into Peking and
distributes it locally gratis. It is purely a Bolshevik
propaganda service. It used to have a special agent in Shanghai
where its news is at present distributed by mail from Peking.
The activity of the Rosta News Agency is said to be very
noticeable in Peking and Canton.

The United Press
The United Press is the second largest news agency in
America. It brings a service into Japan through the Japan
Telegraphic News Agency and sends a direct service to China via
London and Peking. This service is received by telegram at
Peking where it is supplied to one or two newspapers for a nominal
charge. Items of special interest are telegraphed to Shanghai
(The China Press) and Hongkong (South China Morning Post) and
Hongkong Telegraph) which in return pay only the cost of the
telegram from Peking. In the Far East this service is allied
to the Japan Telegraphic News Agency which probably is the
pages.zh:
向上海外文及中文报纸提供新闻的外国新闻通讯社名录。
------------------
路透社（Reuter's），著名的英国通讯社，爱德华七世大道4号。
经理：W. 特纳（Turner），远东总经理，
会计：A. H. C. 汤普森（Thompson）。
这可能是唯一在中国与日本和中国通讯社形成有力竞争的新闻通讯社，但与后两个享有补贴的国家的服务不同，它似乎依靠自身收入维持运营。路透社在中国的服务偏向英国和美国。

罗斯塔通讯社（Rosta News Agency）
罗斯塔通讯社是莫斯科苏维埃政府的官方通讯社。它通过电报将服务引入北京，并在当地免费分发。这纯粹是布尔什维克的宣传服务。它过去在上海设有特派员，目前其新闻由北京通过邮件分发。据说罗斯塔通讯社在北京和广州的活动非常显著。

合众社（The United Press）
合众社是美国第二大新闻通讯社。它通过日本电报新闻社将服务引入日本，并通过伦敦和北京向中国发送直接服务。该服务在北京通过电报接收，并以象征性费用提供给一两家报纸。特别感兴趣的稿件被电传至上海（《大陆报》）和香港（《南华早报》及《香港电讯报》），作为回报，这些报纸仅支付从北京发出的电报费用。在远东，该服务与日本电报新闻社结盟，后者可能是

pages.en:
explanation of its ability to distribute news almost free.
There are nevertheless possibilities of making this service
pay, and it is probable the charges for the news it supplies
will be increased later. Reuter's American Service to China
has been extended to meet the competition of the United Press.

The French Wireless.
The French wireless is official and its news consists
largely of propaganda. Notwithstanding reports that the
French intended to stop the service, it is still being carried
on as vigorously as formerly. Reuter's sells a translation
of the service to local newspapers which, with the exception
of the North China Daily News and Mercury, publish all or
part of its news. There is a strong feeling in certain French
circles in the Far East that French propaganda in these parts
is not being pushed sufficiently.

Italian Wireless
The Italian Wireless, which is also propaganda, comes
in English at irregular intervals. It is picked up in Peking
and sent to Shanghai by post.
pages.zh:
解释其能够几乎免费分发新闻的能力。
尽管如此，使这项服务盈利仍有可能，且其提供的新闻收费日后可能会提高。路透社的美国对华服务已扩展，以应对合众社（United Press）的竞争。

法国无线电台。
法国无线电台是官方的，其新闻主要由宣传内容组成。尽管有报道称法国打算停止该服务，但它仍像以前一样 vigorously 地运作着。路透社向当地报纸出售该服务的译文，除《字林西报》（North China Daily News）和《捷报》（Mercury）外，其他报纸均刊登其全部或部分新闻。在远东的某些法国圈子里，有一种强烈的感觉，认为法国在这些地区的宣传力度不够。

意大利无线电台
意大利无线电台也是宣传性质的，不定期以英语播出。它在北京被接收，然后通过邮政寄往上海。

pages.en:
List of Japanese News Agencies in Shanghai
which supply news to the foreign and Chinese Press.
--------------------------

The Eastern News Agency.
(Toho Tsushin Sha.), No. 25 Ninghow Road.
Represented in Shanghai by a Japanese named I. Kata.
Established about 1915. Has correspondents all over China,
almost all of whom are either Japanese Consular officials
or persons in close touch with Japanese Consulates.
This agency is undoubtedly subsidized by the Japanese
Government, and is Reuter's most serious rival in China.
There is hardly any newspaper in China, foreign or
Chinese, which does not publish at least some of the news
emanating from the Eastern News Agency whose service is
almost free. It is conceivable that in a serious war in China
or Japan, in which censorship, cut cables and wireless
blanketing would play the usual part, that newspapers in China
would be almost entirely dependent upon the Eastern News
Agency for their information. There is good reason to
believe that Japanese Consular officials have instructions
from the Tokyo Foreign Office to give official news first
to the Eastern News Agency which has a preference over
foreign competitors on the Japanese telegraph lines In this
way it is able to forestall Reuter's and others and the
newspapers cannot afford to ignore it. Mr. Hata left
Shanghai on February 27 en route for the United States
on a world tour.

The Japan Telegraphic News Agency.
Nihon Dempo Tsushin Sha, No. 3 Foochow Road.
Represented in Shanghai by H.S. Kodama.
This agency, which is perhaps the most influential local
news agency in Japan, is subsidized by the Seiyukai Party.
pages.zh:
在上海向外国和华文报业提供新闻的日本通讯社名单
--------------------------

东方通讯社。
(Toho Tsushin Sha.)，宁波路25号。
在上海由一名叫 I. Kata 的日本人代表。
成立于1915年左右。在中国各地设有通讯员，其中几乎所有人都是日本领事馆官员或与日本领事馆关系密切的人士。
该通讯社无疑受到日本政府的资助，是路透社在中国最严重的竞争对手。
中国几乎没有一家报纸，无论是外文还是中文，不刊登至少部分来自东方通讯社的新闻，因为其服务几乎是免费的。可以设想，如果在中国或日本发生严重战争，审查制度、切断电缆和无线电信号干扰将发挥通常的作用，那么中国的报纸将几乎完全依赖东方通讯社获取信息。有充分理由相信，日本领事官员接到东京外务省的指示，首先将官方新闻提供给东方通讯社，该社在日本电报线上享有优于外国竞争对手的特权。通过这种方式，它能够先发制人，胜过路透社和其他机构，而报纸也不敢忽视它。Hata 先生于2月27日离开上海，途经美国进行环球旅行。

日本电报通讯社。
Nihon Dempo Tsushin Sha，福州路3号。
在上海由 H.S. Kodama 代表。
该通讯社也许是日本当地最有影响力的新闻机构，受到政友会（Seiyukai Party）的资助。

pages.en:
Its President is a prominent politician named Matsumaga.
It supplies a number of newspapers in China, including
the China Press, with both foreign (through the United
Press, an American Agency) and Japanese news. The Japan
Telegraphic News Agency is fairly well organized in China,
but is not nearly so formidable as the Eastern News Agency.
It was established in 1918.

The Shunshin News Agency
(Taushin Sha) No. 826 Miller Road. Owned by a Japanese
named T. Watanabe. Deals with economic matters about
which it extracts a good deal of information from the
Chinese newspapers. Established in 1916.

The Shunshin Translation News Agency( Shunshin Honyaku
Taushin, No. 8 Quinan Thantzin Road) Owned by a Japanese named
J. Nishimura. Makes translations of interesting news
bearing on political and other subjects. Established in 1917.

Eastern Asiatic News Agency
(The Taushin Sha) No. 67 Thorne Road. Owned by a
Japanese named Sasaki . Deals with all interesting news
but is not influential. Established in 1923.
pages.zh:
其总裁是一位名叫 Matsumaga 的著名政治家。
它向中国多家报纸提供新闻，包括《大陆报》（China Press），既有外国新闻（通过美国机构合众社），也有日本新闻。日本电报通讯社在中国的组织相当完善，但远不如东方通讯社那样令人畏惧。
它成立于1918年。

顺信通讯社
(Taushin Sha) 米勒路826号。由一名叫 T. Watanabe 的日本人拥有。处理经济事务，并从中文报纸中提取大量相关信息。成立于1916年。

顺信翻译通讯社 (Shunshin Honyaku Taushin，祁南坦津路8号) 由一名叫 J. Nishimura 的日本人拥有。翻译涉及政治和其他主题的有趣新闻。成立于1917年。

东亚通讯社
(The Taushin Sha) 索恩路67号。由一名叫 Sasaki 的日本人拥有。处理所有有趣的新闻，但影响力不大。成立于1923年。

pages.en:
The Kuo Wen News Agency ( 社信通聞國) is
one of the first Chinese news agencies to be started
in Shanghai. It was organised by Wu Tsung Tse
( 之政胡 ) , a Chinese journalist, in October,
1921. It has now established a name for itself,
and its service is taken by practically all the
newspapers in Shanghai, whilst a number of private
families also subscribe to it. It has a large
number of newspapers on its foreign and outport
service also. The amount of the Capital of the
concern is not known, but it is believed that
a syndicate of ten to twelve persons started it
as an experiment with limited funds, and as the
business developed and became more flourishing,
more money was put into the undertaking. The
present day expenses of the Agency do not exceed
$800 per month. The Agency has correspondents in
all the principal cities in China. The income of
the agency is not inconsiderable. The Editor is
Li Tse Kwan ( 宽子李 ).

Address: 202/203 Shantung Road.
pages.zh:
国闻通讯社 ( 社信通聞國 ) 是
上海最早成立的中文通讯社之一。它由
中国记者胡宗政 ( 之政胡 ) 于1921年10月
组织成立。它现在已建立起自己的声誉，
其服务实际上被上海所有报纸采用，同时
许多私人家庭也订阅它。它在外国和外埠
服务方面也有大量报纸客户。该机构的资
本数额不详，但据信是由一个十至十二人
的辛迪加以有限资金作为实验创办的，随
着业务的发展和繁荣，更多的资金投入了
该项目。该通讯社目前的支出不超过每月
800美元。该通讯社在中国所有主要城市
设有通讯员。该通讯社的收入相当可观。
编辑是李子宽 ( 宽子李 )。

地址：山东路202/203号。

pages.en:
The China News Agency (中國新聞社) was
established in the fifth year of the Republic
by two men, Tsung Chuin (陳清), owner
of the"Young China", a newspaper published
in San Francisco where he is at present,
and Sun Chao Lu (吳景濂 沈卓吾) who is
connected with the China Evening News in
whose offices the Agency is located. The
capital is provided by emigrants who sent
in their subscriptions from abroad. Every
day the Agency sends out 230 copies of its
service, and with the exception of 14 copies
to local newspapers and private families, the
remainder are despatched abroad. Its charges
are $60 per month for outport subscribers,
and $6 for local subscribers. Its expenses
are estimated at about $1,500 per month.
The Agency is a supporter of the Kuomintang
Party.
Address: 258 Nanking Road.
pages.zh:
中国新闻社 (中國新聞社) 成立于
民国五年，由两人创办，陈清 (陳清)，
旧金山出版的《少年中国报》(Young China)
的所有者，他目前就在旧金山；以及沈卓吾
吳景濂 沈卓吾，他与《中国晚报》有关联，
通讯社就设在该报办公室内。资本由海外
侨民从国外汇款认购提供。该通讯社每天
发出230份服务稿件，除14份发给当地报
纸和私人家庭外，其余均发往国外。其收
费标准为外埠订阅者每月60美元，本地订
阅者每月6美元。其支出估计约为每月1,500
美元。该通讯社支持国民党。
地址：南京路258号。

pages.en:
The Lien Huh News Agency (联合通讯社)
was established by Li Tse Sai, (李次山) a
Chinese barrister-at-law, about six years ago.
During the past year it was subsidised by Wu
Chien Lien (吴景濂), Speaker in the House
of Representatives, but since his fall from
favour after the election of Tsao Kun to the
Presidency, this subsidy has been discontinued,
and the Agency is in bad financial condition.
Only seven Chinese newspapers receive this
service. Its expenses amount to $300 per
month. The Editor is Yue Yi Yung (余翼文).
Address: 133 Peichow Road.
pages.zh:
联合通讯社 (联合通讯社)
由华人律师李次山 (李次山) 于大约六年前
成立。在过去的一年里，它得到了众议院
议长吴景濂 (吴景濂) 的资助，但自从曹
锟当选总统后吴失势以来，这笔资助已停
止，该通讯社财务状况不佳。只有七家中
文报纸接收此服务。其支出为每月300美
元。编辑是余翼文 (余翼文)。
地址：北周路133号。

pages.en:
The Dah Doong News Agency ( 大同 ) was
started by its proprietor Ma Voong Sze (馬鳳池)
about four years ago. It specialises in local
news items and sends but few telegrams to the
newspapers subscribing to its service. Capital
unknown. Its policy is stated to be to bring
about the reunification of the country by means
of peaceful methods. There is reason to believe
that this Agency is pro-Anfu in political
feeling; and that it is closely connected with
the notorious Little Hsu. Editor: Chao Ching Hai
(趙清漢). Address of Agency: 1565 Kwang Ming
Lee (廣仁里), Chengtu Road.
pages.zh:
大同通讯社 ( 大同 ) 由其所有者马凤池
(馬鳳池) 于大约四年前创办。它专门从事
本地新闻报道，向订阅其服务的报纸发送
的电报很少。资本不详。据称其政策是通
过和平手段实现国家统一。有理由相信，
该通讯社在政治情感上亲安福系；并且与
臭名昭著的小徐关系密切。编辑：赵清汉
(趙清漢)。通讯社地址：成都路广仁里
(廣仁里) 1565号。

pages.en:
The Soo Soo News Agency (蘇蘇通信社) was
established in May, 1925 by members of the 55 out
of the 60 District Councils in Jiangsu province
with the object of agitating and propagating the
restoration of these Councils and the establishment of
self-government in the Province of Jiangsu. Each
of the 55 District Councils contributed a share
and the total amount of money thus raised was
$5,000. The expenses of the Agency do not exceed
$500 per month. Its service is taken on by the
nine large Chinese newspapers in Shanghai who pay
on an average $6 per month for its use. The manager
is Li Yu Tse (李佑之) Chairman of the District
Council.
Address: 382 North Shensi Road.
pages.zh:
苏苏通讯社 (蘇蘇通信社) 成立于
1925年5月，由江苏省60个区议会中的55个
的成员建立，目的是鼓动和宣传恢复这些
议会并在江苏省建立自治。这55个区议会
各出资一份，筹集的资金总额为5,000美元。
该通讯社的支出不超过每月500美元。上海
的九家大型中文报纸采用其服务，平均每
月支付6美元使用费。经理是区议会主席李
佑之 (李佑之)。
地址：陕西北路382号。

pages.en:
The Chung 'ha News Agency (中華通信社 )
was started by Jue An Dong (瞿愛棠 ) who is
also the Editor. There are twelve promoters
whose names are unknown. Its correspondents are
not paid and for this reason the expenses of the
Agency in a month amount to only about $100
per month. The Civil Governor of Chekiang,
Chang Tsai Yang, contributes $100 a month towards the
expenses of the concern. The Agency is a strong
supporter of General Lu Yun; Xiang.
Address:M 1790 Avenue Road.
pages.zh:
中华通讯社 (中華通信社 )
由瞿爱棠 (瞿愛棠 ) 创办，他也是编辑。
有十二位发起人，姓名不详。其通讯员没
有报酬，因此该通讯社每月的支出仅约100
美元。浙江省省长张载阳 (Chang Tsai Yang)
每月为该机构贡献100美元用于开支。该通
讯社是卢永祥将军的坚定支持者。
地址：爱文义路 M 1790号。

pages.en:
The Tung-Nan News Agency (東南通訊社) was
started in May, 1923 by Sung Siao Yoh (沈小霞 )
who is also the Editor. Its expenses amount
to about $300 per month. Tang Chi Yao (唐继尧)
Tuciun of Yunnan, contributes about $300
per month. The Agency employs five reporters
in Shanghai and four abroad. Subscribers to
its service number 30, local and outports
included. The Capital is subscribed by a
small syndicate of five persons, but the amount
is unknown.
Address: 7 Shantung Road.
pages.zh:
东南通讯社 (東南通訊社) 成立于
1923年5月，由沈小霞 (沈小霞 ) 创办，他
也是编辑。其支出约为每月300美元。云南
督军唐继尧 (Tang Chi Yao) 每月贡献约300
美元。该通讯社在上海雇用五名记者，在
国外雇用四名。其订阅者数量为30家，包
括本地和外埠。资本由一个五人小辛迪加
认购，但金额不详。
地址：山东路7号。

pages.en:
The Chun Hwa News Agency (中外通訊社) was
established by Tseu Shiao ligoh (周孝諤) one
of the Editors of the China Times, a local Chinese
newspaper, in 1923. It is in bad financial straits.
As far as could be ascertained, the Agency has no
political connections. Its office is located at
No. 38 Ling Ying Road, West Gate. The service
has hardly any subscribers.
pages.zh:
中外通讯社 (中外通訊社) 由
本地中文报纸《时报》(China Times) 的编
辑之一周孝諤 (Tseu Shiao ligoh) 于1923年
成立。它处于财务困境中。据查，该通讯
社没有政治联系。其办公室位于西门灵英
路38号。该服务几乎没有订阅者。

pages.en:
Hung Pin; News Agency (公平通信社).
Started by Li Siao Nan(李小南), a prominent member
of the Anhwei Fellow Countrymen's Association,
16 Kuling Road, in 1922. It is said to be subsidized
by General Ho Fung Ling, Military Governor of Shanghai
and Chekiang. It distributes news free of charge
to fifteen local Chinese newspapers and an equal
number of prominent Anhwei Residents in Shanghai.
Address : 747 Avenue Edward VII,
French Concession.
pages.zh:
公平通讯社 (公平通信社)。
由安徽同乡会 prominent member 李小南
(李小南) 于1922年在古岭路16号创办。据
说它得到淞沪护军使兼浙江督军何丰林
(Ho Fung Ling) 将军的资助。它向十五家
本地中文报纸和同等数量的上海知名安徽
籍居民免费分发新闻。
地址：法租界爱德华七世路747号，

pages.en:
Hung Pin News Agency ( 公平通信社 )。
Started by Li Siao Nan ( 李小南 ), a prominent member
of the Anhwei Delta Countrymen's Association,
16 Hubin Road, in 1922. It is said to be subsidized
by General Lo Heng Ling, Military Governor of Anhwei
and Kiangsu. It distributes news free of charge
to fifteen local Chinese newspapers and an equal
number of prominent Anhwei Residents in Shanghai.
Address : 747 Avenue Edward VII,
French Concession.
pages.zh:
公平通讯社 ( 公平通信社 )。
由安徽同乡会 prominent member 李小南
( 李小南 ) 于1922年在湖滨路16号创办。据
说它得到安徽兼江苏督军罗恒林 (Lo Heng
Ling) 将军的资助。它向十五家本地中文报
纸和同等数量的上海知名安徽籍居民免费
分发新闻。
地址：法租界爱德华七世路747号，

pages.en:
H.B.M. Consulate-General,
SHANGHAI,
19th February, 1924.

CONFIDENTIAL

My dear Hilton-Johnson,
I beg to acknowledge,
with thanks, receipt of your letter of yester-
day transmitting notes on newspapers published
in Shanghai together with some notes of my
own and the confidential Guide to the Press of
Asia.
I have read the notes carefully and take
this opportunity to express to Mr. McEuen and
you our gratitude for the service you have
rendered in providing this Consulate with such
an exhaustive up to date report on the local
press, and my particular thanks for the
speeding up of the work which has been carried
out through the China New Year holidays so
ably by your special staff. The report is
now being copied for the Foreign Office and the
Legation/
Major A. H. Hilton-Johnson,
etc. etc. etc.,
Shanghai Municipal Council.
pages.zh:
英国驻上海总领事馆，
上海，
1924年2月19日。

机密

亲爱的希尔顿-约翰逊：
我谨此确认，并感谢收到你昨日的来信，
信中转交了关于上海出版报纸的笔记，以
及我自己的一些笔记和《亚洲报业机密指
南》。
我已仔细阅读了这些笔记，并借此机会向
麦克尤恩先生和你表示我们的感激之情，
感谢你们为本领事馆提供了如此详尽、时
效性强的当地报业报告，并特别感谢你加
快工作进度，这项工作由中国新年假期期间
你的特别团队出色地完成。该报告正在复
印，以便送交外交部和公使馆/
A. H. 希尔顿-约翰逊 少校，
等等，等等，等等，
上海工部局。

REPORT ON News-papers Published in Shanghai.

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by...

Sir,

In accordance with your instructions, I am attaching herewith lists and short accounts of the daily newspapers in Chinese and newspapers and periodicals published in English, French, Russian, and Japanese in Shanghai. I am returning herewith the notes re Chinese publications and the book entitled 'A Guide to the Press of Asia.'

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. I.

D. C. I.

North China Daily News, 17 The Bund, Shanghai -
Daily paper, founded in 1864 issuing a weekly edition,
the North China Herald. Owned by the North China Daily
News and Herald Ltd., whose principal shareholders are
Mr. H. M. Morris and Mr. G. Morris. The largest daily
paper printed in English published in China, Japan
and the Straits. It has also the largest circulation,
subscription list and advertisement income, and is the
official organ for Consular, Municipal and Legal notices.
Capital, 250,000 taels. General reputation, first class.
Circulation 5,000 to 6,000 daily. Caters for all
foreign and English-speaking residents of Shanghai, the
larger cities of the China coast, and the Yangtse Valley,
and aims at maintaining and developing British trade in
the East. Has correspondents at Peking and in fifty
three other cities in China, who write on all phases
of Chinese trade, agriculture, politics, etc. Has also
correspondents in London, Edinburgh, Paris, Manila, Washington,
Vancouver, Montreal, Sydney, etc. In British politics
the present editor endeavours to favour the Conservative
party. The paper generally supports British interests.
The cosmopolitan nature of the community to which it
caters is nevertheless reflected in its articles which
appear to aim at upholding all foreign interests in China.
It is partial to France and the United States. It is very
critical when dealing with Chinese matters and to
a greater extent adopts the same attitude towards Japan.
The Chinese writer on its editorial staff, who is in the
pay of Chinese officials, carries on propaganda work on
their behalf in some of the articles which he contributes.
The best newspaper advertising medium in the East.
Proprietor : The North China Daily News & Herald Ltd.

1924年2月18日

《字林西报》，上海外滩17号 -
日报，创刊于1864年，发行周报版《北华捷报》。由字林洋行有限公司（North China Daily News and Herald Ltd.）所有，其主要股东为 H. M. Morris 先生和 G. Morris 先生。是在中国、日本和海峡殖民地出版的发行量最大的英文日报。其发行量、订阅名单和广告收入也最大，是领事馆、工部局和法律公告的官方刊登机构。资本25万两白银。总体声誉一流。日发行量5,000至6,000份。面向上海、中国沿海大城市及长江流域的所有外籍人士和讲英语的居民，旨在维持和发展英国在东方的贸易。在北京及中国其他五十三个城市设有通讯员，撰写有关中国贸易、农业、政治等各方面的文章。在伦敦、爱丁堡、巴黎、马尼拉、华盛顿、温哥华、蒙特利尔、悉尼等地也设有通讯员。在英国政治方面，现任编辑力求偏向保守党。该报总体上支持英国利益。尽管如此，其所服务的社群具有国际性，这也反映在其文章中，这些文章似乎旨在维护所有外国在华利益。该报偏向法国和美国。在处理中国事务时非常挑剔，并在更大程度上对日本采取相同态度。其编辑部中的一名中文撰稿人受雇于中国官员，在其贡献的一些文章中代表他们进行宣传工作。是东方最好的报纸广告媒介。
所有者：字林洋行有限公司（The North China Daily News & Herald Ltd.）

THE NORTH CHINA HERALD AND SUPREME COURT AND CONSULAR GAZETTE.
(17, The Bund, Shanghai).- Weekly edition of the North China Daily
News (Shanghai). Founded, 1850. Owned by the North China Daily
News and Herald, Ltd. Three supplements are issued with it: The
Municipal Gazette, The North China Herald Telegraphic Supplement,
and the North China Daily News and Herald, Ltd., Weekly Share
Supplement. Capital. 250,000 taels. The sub-title is indicative
of its standing. Circulation, 1,800-2,000, which is larger than
that of any other weekly. Published specially for circulation in
the interior of China, where mails are comparatively infrequent,
and a bulky paper would entail heavy postage; at the same time
contains more news matter than other weeklies. It reaches practically
all Consular, Customs, and Postal officials, business men and
missionaries in the interior. Under the same Directorship as, and
shares the Editorial Staff and Correspondents of the North China
Daily News. Its policy is British, and is aimed at establishing
British trade and interests in the Far East. The remarks about
the North China Daily News applies to its policy regarding Chinese
politics.
A useful medium for advertisements likely to appeal to
foreigners and officials in the interior of China.
For staff see North China Daily News (Shanghai).

《北华捷报及最高法庭与领事馆公报》。
（上海外滩17号）。- 《字林西报》（上海）的周报版。创刊于1850年。由字林洋行有限公司（North China Daily News and Herald, Ltd.）所有。随报附发三份增刊：《工部局公报》、《北华捷报电讯增刊》以及字林洋行有限公司《每周股票增刊》。资本25万两白银。其副标题表明了其地位。发行量1,800-2,000份，大于任何其他周报。专门为中国内地发行而出版，那里邮件相对稀少， bulky 的报纸会导致高昂邮资；同时包含的新闻内容比其他周报更多。它实际上送达内地所有的领事馆、海关和邮政官员、商人和传教士手中。由与《字林西报》相同的董事会领导，并共享《字林西报》的编辑人员和通讯员。其政策是英国的，旨在建立英国在远东的贸易和利益。关于《字林西报》的评论适用于其对中国政治的政策。
是一种有用的广告媒介，可能吸引中国内地的外国人和官员。
工作人员见《字林西报》（上海）。

THE CHINA PRESS, 14 Kiukiang Road, Shanghai -
Daily paper (except Mondays). Founded 1911. Published
by the China Press Inc., a company registered in Delaware,
U. S. A. The capital consists of 10,000 shares of G.$5.00
each, and the controlling interests is held by Sopher & Co.
British Jews, in their capacity as executors of the Edward
Ezra estate. Other important shareholders are Dr. Crane, a
former American Minister to China, Rev. G. Castrillo, Spanish
Augustinian R. C. Mission, and H. C. Norman, British. The
circulation is between 4,000 and 5,000. The paper caters for
foreigners and English-reading Chinese. It receives news
through all Reuter's services as well as American, French,
Italian and German wireless. It obtains Chinese news through
a Chinese member of the editorial staff who appears to be
well informed, and in addition has over eighty correspondents
in the interior. In home politics it is non-partisan, but
supports American interests in China. It opposes the Japanese
chauvinist policy in China and the pretentions of that nation
to have special rights in this country. At present it appears
to be favourably disposed towards Great Britain. It is also
partial to progressive movements in China and has a large
circulation among English speaking Chinese officials, merchants
and students in treaty ports and the interior. It seems to
be deferential to the opinions of this section of its readers
in matters affecting China. In spite of its policy of
neutrality in Chinese politics it publishes at infrequent
intervals propaganda favouring one or other of the Chinese
militarists in their quarrels with one another. American
and British editorials are contributed by J.B.Powell and R.
Peyton-Griffin respectively. It is a good advertising medium.
The staff consist of :-
H. C. Norman, General Manager,

《大陆报》，上海九江路14号 -
日报（周一除外）。创刊于1911年。由大陆报公司（China Press Inc.）出版，这是一家在美国特拉华州注册的公司。资本由10,000股组成，每股5美元，控股权由 Sopher & Co. 持有，他们是英国犹太人，作为 Edward Ezra 遗产的执行人。其他重要股东包括前美国驻华公使 Crane 博士、西班牙奥古斯丁罗马天主教传教团的 G. Castrillo 牧师，以及英国人 H. C. Norman。发行量在4,000至5,000之间。该报面向外国人和懂英语的中国人。它通过路透社的所有服务以及美国、法国、意大利和德国的无线电台接收新闻。它通过编辑部中一名似乎消息灵通的中国成员获取中国新闻，此外在中国内地还有八十多名通讯员。在国内政治方面，它不持党派立场，但支持美国在华利益。它反对日本在华的沙文主义政策以及该国声称在本国拥有特权的企图。目前看来它对大英帝国持友好态度。它也偏向中国的进步运动，在通商口岸和内地的讲英语的中国官员、商人和学生中拥有大量读者。在涉及中国的事务上，它似乎尊重这部分读者的意见。尽管其在中国政治中保持中立政策，但它偶尔会刊登宣传文章，支持中国军阀在相互争斗中的某一方。美国和英国的社论分别由 J.B. Powell 和 R. Peyton-Griffin 撰写。是一个良好的广告媒介。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, 21 Museum Road, Shanghai -
Daily paper. Founded about 1895. It is the property of
a British subject, but its policy appears to be controlled
by Japanese. General reputation good. Circulation 1,250
except on Sundays when it reaches 3,200. Caters for a
cosmopolitan public. Exchanges news with other papers.
Has correspondents throughout China, and also in London,
New York, etc. In home politics hostile to Labour, and
inclined to be partial to Liberalism. Its general attitude
towards the officials and people in China may be described
as very captious. It usually favours the Northern Party and
is very antagonistic to Dr. Sun Yat Sen and other leaders
holding radical views. It supports the interests of all
foreign nations, especially Great Britain and Japan. Its
comments nevertheless are very often unfavourable to France.
A fairly useful advertising medium, especially the Sunday
Edition.

《上海泰晤士报》，上海博物馆路21号 -
日报。创刊于1895年左右。它属于一位英国臣民，但其政策似乎由日本人控制。总体声誉良好。发行量1,250份，周日达到3,200份。面向国际公众。与其他报纸交换新闻。在中国各地以及伦敦、纽约等地设有通讯员。在国内政治方面敌视工党，倾向于偏向自由主义。其对中国官员和民众的总体态度可描述为非常吹毛求疵。它通常偏向北方派系，并对孙中山博士及其他持有激进观点的领导人非常敌对。它支持所有外国国家的利益，特别是大英帝国和日本。尽管如此，其评论往往对法国不利。是一个相当有用的广告媒介，尤其是周日版。

Shanghai Mercury, 5 Hongkong Road, Shanghai.
Evening daily paper, with which is incorporated
the Shanghai Courier. Founded 1879. Owned by the
Shanghai Mercury Ltd. The majority of the shares
which are registered in the name of a Briton, are
held by Japanese who, it is believed, are agents of the
Japanese Government. The proprietors issue a weekly

The "NEW SHANGHAI LIFE" 47 Boone Road, Corner of Seward Road 18/2/24
The newspaper is published in Russian daily (except Mondays).
Founded in 1919 under the name of the "Shanghai Life" by G. F.
Semeshko, a well-known Bolshevik. In 1922 the newspaper changed
its name when its former proprietor, Semeshko, handed it over
to its present owners, the "New Shanghai Life Publishing
Company". Believed to be subsidised by the Central Asiatic
Bureau of Propaganda, Moscow. The circulation is about 700.
Receives foreign news from Reuter's and "Rosta" Agencies, and
copies extensively from Russian, American, British and French
papers. Correspondents in a few large cities in China. Supports
the present Soviet Government in Russia, and execrates all its
enemies. Has shown a friendly attitude towards Great Britain,
Italy and Germany since these countries recognized the Soviet
Government. Very hostile to France and America. Advocates
a strong policy on the part of Russia towards China, and is
very friendly towards Dr. Sun-Yat-sen's party. In disputes
between Chinese and foreigners not of Russian nationality, it
is inclined to support the former.
Useful in some ways as an advertising medium.
The principal members of the editorial staff of the
newspaper are Messrs: V. Nesvadba, Doenin, D. Leontieff,
S. Podgursky, Strijevsky, Fomin and Russanoff, the first
five being the ostensible owners of the publication and also
members of the "Editorial Board".
pages.zh:
《新上海生活报》（"NEW SHANGHAI LIFE"），布恩路47号，西华德路转角 1924年2月18日
该报以俄文每日出版（星期一除外）。
1919年由著名的布尔什维克 G. F. Semeshko 以《上海生活报》之名创办。1922年，当原业主 Semeshko 将其移交给现任所有者“新上海生活出版公司”时，该报更改了名称。据信由莫斯科中亚宣传局提供补贴。发行量约为700份。从路透社和“罗斯塔”（Rosta）通讯社接收国际新闻，并大量转载俄罗斯、美国、英国和法国报纸的内容。在中国少数大城市设有通讯员。支持俄罗斯目前的苏维埃政府，并谴责其所有敌人。自英国、意大利和德国承认苏维埃政府以来，对该三国表现出友好态度。对法国和美国非常敌视。主张俄罗斯对中国采取强硬政策，并对孙中山博士的党派非常友好。在中籍人士与非俄籍外籍人士的纠纷中，倾向于支持前者。
在某些方面作为广告媒介是有用的。
该报编辑部的主要成员有：V. Nesvadba、Doenin、D. Leontieff、S. Podgursky、Strijevsky、Fomin 和 Russanoff 先生，前五人是该出版物的名义所有者，也是“编辑委员会”的成员。

from other papers, Friendly to all nations except Soviet
Russia which it consistently condemns. The paper is particularly
friendly to America, France and Serbia. In its local policy,
it aims at upholding foreign interests in China.
Not much use as an advertising medium.
The principal members of the editorial staff are Messrs:
Agapoff, manager, Popoff, acting editor, Zenkovitch and Nadejdin.

作为广告媒介用处不大。
编辑部主要成员有：经理 Agapoff，代理编辑 Popoff，Zenkovitch 和 Nadejdin 先生。

CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW (formerly Millard's Review) 113, Avenue
Edward VII, Shanghai.- Weekly paper. Founded, June, 1917. Owned
by THE Millard Publishing Company, Inc. (Delaware). Capital,
100,000 dollars. Describes itself as having a very high reputation
among Americans, British and Chinese of Liberal tendencies, and
declares itself to be decidedly unpopular among the Japanese
and other reactionary elements in the Orient. The paper sometimes
publishes matters prejudicial to British prestige and interests.
Circulation (paid-up subscriptions), 5,000. Caters for the
English-reading public in all parts of China. It is widely read
by English speaking Chinese, especially the student element.
Deference to the opinions of this section of its readers is
noticeable in its writings. Subscribes to the Chung Mei Agency,
Peking, and to the Far Eastern Advertising Agency, London. About
100 leading Chinese newspapers reprint its editorials and leading
articles. In America it is the most quoted journal published in
the Orient. In American politics, it seems to be most partial
to the Republicans; claims to evince a sympathetic attitude
towards the development of Chinese business and Chinese institu-
tions. As regards foreign affairs, describes itself as a strong
advocate of the fullest possible co-operation of foreign, that
is American and British, and Chinese commercial interests, and
a supporter to the fullest possible extent of all legitimate
foreign enterprise in China.

As an advertising medium is not patronised by British firms.

《劳埃德周刊》（LLOYD'S WEEKLY）。南京路与江西路转角的 Zylstra 大楼，周报，其中合并了《上海舞台》（The Shanghai Stage）和《每周电影评论》（Weekly Cinema Review）。创办于1919年5月。总体声誉良好，因其对本地及东方事务、人物和运动的坦率批评。发行量1,000-1,500份。面向英国人、美国人和华人。不使用代理机构。与少数几家报纸交换新闻。其撰稿人主要为自愿性质，代表各个阶层，以及所面向的三个国籍群体。在国内政治方面，持帝国主义立场。关于外交事务，持有广泛的英国观点；被贴上“百分之百英国化”的标签，并旨在践行这一理想。
作为广告媒介的用途存疑。
所有者、董事兼编辑：George Talorein Lloyd。

The Blue Lantern, 25 Jinloo Road, a monthly
magazine published by the Blue Lantern Publishing Co.
Owned and edited by Harry Chrimes, a British subject
of English origin, Circulation 2,000 monthly.
It aims at supplying the public with light reading
matter, and is silent on political subjects. Useful
as a medium for advertising household articles, dress
and schools.

《蓝灯笼》（The Blue Lantern），金陵路25号，由蓝灯笼出版公司出版的月刊杂志。由英籍人士、英格兰裔 Harry Chrimes 所有并编辑，月发行量2,000份。
旨在向公众提供轻松读物，对政治主题保持沉默。作为家居用品、服装和学校的广告媒介是有用的。

Israel's Messenger, Corner of Soochow and
Museum Roads, Shanghai Official organ of the Shanghai
Zionist Association. Founded, 1904 ; discontinued,
February 1910 ; revived October 27, 1918, and now
issued at irregular intervals. Supported entirely
by friends and well-wishers of the local Jewish
community. General reputation excellent.
Circualtion:500 copies are printed,
devoted entirely to the interests of Jews and
Judaism in the Far East. Exchanges news with
other papers, and has various local contributors.
Employs correspondents in London, New York, India,
etc. As regards foreign affairs, neutral.
Doubtful use as an advertising medium.
Proprietor and Editor: N. E. B. Ezra.

完全致力于远东犹太人和犹太教的利益。与其他报纸交换新闻，并有各种本地撰稿人。
在伦敦、纽约、印度等地雇用通讯员。关于外交事务，持中立态度。
作为广告媒介的用途存疑。
所有者兼编辑：N. E. B. Ezra。

The Chinese Christian Intelligencer, 135 North
Szechuen Road, published weekly by the Presbyterian
Missions in China. Circulation about 7,000 copies.
Specializes in news about Christian missionary
activities in various parts of the world with
special reference to China. Avoids interference
in Chinese politics, but seems anxious to acknowledge
everything worthy in the behaviour of the people.
Friendly towards all foreign countries but probably
a little partial to the U. S. A.
Editor : G. McIntosh
Contributors : People engaged in Missionary work in
China and abroad.

《中华基督教会报》（The Chinese Christian Intelligencer），北四川路135号，由在华长老会传教团每周出版。发行量约7,000份。专门报道世界各地基督教传教活动的新闻，特别关注中国。避免干涉中国政治，但似乎急于认可民众行为中一切值得肯定之处。对所有外国都友好，但可能略微偏向美国。
编辑：G. McIntosh
撰稿人：在中国及海外从事传教工作的人员。

The China Medical Journal, No. 135 N. Szechuen
Road. Monthly magazine. Founded about 1886.
Supported and published by the China Medical Missionary
Association ; the cost of publication is covered by the
annual dues of the members to the Association (each
member pays 500 dollars). The annual subscription
to the paper is 5 dollars ; but members of the
Association receive the journal free. Circulation 800.
Exchanges copies with other medical journals in India,
England and the United States. Medical men in the Far
East contribute articles on medical subjects, public
health, etc. It has no special correspondents abroad.
Takes a special interest in medical missions in China,
and other countries in the Far East. A strictly
professional publication, it does not touch on home
politics or on foreign affairs, except as it may
affect medical missionary work in the Far East.
Editor : H. H. Morris M. D.
Executive Secretary and Treasurer : James L. Maxwell
Recording Secretary H.H. Morris, M. D.

The Shanghai Nippo, 4 Barchet Road, Daily newspaper
published in Japanese. Owned by S. Ide. Circulation
3,200. It gets foreign news from the Reuter's service,
Nippon Denpo, Far Eastern News Agency and Kokubun
Tsushin. It has correspondents in Tokyo, Osaka, and
Nagasaki. It gets Chinese news from correspondents in
the interior and Chinese News-papers. It is very
critical in dealing with Chinese affairs and to a lesser
extent adopts the same attitude towards all foreign
nations. Favours constitutional government in Japan
and is opposed to the Kiyoura Cabinet. Invariably
favours Japanese in their disputes with people of
other nations.

《上海日日新闻》（The Shanghai Nippo），白礼查路（Barchet Road）4号，日文日报。由井上（S. Ide）所有。发行量3,200份。其国际新闻来自路透社服务、日本电报通讯社、远东新闻社和国文通信社。它在东京、大阪和长崎设有通讯员。它通过内地通讯员和中国报纸获取中国新闻。它在处理中国事务时非常挑剔，并在较小程度上对所有外国国家采取相同的态度。赞成日本的宪政政府，反对清浦内阁。一贯支持日本人在与其他国家人民的纠纷中的立场。

The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi Shimbun, 10 Wuchow Road,
Daily newspaper published in Japanese. Owned by Mr. K.
Miyachi, a journalist. Circulation about 3,500. The
paper obtains foreign news from Rueter's service, Nippon
Denbo, Far Eastern News Agency and Kikubun Tsushin. It

Municipal Council. Favours government in Japan by
constitutional methods. Fairly useful as an advertising
medium.

pages.en:
Sin Wan Pao ( 新聞報 ) , the most
influential Chinese newspaper in Shanghai,
was established in 1893, and is owned by
the Sin Wan Pao Co. an American concern
incorporated under the laws of Delaware, U.S.A.,
with a capital of Tls. 100,000. The
principal shareholder is Dr. J. C. Ferguson.
The paper is independent of any political
party, and caters to the commercial classes.
It has correspondents in all the principal
cities of the world. It is pro-American
and anti-Japanese. This paper is the
recognized best advertising medium and all
matters ordered to be advertised by law
must appear in the Sin Wan Pao.
The paper has a circulation of about
55,000 in Shanghai and 65,000 abroad.
The Director is Wang Hai Zee, Editor: Li 汪漢溪
Hao Zai ( 汪伯奇 ), Business Manager:
Wang Peh Chi.( ).
Address: 19 Hankow Road.

Note: This is the only Chinese newspaper
that is fitted up with a radio
apparatus.

18/2/24
pages.zh:
《新闻报》（Sin Wan Pao），上海最具影响力的中文报纸，成立于1893年，由新闻报公司所有，这是一家根据美国特拉华州法律注册的美资企业，资本为十万两白银。主要股东是福开森（J. C. Ferguson）博士。该报独立于任何政党，面向商界人士。它在世界各主要城市设有通讯员。该报亲美反日。该报被公认为最佳广告媒介，所有依法必须刊登的广告都必须出现在《新闻报》上。
该报在上海的发行量约为55,000份，在外埠为65,000份。董事为汪汉溪，编辑：汪伯奇（Li Hao Zai），业务经理：汪佩芝（Wang Peh Chi）（原文不清）。
地址：汉口路19号。

注：这是唯一配备无线电设备的中文报纸。

1924年2月18日

pages.en:
18/2/24.
Shun Pao ( 申報 ) established in 1872, is
the oldest Chinese newspaper in Shanghai. It is
registered in the French Consulate. The name of the
proprietor is not known, but it is believed that
it is owned by a syndicate of Chinese shareholders.
The Managing Director is Sg Liang Zai ( 史量才 )
who was one of the Kiangsu peace delegates working
to bring about the signature of a Peace Agreement
between Kiangsu and Chekiang, and who also worked
in co-operation with Sir Robert Hotung when the
latter was in Shanghai endeavouring to arrange a
round table peace conference. Manager: Chang Tso
Bing ( 張竹平 ). Advertising Manager: Francis
Zia. The paper has a circulation of 20,000 in
Shanghai and 40,000 outports. It is independent
of any political party. Address: corner of Hankow
and Shantung roads.
pages.zh:
1924年2月18日。
《申报》（Shun Pao）成立于1872年，是上海最古老的中文报纸。它在法国领事馆注册。业主姓名不详，但据信由一群中国股东组成的辛迪加所有。总经理是史量才（Sg Liang Zai），他曾是江苏和平代表之一，致力于促成江苏和浙江之间签署和平协议，并在何东爵士（Sir Robert Hotung）在上海期间与其合作，试图安排圆桌和平会议。经理：张竹平（Chang Tso Bing）。广告经理：谢颂三（Francis Zia）。该报在上海的发行量为20,000份，在外埠为40,000份。它独立于任何政党。地址：汉口路与山东路转角。

pages.en:
5526
18/2/24

Shanghai Tribune (新申報) established
about seven years ago, and is not registered at present
in any foreign Consulate, but formerly when it was
known under the name of Hsin Hsun Pao it was registered
in the Portuguese Consulate. The Managing Director
is Hsu Chien Ping better known to foreigners as Jabin
Hsu (許建屏 ) one of the Chinese Advisers to the
Shanghai Municipal Council and who is the Chinese
writer on the China Press. Editor: Tsai Hai Jao
(崔漢超). Manager:
Circulation: about 2,500 Shanghai and 13,500 outports.
The paper is much read by the merchants in the Three
Eastern Provinces to which place 5,000 copies are sent
daily. The Shanghai Tribune supports Lu Yung Hsiang.
It is said that Wang Tsoo Chiu (黃楚九) Managing
Director of the Great World Amusement Resort in the
French Concession, is giving financial support to the
newspaper on the condition that General Lu Yung Hsiang
permits him to sell a certain lottery in the Chinese
territory adjoining Shanghai.

When the paper was operating under the name of
Hsin Hsun Pao, the capital of the concern was $55,000
the shareholders being: Liang Shih Yi $10,000, Chang
Tso Lin $10,000, Sun Yat Sen $15,000 and Wen Tsung Yao
(as representing the Kwangsi Party) $15,000.
Owing to the heavy demands upon his time, it is
believed that Hsu Chien Ping will probably resign
but he will be given a less onerous position on the
paper. Address of paper: 159 Shantung Road.
pages.zh:
5526
1924年2月18日

《新申报》（Shanghai Tribune）成立于约七年前，目前未在任何外国领事馆注册，但以前以《新讯报》（Hsin Hsun Pao）为名时，曾在葡萄牙领事馆注册。总经理是许建屏（Hsu Chien Ping），外国人更熟悉的名字是贾宾·许（Jabin Hsu），他是上海公共租界工部局的华人顾问之一，也是《大陆报》（China Press）的中文撰稿人。编辑：崔汉超（Tsai Hai Jao）。经理：
发行量：上海约2,500份，外埠13,500份。
该报在东三省商人中阅读广泛，每天向该地发送5,000份。《新申报》支持卢永祥。据说，法租界大世界游乐场的总经理黄楚九（Wang Tsoo Chiu）正在为该报提供财政支持，条件是卢永祥将军允许他在上海毗邻的中国领土销售某种彩票。

当该报以《新讯报》名义运营时，该企业资本为55,000美元，股东为：梁士诒10,000美元，张作霖10,000美元，孙中山15,000美元，温宗尧（代表桂系）15,000美元。
由于时间精力耗费巨大，据信许建屏可能会辞职，但他将在该报获得一个负担较轻的职位。报社地址：山东路159号。

pages.en:
5
18/2/24.

Minkuopeo ( 民國日報 ), Republican
Daily News, is the official organ in Shanghai
of the Kuomintang Party. It was established
in the year 1916, and is registered in the
Japanese Consulate. Circulation 4000 abroad,
and 2,000 in Shanghai. The paper has strong
Bolshevik tendencies and is in sympathy
with every movement started by students.
It is anti-Peking and anti-Japanese in
politics. Manager: Shao Chung Hui (          ),
Editor: Yeh Chu Tsang ( 葉楚 ).
Address: 163 Shantung Road.
pages.zh:
5
1924年2月18日。

《民國日報》（Minkuopeo），即《Republican Daily News》，是国民党在上海的机关报。该报成立于1916年，并在日本领事馆注册。海外发行量为4000份，上海本地发行量为2000份。该报具有强烈的布尔什维克倾向，同情学生发起的一切运动。在政治上持反北京政府和反日立场。经理：邵仲辉（Shao Chung Hui，音译），编辑：葉楚伧（Yeh Chu Tsang）。地址：山东路163号。

pages.en:
537
18/2/24.

The Eastern Times ( 時 報 ) has just entered
the twenty-first year of its existence. It devotes
itself mainly to the advancement of education,
and is therefore read principally by students,
in short, it is known as the students' paper.
It also has Bolshevik tendencies. The paper is
being administered by followers of Kang Yu Wei (康有為)
and Liang Chi Chao (梁任超). Managing Director:
T. C. Dih. Editor: L. Chen. Manager: Y. D. Shen.
Circulation: Shanghai 4,000, outports 16,000.
The paper supports in a measure the Anfu Party.
Adress: 30 Foochow Road.
pages.zh:
537
1924年2月18日。

《時報》（The Eastern Times）刚刚进入其存在的第二十一个年头。该报主要致力于推动教育进步，因此主要读者群为学生，简而言之，它被称为“学生报”。该报也具有布尔什维克倾向。该报由康有为和梁启超（原文为Liang Chi Chao，通常译为梁启超，此处依原文拼音对应人物）的追随者管理。董事总经理：T. C. Dih（音译）。编辑：L. Chen（音译）。经理：Y. D. Shen（音译）。发行量：上海4,000份，外埠16,000份。该报在一定程度上支持安福系。地址：福州路30号。

pages.en:
The China Times (時事新報) was
established about 16 years ago, and is registered
in the French Consulate. It is owned by a
syndicate, the largest shareholder in which is
Chang Yung Leu (張蓉騫). The editor is
Chang Tung Sung (張東). There is no
manager, the administration of the paper
being in the hands of the heads of four
departments who decides all important
matters connected with the journal. In former
years the paper was a supporter of the 研究
Chinputang Partyand of Liang Chi Chao, but
since the Eighth Year of the Republic the
paper has had no political leanings. Its
policy to-day is to advance the interests of
labourers and students. Its articles are
at times tinged with Bolshevism. The paper
has a circulation of 3,400 in Shanghai and
11,000 outports. Address: 162 Shantung Road.
（批：18/2/24）
pages.zh:
《時事新報》（The China Times）成立于约16年前，并在法国领事馆注册。该报由一个辛迪加（联合集团）拥有，其中最大股东是张蓉騫（Chang Yung Leu）。编辑是张东荪（Chang Tung Sung，原文仅写张东，依史实补全或保留原文意图，此处按常见译名处理，若严格对应原文则为张东）。没有设经理，报纸的管理由四个部门的负责人掌握，他们决定与报刊有关的所有重要事项。早年该报支持研究系和梁启超，但自民国八年以来，该报已无政治倾向。目前的方针是增进劳工和学生的利益。其文章有时带有布尔什维克色彩。该报在上海的发行量为3,400份，外埠为11,000份。地址：山东路162号。
（批注：1924年2月18日）

pages.en:
Shanghai Journal of Commerce ( 商 報 ) was
established by Tong Chih Tse ( 湯 節 之 ) about five and
a half years ago, who registered it in the American
Consulate under the name of G. Sokolsky. After the
arrest and imprisonment of Tong Chih Tse in connection
with the suicide of one of the Chinese girl clerks
employed on the paper, the management was taken over by
Lee Tsun Woo, formerly Commander of the Glorious
Restoration Army in Chapei. He is one of the prominent
Ningpo residents in Shanghai, and is connected with the
Ningpo Fellow Provincials Association. He is well known
as a member of the Kuomintang Party. The newspaper is
at present registered in the French Consulate. The
Editor is Ching Poo Lai, (          ). Managing Director:
Zee Lao Shoo. Circulation: Shanghai 5,000, outports
12,000. The policy of the paper is to advance commerce,
but it has strong Kuomintang proclivities, tinged with
Bolshevism. Address: 95 Foochow Road.
(批：18/2/24)
pages.zh:
《商報》（Shanghai Journal of Commerce）由汤节之（Tong Chih Tse）于约五年半前创办，他以G. Sokolsky的名义在美国领事馆注册。在汤节之因报社一名中国女职员自杀案被捕入狱后，管理工作由李尊武（Lee Tsun Woo，音译）接管，他曾是闸北光复军司令。他是上海著名的宁波籍人士，与宁波同乡会有联系。作为国民党成员，他颇有名气。该报目前在法国领事馆注册。编辑是程步莱（Ching Poo Lai，音译）。董事总经理：Zee Lao Shoo（音译）。发行量：上海5,000份，外埠12,000份。该报的方针是促进商业，但具有强烈的国民党倾向，并带有布尔什维克色彩。地址：福州路95号。
（批注：1924年2月18日）

pages.en:
National Herald (神州日報) was established 18/2/24
about 18 years ago and has a circulation of about
300 in Shanghai and 1,200 outports. It is registered
in the Japanese Consulate and is supported by
the Japanese Government and the Anfu Party.
The Manager is Yuen Ko Ming (余敦民) and
the Editor is Woo Zai Tsu (吳瑞祖).
Address: 161 Shantung Road.

The Crystal (晶報) is a supplement
published by the National Herald every three
days. It was started about five years ago.
The articles have a tendency bordering on the
indecent but are written in classical and
flowery language which is capable of many
interpretations. It does not meddle with
political affairs. The circulation is 5,000
in Shanghai and 2,000 outports.
pages.zh:
《神州日報》（National Herald）成立于约18年前，在上海的发行量约为300份，外埠为1,200份。该报在日本领事馆注册，得到日本政府和安福系的支持。经理是余敦民（Yuen Ko Ming），编辑是吴瑞祖（Woo Zai Tsu）。地址：山东路161号。

《晶報》（The Crystal）是《神州日报》每三天出版一次的副刊。它创办于约五年前。文章内容倾向于不雅，但用典雅华丽的文言写成，可有多种解读。该报不干涉政治事务。发行量为上海5,000份，外埠2,000份。

pages.en:
552
18/2/24.

The Diamond (金剛鑽 ) is published
every three days and is being supported,
it is believed, by 20 persons who make
use of the paper to write articles of
criticism against the "Crystal." The
Editor is believed to be Sz Chee Chuan (史濟磐 ).
No confirmation of the above could be
obtained as the office of the paper at
No. 10 Rue de Ningpo had been removed,
and its present address is unknown.
The paper has not been published since
its last issue, which was at about the
time that all the Chinese papers
suspended publication for the China
New Year holidays.
pages.zh:
552
1924年2月18日。

《金剛鑽》（The Diamond）每三天出版一次，据信由20人资助，这些人利用该报撰写文章批评《晶报》。编辑据信是史济磐（Sz Chee Chuan）。由于该报位于宁波路10号的办事处已搬迁，且目前地址不明，无法证实上述信息。自上一期出版以来，该报未再出版，上一期出版时间大约在所有中文报纸因中国新年假期停刊之时。

pages.en:
18/2/24
Industrial and Commercial Press (工商新报)
was established in the fifth moon last year
by Dee Chi Hung (田季恒 ). The Editor is
Wang Dun Kun (王钝根). Its policy is
to bring about improvements in commerce
and to obtain better knowledge of labour
conditions. Circulation: Outports 6,000,
Shanghai 2,000. It is published every Saturday.
Address: 541 Tai Koo Fong, Foochow Road.
pages.zh:
1924年2月18日
《工商新报》（Industrial and Commercial Press）由田季恒（Dee Chi Hung）于去年五月创办。编辑是王钝根（Wang Dun Kun）。其宗旨是改善商业状况并更好地了解劳工条件。发行量：外埠6,000份，上海2,000份。每周六出版。地址：福州路太古坊541号。

pages.en:
18/2/24
China Evening News. (中國晚報) was
established about three years ago. It claims
claims to have no political leanings, and that
it devotes its columns to criticism of public
affairs. But its articles and other writings
indicate that the paper is in favour of the
Kuomintang Party. It is financially supported
by Chinese who have returned from overseas.
It is owned by a syndicate. The Editor is
Sung Tsoo Hoo (沈卓吾 ), and the Manager
is Tsai Ting Z ng (蔡鼎成 ) . Circulation:
4,000 outports, and 1,000 Shanghai.
Address: 236 Nanking Road.
pages.zh:
1924年2月18日
《中國晚報》（China Evening News）成立于约三年前。该报声称没有政治倾向，并称其版面致力于评论公共事务。但其文章和其他 writings 表明该报支持国民党。该报由归国华侨提供资金支持。该报由一个辛迪加拥有。编辑是沈卓吾（Sung Tsoo Hoo），经理是蔡鼎成（Tsai Ting Z ng，原文拼写可能有误，依音译）。发行量：外埠4,000份，上海1,000份。地址：南京路236号。

pages.en:
18/2/24

Tsing Sing Pao (正心報) was
established by members of the staff of the
Chartered Stock and Produce Exchange, No. 1
Szechuen Road for the purpose of exchanging
knowledge of the business amongst themselves.
It does not deal with political matters.
The Editor is Vung Tsoon Hai (闻春南).
Circulation: 1,000 copies Shanghai, 100
outports. It is published every three days.
Address: No. 1 Szechuen Road.
pages.zh:
1924年2月18日

《正心報》（Tsing Sing Pao）由四川路1号特许证券物品交易所的工作人员创办，目的是在他们之间交流业务知识。该报不涉及政治事务。编辑是闻春南（Vung Tsoon Hai，音译）。发行量：上海1,000份，外埠100份。每三天出版一次。地址：四川路1号。

pages.en:
18/2/24.

The Fei Ting (Aeroplane) was established
about eleven years ago. Its present proprietor
is Chen Pao Zun (陳宝家), and the Editor is
Yu Siao Loh (于笑樂). The paper specialises
in social news, such as society events etc. It
has a circulation of about 1,200 copies, 400 of
which go abroad.
Address: 40 Bing Vong Ka, off Canton Road.

------------------

Doo On Jih Pao (圖畫捷報) was established
about ten years ago. The proprietor is Chen
Sung Sion (程八泉) and the Editor Hu Pao An (胡宝巷)
The paper is edited at the same address as the
Fei Ting, and its object is also the same. The
circulation is about the same.
Address: 40 Bing Vong Ka, off Canton Road.
pages.zh:
1924年2月18日。

《飛亭》（The Fei Ting，意为飞机/Aeroplane）成立于约十一年前。目前的业主是陈宝家（Chen Pao Zun），编辑是于笑乐（Yu Siao Loh）。该报专攻社会新闻，如社交活动等。发行量约为1,200份，其中400份销往外地。

CHINESE NEWSPAPERS SUBSIDIZED BY JAPANESE

I have made exhaustive inquiries into this matter amongst various well-informed persons who are connected with Chinese newspapers. As far as could be ascertained there are no Chinese newspapers being subsidized by the Japanese Government at present nor has there been any since 1927.

A few notes relating to several Chinese newspapers about which rumours have been current that they are in receipt of such subsidy are appended for your information.

The National Herald.

When this paper was started it was placed under the control of one Yuen Ko King 袁穀民 who is also known as Yuen Dah Yang 余大雄 , a returned student from Japan. The Chinese name of the paper was then "Zung Chow Zuh Lao" 神州日報 . The paper was then in receipt of a subsidy from the Japanese Government as well as from the Anfu Club which it supported. Tuan Chi Jui, the leader of the Club, who was then in power, was on good terms with Japan.

In 1919 the influence of the Anfu Club began to wane, while on May 4 of the same year occurred the students demonstration in Peking which resulted in the death of several of the students at the hands of Tuan Chi Jui's soldiers. Because of this incident Japan became extremely unpopular with the Chinese people.

At about this time the remittances from the Anfu Club became irregular and eventually ceased altogether and this caused Yuen Ko Ling to dispose of the paper to Soh Veng Ling 宋鳳鳴 the advertising manager on the National Herald, who changed the name of the paper to "Zung Chow Hsin Pao" 神州新報 which it has retained to this day. The foreign name was not changed.

The present circulation of the National Herald is about 80 copies a day which are distributed mainly amongst its advertisers. Its income from advertisements is estimated at about $170 a month, and its expenses at about $80. As it has no plant of its own, the paper is printed by the Chun Hwa Dah Sz Wei Pao 中外大事報 whose office is at Tung Sing Jao. 東新橋 . This establishment also prints five other papers of the same type as the National Herald.

When Yuen Ko Ling was in charge of the Herald, he started on his own a mosquito paper called the "Crystal" and it was so popular with the Chinese people that it soon became the leading mosquito paper in Shanghai.

It is generally believed that Yuen Ko Ling is at the present time receiving a sum of $200 from the local Japanese Consulate-General, probably in continuation of the subsidy which he had received whilst in charge of the National Herald. This money is being paid not for the purpose of writing

受日本人资助的中文报纸

我就此事向多位与中文报纸有关的知情人士进行了详尽的调查。据查，目前没有任何中文报纸接受日本政府的资助，自1927年以来也没有此类情况。

附录几份关于谣传接受此类资助的几家中文报纸的笔记，供你参考。

《神州日报》。

该报创办时，由袁穀民（Yuen Ko King，又名余大雄 Yuen Dah Yang）控制，他是一名留日归国学生。当时该报的中文名称为“神州日报”。该报当时接受日本政府以及其所支持的安福俱乐部的资助。俱乐部首领段祺瑞当时掌权，与日本关系良好。

1919年，安福俱乐部的影响力开始减弱，同年5月4日发生了北京学生示威游行，导致多名学生死于段祺瑞士兵之手。由于这一事件，日本在中国民众中变得极不受欢迎。

大约在此时，来自安福俱乐部的汇款变得不规律，最终完全停止，这导致袁穀民（原文此处拼写变为Yuen Ko Ling，应指同一人）将报纸出售给《神州日报》的广告经理宋鳳鳴（Soh Veng Ling），宋将报名改为“神州新报”，并沿用至今。外文名称未变。

目前《神州日报》的发行量约为每天80份，主要分发在其广告客户中。其广告收入估计每月约170美元，支出约80美元。由于没有自己的印刷设备，该报由位于东新桥的《中外大事報》（Chun Hwa Dah Sz Wei Pao）印刷。该机构还印刷其他五份与《神州日报》类型相同的报纸。

当袁穀民负责《神州日报》时，他自己创办了一份小报（mosquito paper，指八卦小报）叫《晶报》，它在中国民众中非常受欢迎，很快成为上海领先的小报。

人们普遍认为，袁穀民目前正从当地日本总领事馆收取200美元，这可能是他在负责《神州日报》期间所获资助的延续。这笔钱的支付目的并非为了撰写

propaganda articles in favour of Japan----for no
paper would be so daring----but probably for oral
propaganda at social functions and also for the
silence of the Crystal in Sino-Japanese disputes.
It is believed that Yuen Ko Ling's income from the
Crystal, including the subsidy from the Japanese,
amounts to about $800 a month. His principal
associate on the Crystal is a man name Chang Tai Fu 张太夫
who was formerly with him on the Herald. Chang
knows a great deal about Yuen Ko Ling's relations
with the Japanese as well as of his shady activities
as editor of the Crystal, such as blackmail etc.
This is the reason why Yuen Ko Ling is still
retaining Chung's services although Chang is now
well over 60 years of age.

The Shanghai Tribune.

This paper was established about 15 years ago
by Zih Ts Bai 席子佩 who was formerly connected with
the Shun Pao, with the proceeds of a successful legal
action he brought against Sz Liang Zay of that paper.
The paper supported the Anfu Club and through its
leader Tuan Chi Jui it was given a subsidy by the
Japanese Government. Four years later it was
sold to Hsu Chi Bing (better known as Jabin Hsu, a
former Chinese advisor to the Shanghai Municipal
Council) and the paper began to support the Chihli
Clique which was represented by General Sun Chuan Fang,
the Inspector-General of the five South-Eastern
Provinces. The paper was placed under the control
of Soong Sin Jing 宋鑫琴 the Director of the Shanghai
office of Sun Chuan Fang, with Wang Chiu Igo 王秋皋
as Editor.
After the arrival of the Nationalist Army
in Shanghai, the Kuomintang confiscated the
printing plant of the Tribune but not before Soo
Sih Jing's brother-in-law had removed the type and
other accessories with which he later started a
printing plant known as the Peacock Printing Co.
on Sinza Road.

The Kiangnan Evening News.

This paper was started by members of the West
Hill Clique of the Kuomintang for the sole purpose
of conducting propaganda against the Right Wing of
the Party as represented by Chiang Kai Shek's Clique.
It is financed by members of the West Hill Clique
and has never been in receipt of a subsidy from the
Japanese Government. The object of the founders
in placing the paper under a Japanese Editor whose
name is Yamada and having it registered in the
Japanese Consulate , is to prevent it from being
interfered with by the Chinese authorities. The
paper has not written a line of pro-Japanese
propaganda.
At one time the paper became very popular with
the Chinese people because of its articles against
Chiang Kai Shek and the price of the paper rose from
3 coppers to 30 coppers. It is said that Chiang Kai
Shek was so annoyed that he actually sent a
representative to buy over the paper but the

亲日宣传文章——因为没有哪家报纸敢如此大胆——但可能是为了在社交场合进行口头宣传，以及为了《晶报》在中日争端中保持沉默。据信，袁国梁（Yuen Ko Ling，音译）从《晶报》获得的收入，包括来自日本人的津贴，每月约为800元。他在《晶报》的主要合伙人名叫张太夫（Chang Tai Fu），此前曾与他共事于《字林西报》。张太夫对袁国梁与日本人的关系，以及他作为《晶报》编辑进行的敲诈勒索等 shady 活动知之甚详。这就是尽管张太夫现已年过六旬，袁国梁仍留用他的原因。

《上海论坛报》（The Shanghai Tribune）。

该报大约由席子佩（Zih Ts Bai）于15年前创办，他此前曾供职于《申报》，创办资金来自他对该报经理史量才（Sz Liang Zay）提起的一场胜诉所得。该报支持安福俱乐部，并通过其首领段祺瑞获得日本政府的津贴。四年后，该报被出售给许季彬（Hsu Chi Bing，更广为人知的名字是贾宾·许 Jabin Hsu，前上海公共租界工部局华董顾问），该报开始支持以五省联军总司令孙传芳将军为代表的直系军阀。该报置于孙传芳上海办事处主任宋鑫琴（Soong Sin Jing）的控制之下，由王秋皋（Wang Chiu Igo）担任编辑。
国民革命军抵达上海后，国民党没收了《论坛报》的印刷厂，但在此之前，宋鑫琴的妹夫已将铅字和其他设备搬走，他后来利用这些设备在新闸路开办了一家名为孔雀印刷公司（Peacock Printing Co.）的印刷厂。

《江南晚报》（The Kiangnan Evening News）。

该报由国民党西山会议派成员创办，唯一目的是针对以蒋介石派系为代表的党内右翼进行宣传。其资金由西山会议派成员提供，从未接受过日本政府的津贴。创办人将报纸交由一名名叫山田（Yamada）的日本编辑管理，并在日本领事馆注册，其目的是防止受到中国当局的干涉。该报未刊登过任何亲日宣传文章。
该报曾因发表反蒋介石的文章而深受中国民众欢迎，报纸价格从3个铜板涨至30个铜板。据说蒋介石对此极为恼火，甚至派代表试图收买该报，但

The Shun Pao.
It is not generally known but it is a fact that
there are Japanese interests in the Shun Pao. When
the paper was started certain Japanese took up a
large block of shares in the same way that Dr. J. C.
Ferguson acquired his shares in the Sin Wan Pao.
As the paper began to prosper a movement was started
to buy out the Japanese interests but the latter,
probably with an eye to acquiring a controlling
interest in the paper, refused to dispose of their
holdings. It is related that one of its former
editors, a man named Kung Teh Pah 龔德柏 was
dismissed for having written an anti-Japanese
article. Kung is now attached to the Ministry of
Foreign Affairs of the National Government, after
holding the position of Commissioner of Foreign
Affairs in Hunan, his native province. It is said
that Sz Liang Zai 史量才 the manager of the Shun Pao
shows great deference to Kung because the latter
knows too much about the internal affairs of the
Shun Pao. An examination of the paper's account
books will not show the amount of the Japanese holding
because if this became known the paper would be
boycotted by the people and the Government would
probably take action.
Attempts have been made in recent years to
prevail upon the Japanese to relinquish their
interests but without success.
Your obedient servant,

这并非广为人知的事实，但《申报》中确实存在日本利益。在该报创办之初，某些日本人以类似弗格森博士（Dr. J. C. Ferguson）获取《新闻报》（Sin Wan Pao）股份的方式，购买了大量股份。随着报纸日益繁荣，有人发起运动试图买断日本方面的利益，但后者可能着眼于获取报纸的控制权，拒绝出售其持股。据称，该报前编辑之一龚德柏（Kung Teh Pah）因撰写反日文章而被解雇。龚德柏在其家乡湖南省担任外交专员后，现任职于国民政府外交部。据说，《申报》经理史量才（Sz Liang Zai）对龚德柏表现出极大的恭敬，因为后者对《申报》的内部事务知之过多。查阅该报的账簿不会显示日本持股的金额，因为一旦此事公开，该报将遭到民众抵制，政府也可能采取行动。
近年来曾试图说服日本人放弃其利益，但未获成功。

Russian Newspaper "Verchor," (The Evening).

This publication first made its appearance on

The policy of the paper was devoted to the
affairs of the Committee of Autonomous Siberian
Organizations which has in view the separation of
Siberia from Soviet Russia.

It was reported that funds for the publication
were supplied by the Japanese Government through
Mr. Chertkoff, who is the representative of the
Siberian Committee in Japan and who is in close
touch with the Japanese.

The paper was printed at the Far Eastern Press
Coy, No. 59 Rue Moliere.

The offices were closed down about three weeks
ago owing to lack of funds.

The Editor expects to receive a further
subsidy from Japan in the near future when the
paper will again commence publication.

Rea who resides chiefly in Japan and is assisted by

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY. SEPTEMBER 10. 1931

Press Privileges
Given To Rengo

Agency Will Not Issue
Unfounded Reports,
Is Promise

(Special To The China Press)
NANKING, Sept. 9.—The ministry of foreign affairs notified today the ministry of communications to restore the telegraph privileges of the Japanese Rengo News Agency in China, a specially appointed representative of the agency from Tokyo having made an official apology to the foreign ministry over its misleading reports in the past relative to China's political developments.
The Japanese representative is also understood to have promised that his agency will hereafter refrain from issuing unfounded reports..
The Rengo News Agency was deprived of its telegraph privileges in China several months ago after repeated warnings from the foreign ministry in connection with its inaccurate reports on the country's domestic situation. The foreign ministry at the time also released a bulletin showing many specific occasions when the agency gave out unreliable and false news.
Subsequent attempts on the part of the agency to recover its telegraph privileges proved resultless until the arrival of its special representative some time ago and his formal presentation of apology to the Chinese authorities.

《字林西报》，1931年9月10日，星期四

新闻特权
授予联合通讯社

该社承诺不发布
无根据的报道

（《字林西报》特约专电）
南京，9月9日电。——外交部今日通知交通部，恢复日本联合通讯社在华的电报特权，该社从东京派出的特派代表已就其过去关于中国政治发展的误导性报道向外务部正式道歉。
据悉，这位日本代表还承诺，其所属机构今后将 refrain from issuing unfounded reports（避免发布无根据的报道）。
数月前，在外交部就其关于中国国内局势的不准确报道多次发出警告后，联合通讯社被剥夺了在華的电报特权。当时，外交部还发布了一份公告，列举了该社发布不可靠和虚假新闻的许多具体事例。
此后，该社为恢复电报特权所作的尝试均无结果，直到不久前其特派代表抵达并向中国当局正式呈递道歉书。

28 - 4 - 31

The Rengo News Agency And China

THE latest news received from the Capital indicates
the determination of the Government not to restore
telegraph, telephone and mail privileges to the Japanese
Rengo News Service until after proper amends have
been made in connection with the circulation of inac-
curate Chinese news for a period extending over eight
months.

As long as this deadlock lasts, the Rengo must find
it increasingly difficult to discharge its daily duties to
its clients in China, and especially to those in Japan,
with any degree of satisfaction, and is faced with the
imminent prospect of losing patronage and running its
service at a loss, and under circumstances not only try-
ing to itself but which will in the end embarrass its
own government.

Being a business proposition, no foreign news
agency can afford deliberately to antagonize the govern-
ment of a country in which it is conducted without
coming to financial grief. That is, of course, unless
it is backed for propaganda purposes, either destructive
or otherwise, by a foreign government whose national
the owner of the news agency is.

The Japanese Government, which exercises the
most rigid control over news emanating from Japan,
is unlikely to countenance any news agency conducted
by its subjects in China which has been proved to have
been circulating inaccurate news derogatory to Chinese
national interests.

In view of the Rengo Agency being of a business
nature and of the impossibility of successful repudiation
by Tokyo of the charges of inaccuracy in some of its
news reports, the Rengo, in our opinion, would do well
to satisfy the Chinese Government by the appointment
of a new representative who will steer clear of the
rock on which his predecessor was wrecked.

A newspaper is always ready to make prompt cor-
rection when it has published untrue news, publication
of which may have been unavoidable, working as it
does under high pressure. A similar attitude should
be taken by a news agency, unless its policy is not to
give facts, but to misrepresent or color them.

In the present case, if the Rengo changes its repre-
sentative in China, it may result in the wholesale
liquidation of the unfortunate past, and the beginning
of a new career under happier auspices.

Following the settlement of the Rengo case, we
hope that the Government will see to it that correct
news gets ahead of incorrect news in print, and that
it will not be satisfied until immediate corrections are
made if there should be any inaccurate news circulated
by any news agency or printed by any newspaper.

1931年4月28日

联合通讯社与中国

从首都收到的最新消息表明，
政府决心在就长达八个月期间
传播不准确的中国新闻一事作出
适当补救之前，不恢复日本
联合新闻服务社的电报、电话和邮件特权。

只要这种僵局持续下去，联合通讯社就会发现，
要令人满意地履行其对在华客户，尤其是对在日本
客户的日常职责，将日益困难，并且面临
失去客源和亏本运营服务的紧迫前景，这种情况
不仅对其自身构成考验，最终还将使其
本国政府陷入尴尬境地。

作为一家商业机构，任何外国新闻
社都承担不起故意与其开展业务所在国的
政府对抗而不遭受财务损失的后果。当然，除非
它得到其所有者所属国籍的外国政府的支持，用于
宣传目的，无论是破坏性的还是其他性质的。

日本政府对其境内发出的新闻实行
最严格的控制，不太可能纵容由其国民
在中国经营的、已被证实传播有损中国
国家利益的不准确新闻的任何新闻机构。

鉴于联合通讯社具有商业性质，且东京方面
不可能成功否认其部分新闻报道中
存在不实指控，我们认为，联合通讯社最好
任命一位新代表来满足中国政府的要求，这位新代表
将避开其前任触礁的那块“岩石”。

报纸在高压下运作，一旦发布了虽不可避免但属
不实的新闻，总是乐于迅速更正。新闻机构也应
采取类似态度，除非其政策不是提供事实，
而是歪曲或渲染事实。

在目前的情况下，如果联合通讯社更换其在华
代表，可能会导致对不幸过去的全面清算，并在
更顺利的兆头下开启新的职业生涯。

随着联合通讯社案件的解决，我们希望
政府确保印刷品中正确的新闻领先于错误的新闻，
并且，如果有任何新闻机构传播或任何报纸刊登
不准确的新闻，政府不会满足于现状，直到
立即作出更正。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, APRIL 19, 1931 SPECIFIC INSTANCES WHERE RENGO FILED DEFINITELY FALSE REPORTS ARE TAKEN FROM OFFICIAL RECORDS (By China Press Nanking Correspondent) Nanking, April 18.—The government ban on Rengo has aroused considerable discussion and Japanese newspaper groups have already made representations in the matter. For the purpose of clarifying the causes underlying the government action, your correspondent is now in a position to set forth some of the specific instances as culled from official records in which Rengo has filed despatches giving wide circulation to reports which later proved to be false. By way of comparison, one may reproduce the reports of the Kuo Min News Agency, Reuters and special correspondents of several Shanghai and Peiping newspapers. The facts of the various situations as listed below are qualified by their sources. Government communiques and other records yielded the facts which are included in the compilation. | RENGO REPORTS | OTHER PRESS REPORTS | FACTS | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | May 26, 1930, Peiping
“The alleged victory of the Northern Coalition forces over th Government troops in the Lunghai area ... has been practically confirmed.” | “The rebel claims to sweeping victories are absolutely groundless, they are claims of victories in battles which have never been fought and of units that do not exist.”
—Kuo Min, May 27. | There had been a lull during the last few days on the Lunghai Railway front following the complete collapse of the first line of the rebels’ defence. | | June 8, 1930, Nanking
“Addressing a letter to General Chiang Kai-shek yesterday morning, General Feng Yu-hsiang urged the former to resign his present post and go abroad. The letter which was dropped to the Government forces at Kueiteh from an aeroplane, read as follows:
......” | “Military Headquarters here say that there is no truth in the press report that General Feng Yu-hsiang has dropped a letter by aeroplane urging President Chiang Kai-shek to go abroad with him.”
—Kuo Min, June 10. | No such letter was ever dropped by General Feng. | | June 9, 1930 Peiping.
“As the result of negotiations between the representatives of Generals Yen Hsi-shan and Han Fu-chu, a compromise is reported to have been reached between the Shansi military authorities and General Han Fu-chu, whereby the Shansi troops are to enter the town of Tsinan within a few days and that the troops of General Han Fu-chu are to withdraw from Tsinan to Chutsun.” | “Military Headquarters here (Nanking) say that there is no truth in the press reports that General Han Fu-chu has agreed with General Yen Hsi-shan to hand over Tsinan.”
—Kuo Min, June 10.
“As General Han Fu-chu failed in making a reply yesterday when the timelimit expired for the ultimatum sent to him by the Shansi troops regarding the transfer of the walled city of Tsinan, the Shansi troops have decided to occupy the city by force of arms.”
Rengo, June 17. | General Han’s retreat from Tsinan was not the result of compromise, but a deliberate move to draw out the Shansi troops from their defensive tactics. | | June 24, 1930, Nanking
“It is now learned that General Chang, addressing telegrams on June 21 and 22 to Generals Yen Hsi-shan and Feng Yu-hsiang respectively, advised the latter to the effect that the present civil disturbance has been caused owing to the differences of political opinion on the part of the Nanking Government and the Northern Coalition——It is earnestly desired that both Nanking and the Northern Coalition would withdraw their troops entirely from all fronts in order to stop warfare ...... on condition that both contending factions shall agree to the establishment of better regions in the districts of Chengchow and Kaifeng.” | “General Chang Hsueh-liang is preparing to dispatch four mixed brigades of the Manchurian Army to Hopei, as a preliminary step for the subjugation of the Shansi rebels.”
Kuo Min, June 18.
“Marshal Chang Hsueh-llliang denies the report that he has telegraphed General Yen-Hsi-shan and Marshal Feng Yu-hsiang urging a peace parley.”
Reuters, June 21. | Such a peace parley to compromise the Northern group and the Central Government was never suggested by the Marshal. |

《字林西报》，1931年4月19日，星期日 官方记录中选取的联合通讯社 提交明确虚假报道的具体事例 （《字林西报》南京通讯员撰稿） 南京，4月18日电。——政府对联合通讯社的禁令引起了广泛讨论，日本报业团体已就此提出交涉。为了澄清政府行动背后的原因，本报通讯员现在能够列出从官方记录中摘录的一些具体事例，在这些事例中，联合通讯社提交的电报广泛传播了后来被证明是虚假的报道。 作为比较，可以转载国民通讯社（Kuo Min News Agency）、路透社以及几家上海和北平报纸特派记者的报道。 下列各种情况的事实均注明来源。政府公报和其他记录提供了汇编中包含的事实。 | 联合通讯社报道 | 其他媒体报道 | 事实 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 1930年5月26日，北平
“北方联军在陇海地区战胜政府军的所谓胜利……已基本得到证实。” | “叛军声称取得全面胜利的说法毫无根据，这些胜利是在从未发生过的战斗中和不存在的部队中取得的。”
——国民通讯社，5月27日。 | 在叛军第一道防线完全崩溃后，陇海铁路前线近几日处于平静状态。 | | 1930年6月8日，南京
“冯玉祥将军昨天上午致信蒋介石将军，敦促前者辞去现职并出国。这封信是从飞机上投掷给归德政府军的，内容如下：
......” | “此处军事总部表示，媒体关于冯玉祥将军空投信件敦促蒋介石总统与其一同出国的报道不实。”
——国民通讯社，6月10日。 | 冯将军从未空投过此类信件。 | | 1930年6月9日，北平。
“据报，经过阎锡山将军和韩复榘将军代表之间的谈判，山西军方与韩复榘将军达成妥协，据此，晋军将在几天内进入济南城，韩复榘将军的部队将从济南撤至朱村。” | “此处（南京）军事总部表示，媒体关于韩复榘将军同意与阎锡山将军移交济南的报道不实。”
——国民通讯社，6月10日。
“由于韩复榘将军在山西军队就移交济南府城发出的最后通牒期限届满时未能作出回复，山西军队决定以武力占领该城。”
联合通讯社，6月17日。 | 韩将军从济南撤退并非妥协的结果，而是为了引诱晋军脱离其防御战术的 deliberate move（蓄意举动）。 | | 1930年6月24日，南京
“据悉，张将军分别于6月21日和22日向阎锡山将军和冯玉祥将军发电报，建议后者称，目前的内乱是由于南京政府与北方联军在政治观点上的分歧所致——恳切希望南京和北方联军从所有战线完全撤军，以停止战争……条件是交战双方同意在郑州和开封地区建立更好的区域。” | “张学良将军正准备派遣四个东北军混合旅前往河北，作为镇压山西叛军的初步步骤。”
国民通讯社，6月18日。
“张学良元帅否认有关他致电阎锡山将军和冯玉祥元帅敦促和平谈判的报道。”
路透社，6月21日。 | 元帅从未提议通过和平谈判来调和北方集团与中央政府的关系。 |

August 14, 1930. Peiping
"The Northern troops which are advancing eastward after occupying Kweiteh and Mamutsi are in very high spirits."

"An official communique from the Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters categorically denies that the Government forces have suffered any reverses on the Lunghai front."
Kuo Min, August 14
"Kweiteh is still in the hands of the Government troops.
Shanghai Times, Aug. 20.

Kweiteh was never held by Northerners.

SEPT. 15, 1930, Mukden.
"Mukden will continue its policy of strict neutrality, but will not spare its efforts to encourage peace negotiations."

"There is no doubt that Manchuria is definitely in favour of Nanking."
—Reuters, Sept. 9
"It is reported that the attitude of Mukden is opposed to the new Peking Government."
—Rengo, Peking Sept. 15.

"We sincerely support the Central Government and oppose the establishment of a second Government."
—General Chang's telegram, Sept. 6, 1930, Peking Leader.
Peiping was taken over by Mukden troops, Sept. 22.
Marshal Changs's acceptance of post as Vice-Commander of the National forces, on Oct. 9. 1930.

Sept. 26, 1930, Peiping.
"Mukden officials ... are, in one way or another, obstructing the activity of Nanking's representatives who are planning to take over various Government organs into their hands. Under these circumstances, observers are entertaining extreme apprehension lest fresh trouble should again brew up between the Mukden and Nanking factions."

"Commenting on your editorial of October 20 Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang states that there is no basis for the rumors of suspicion existing between Chiang Kai-shek and himself ......... The administration is .........in the hands of the Central Government, and orders emanating from Nanking will be valid."
—North China Daily News' Mukden Correspondent, Oct. 29, 1930.

Mukden's policy is to follow the behests of the Central Government. Meeting in Nanking November 14 between General Chang Hsueh-liang and President Chiang Kai-shek resulted in complete accord.

Oct. 25, 1930, Mukden
"It is believed that General Shih Yu-san is entrusted with an important mission by Commander-in-Chief Chiang Kai-shek to negotiate with the Mukden authorities regarding the spheres of influence to be divided between the Nanking Government and the Mukden Faction."

"Regarding military questions.... ..everything will be done in accordance with orders received from the Central Government. Regarding civil questions, the orders of the Central Government will be followed."
Reuters' Mukden Correspondent reporting an interview with Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, October 28.

Sept. 29, 1930, Mukden
"General Chang Hsueh-liang sent a telegram yesterday to the Peiping and Tientsin authorities prohibiting activities of the Central as well as the Municipal Kuomintang."

"Neither the National Government nor the Central Kuomintang authorities here (Nanking) has received reports to this effect....such action is most unlikely."
Kuo Min, Oct. 1.

No such ban ever imposed on Kuomintang. Mukden Headquarters of the Kuomintang opened, Jan. 31, 1931.

Oct. 2, 1930, Peiping
"It is absolutely groundless that General Feng Yu-hsiang has retired from his present post as Commander of the Kuominchun."

"It is reliably reported that General Feng Yu-hsiang announced his retirement upon the earnest request of his subordinates."
Reuters, Sept. 30.
"Feng Yu-hsiang is willing to leave Honan immediately and go abroad together with Sun Liang-chen."
Kuo Min, Oct. 1.

Feng Yu-hsiang has been living in seclusion in Shanghai since October, 1930.

(Continued on Page 17, Col. 1.)
pages.zh:
1930年8月14日，北平
“在占领归德和马牧集后向东推进的北方部队士气高昂。”

“总司令总部发布官方公报，断然否认政府军在陇海前线遭受任何挫折。”
《国民新闻》，8月14日
“归德仍在政府军手中。
《上海泰晤士报》，8月20日。

归德从未被北方人占据。

1930年9月15日，沈阳。
“沈阳将继续其严格中立的政策，但不遗余力地鼓励和平谈判。”

“毫无疑问，满洲 definitely 支持南京。”
——路透社，9月9日
“据报道，沈阳的态度反对新的北京政府。”
——联合通讯社，北平，9月15日。

“我们真诚支持中央政府，反对建立第二个政府。”
——张将军电报，1930年9月6日，《北平导报》。
9月22日，北平被沈阳部队接管。
1930年10月9日，张元帅接受全国部队副总司令职务。

1930年9月26日，北平。
“沈阳官员……正以各种方式阻碍南京代表的活动，这些代表计划接管各政府机构。在这种情况下，观察家们极度担忧，生怕沈阳派系与南京派系之间再次酝酿新的麻烦。”

“评论你方10月20日的社论时，张学良将军表示，关于蒋介石与他之间存在猜疑的谣言毫无根据…………行政权…………掌握在中央政府手中，来自南京的命令将有效。”
——《字林西报》沈阳通讯员，1930年10月29日。

沈阳的政策是遵循中央政府的旨意。11月14日，张学良将军与蒋介石总统在南京举行的会晤达成了完全一致。

1930年10月25日，沈阳
“据悉，石友三将军受总司令蒋介石委派，肩负重要使命，与沈阳当局就南京政府与沈阳派系之间划分的势力范围进行谈判。”

“关于军事问题……一切将依照中央政府收到的命令行事。关于民政问题，将遵循中央政府的命令。”
路透社沈阳通讯员报道对张元帅的采访，10月28日。

1930年9月29日，沈阳
“张学良将军昨日向北平和天津当局发出电报，禁止中央党部及市党部的活动。”

“无论是国民政府还是此间（南京）的中央国民党当局均未收到此类报告……此种行动极不可能发生。”
《国民新闻》，10月1日。

从未对国民党实施过此类禁令。国民党沈阳总部于1931年1月31日开业。

1930年10月2日，北平
“冯玉祥将军辞去其现任国民军总司令职务的说法绝对毫无根据。”

“据可靠消息，冯玉祥将军是在其下属的恳切请求下宣布辞职的。”
路透社，9月30日。
“冯玉祥愿意立即离开河南，并与孙良诚一同出国。”
《国民新闻》，10月1日。

自1930年10月以来，冯玉祥一直隐居在上海。

（续第17页，第1栏。）

PACIFIC INSTANCES WHERE RENGO FILED DEFINITELY FALSE REPORTS ARE TAKEN FROM OFFICIAL RECORDS (Continued from Page 20, Col. 5.) | RENGO REPORTS | OTHER PRESS REPORTS | FACTS | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Oct. 5, 1930, Tokyo
"It is learned that Mr. Sun Fo, Railway Minister of the Nanking Government who arrived at Dairen en route to Mukden from Tientsin, had an interview with Mr. Sengoku, President of the South Manchuria Railway Company" | "Mr. Sun Fo, Minister of Railways, is not now in Dairen."
Shanghai Times, Oct. 7. | Mr. Sun Fo never made the trip to Manchuria. | | Nov. 20, 1930, Shanghai.
"The Nanking Government to pay General Yen Hsi-shan and General Feng Yu-hsiang 1,000,000 yuan each to enable them to go abroad for a period of three years, at the end of which time, on their return; they will be given important posts in the administration." | "As I have definitely retired from politics, I have no intention whatever of returning to China's political life in future."
Yen Hsi-shan's telegram according to Rengo, Dec. 22.
"Commander-in-Chief Chiang Kai-shek petitions that....a general amnesty for all political and military offenders in the country ....with the exception of Yen Hsi-shan, Chen Chiung-ming and the Communists ....be issued on New Year Day (Jan. 1st, 1931)."
Kuo Min, Oct. 5. | No money was paid by the Central Government for this purpose: nor were posts promised them on their return. | | Dec. 7, 1930, Mukden
"In connection with the reported agreement of views between Marshal Chang and Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek regarding the questions of military, diplomatic, financial and other affairs, ......it is reliably reported here (Mukden) that such an understanding was reached between Marshal Chang and General Chiang purely in an individual capacity, the former having reserved definite commitment on the questions until his exchange of views with the big chiefs of the North-Eastern Provinces." | "The North-Eastern Provinces will hereafter be under the complete control of the Central Government."
Kuo Min, Dec. 8. | General Chiang and General Chang have acted in complete accord, and the latter has consulted the Central Government on almost every important move regarding the rehabilitation of the Northern Provinces. | | Dec. 10, 1930, Nanking
"It is understood that Mr. Frank Lee will shortly be appointed Chinese Minister at Washington, replacing Dr. C. C. Wu. Should this change take place, Mr. Wang Chia-chen is expected to replace Mr. Frank Lee." | "Dr. C. T. Wang described the report as entirely inaccurate."
Special to Leader, Dec. 17.
"In a letter to the Leader Mr. Frank Lee .... stated that the reports that the Government had intended to send him first to France and then to the United States were entirely inaccurate."
—Leader, Dec. 28. | Mr. Frank Lee is still Political Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs. | | Dec. 11 1930, Harbin.
"Mr. Mo Teh-hui . . . is expected to leave Moscow on December 16. The possibility of the appointment of Dr. Wellington Koo, to the post of new plenipotentiary delegate to the Sino-Soviet Conference is spoken of generally among official circles." | "An official denial has been issued today of the report that Dr. Wellington Koo is going to Moscow to replace Mr. Mo Teh-hui in the Sino-Soviet negotiations.
—Reuters, Dec. 14.
"On December 12 Mr. Mo Teh-hui informed Mr. Karakhan of his intention to leave for China to be absent for some time."
—Tass, Dec. 15. | Mr. Mo Teh-hui returned to China on leave on December 21; but returned to Russia to resume Sino-Russian negotiations on April 11, 1931, with Karakhan. | | Dec. 30, 1930, Mukdan
"The situation in the Three Eastern Provinces . . . is such that it is apparently impossible to give immediate implement to the provisions of the mandate (to abolish likin) in that area." | "According to reports here (Tientsin) the announcement of Likin abolition for January 1, 1931, finds the provinces of North China and Manchuria lining up behind the National Government and offering full support."
—Shanghai Evening Post, December 29.
"The National Government has received a telegram from Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang stating that likin would be abolished in North China."
Reuters, Jan. 6, 1931. | Likin abolished in Manchuria. Jan. 14, 1931. |
