从官方记录中选取的联合通讯社 提交明确虚假报告的太平洋地区实例 （续第20页，第5栏。） | 联合通讯社报道 | 其他报刊报道 | 事实 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 1930年10月5日，东京
“据悉，南京政府铁道部长孙科先生从天津前往沈阳途中抵达大连，会见了南满洲铁道株式会社总裁仙石先生” | “铁道部长孙科先生目前不在大连。”
《上海泰晤士报》，10月7日。 | 孙科先生从未前往满洲。 | | 1930年11月20日，上海。
“南京政府将向阎锡山将军和冯玉祥将军各支付100万元，使他们能够出国三年，期满回国后，将在政府中担任重要职务。” | “既然我已彻底退出政坛，我无意在未来重返中国政治生活。”
阎锡山的电报，据联合通讯社12月22日报道。
“总司令蒋介石请求……在全国元旦（1931年1月1日）发布大赦令，赦免所有政治和军事罪犯……但阎锡山、陈炯明和共产党人除外……”
《国民新闻》，10月5日。 | 中央政府未为此目的支付任何款项：也未承诺他们回国后担任职务。 | | 1930年12月7日，沈阳
“鉴于张元帅与蒋总司令在军事、外交、财政及其他事务问题上 reportedly 达成观点一致，……此间（沈阳）有可靠消息称，张元帅与蒋将军之间的这种谅解纯属个人性质，前者在与东北各省大头目交换意见之前，对这些事项保留了明确的承诺。” | “此后，东北各省将处于中央政府的完全控制之下。”
《国民新闻》，12月8日。 | 蒋将军与张将军行动完全一致，后者在关于北方各省重建的几乎每一项重要举措上都咨询了中央政府。 | | 1930年12月10日，南京
“据悉，李国鼎先生不久将被任命为驻华盛顿中国公使，接替伍朝枢博士。如果这一变动发生，预计王家桢先生将接替李国鼎先生。” | “王正廷博士称该报道完全不实。”
《导报》特约稿，12月17日。
“李国鼎先生在致《导报》的信中……表示，有关政府打算先派他去法国然后去美国的报道完全不实。”
——《导报》，12月28日。 | 李国鼎先生仍任外交部政务次长。 | | 1930年12月11日，哈尔滨。
“莫德惠先生……预计将于12月16日离开莫斯科。官方圈子普遍谈论任命顾维钧博士为新任中苏会议全权代表的可能性。” | “今日发布官方否认，驳斥顾维钧博士将前往莫斯科接替莫德惠先生进行中苏谈判的报道。
——路透社，12月14日。
“12月12日，莫德惠先生通知加拉罕先生，他打算离开前往中国，缺席一段时间。”
——塔斯社，12月15日。 | 莫德惠先生于12月21日休假返回中国；但于1931年4月11日返回俄罗斯，与加拉罕恢复中俄谈判。 | | 1930年12月30日，沈阳
“东三省……的局势使得显然无法在该地区立即执行（废除厘金）指令的规定。” | “据此间（天津）报道，宣布于1931年1月1日废除厘金，华北和满洲各省正列队支持国民政府并提供全力支持。”
——《上海晚邮报》，12月29日。
“国民政府收到张元帅电报，称将在华北废除厘金。”
路透社，1931年1月6日。 | 1931年1月14日，满洲废除厘金。 |

pages.en:
Jan. 14, 1931, Nanking.
"The struggle for supremacy which has been going on under the surface between General Chang Hsueh-liang . . . and General Chang Tso-shang . . . is coming to a head. . . The relations have been strained to breaking point. . . General Chang is further reported to have decided to hand over his post Commander-in-Chief of the Manchurian armies to General Chang Tso-shang who possesses real power in Manchuria."

"There have been rumors of discord between Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang and General Chang Tso-hsiang. According to a dispatch from Mukden, however, these rumors are groundless. . ."
Reuters, Jan. 15, 1931.
"There has been no truth in any of the statements made by these propaganda agents. . ."
—North China Daily News, January 25, 1931.

These rumored political changes never came about.

Jan. 16, 1931, Peiping.
"Dr. C. T. Wang arrived here (Peiping) this morning from Tientsin. . . Prior to his departure he will call on the foreign diplomatic representatives here to ask them to transfer the legations to Nanking where sites have already been chosen for the various diplomatic establishment."

"As to the question of the removal of the Legations to Nanking, a site being chosen and set aside for them in the Capital, they can remove their quarters any time they feel to be convenient."
Peiping Leader, Jan. 18, 1931.
"Maps of the land so designated (for the accommodation of the various foreign legations) are being forwarded by the Ministry to the legation Ministers so as to enable them to make the choice among themselves."
Kou Min, Jan. 19, 1931.

Dr. C. T. Wang never called on the diplomatic representatives.

March 2, 1931, Nanking.
"Commander-in-Chief Chiang Kai-shek is keeping in confinement Mr. Hu Han-min, President of the Legislative Yuan, in Tangshan. Mr. Hu was held prisoner when he visited the General's headquarters last night at 11."

"The Standing Committee of the Central Executive Committee decided this morning to include among the urgent measures to be discussed by the National Convention on May 5 the question of the adoption of a "Yueh Fah," namely, a provisional constitution during the political tutelage period, pending the promulgation of a permanent constitution for the constitutional period.
"A Committee of 10 members, including Mr. Wu Chih-hui and Dr. Wang Chung-hui, was appointed to draft such "Yueh Fah" (provisional constitution).
"Mr. Hu Han-min, however, holds a contrary opinion and tendered his resignation.
"The Standing Committee of the C.E.C. considers the adoption of a "Yueh Fah" as being in strict conformity with Dr. Sun Yat-sen's view and accepted Mr. Hu Han-min's resignation from his posts as State Councillor and President of the Legislative Yuan . . . .
"Mr. Hu Han-min will remain in Nanking to assist the Government."
—Official Communique, Nanking, March 2, 1931.

March 3, 1931, Nanking
"It is rumored that Mr. Hu Han-min, . . . . . .has started a hunger strike as the only weapon left to him in challenging the Commander-in-Chief."

Mr. Hu returned to his private residence in the city (Nanking) on Sunday, March 8.
Dr. J. Heng Liu examined Mr. Hu on March 6 and categorically denied the reports that Mr. Hu had any fainting fits. He scoffed at the idea that Mr. Hu was on hunger strike. The latter seemed to be affected with high blood pressure which must have lasted for months or years and could not have been brought on suddenly.
pages.zh:
1931年1月14日，南京。
“张学良将军……与张作相将军……之间表面下进行的 supremacy 斗争正达到高潮。……关系已紧张到破裂的边缘。……另有报道称，张将军已决定将其满洲军队总司令的职务移交给在满洲拥有实权的张作相将军。”

“有关于张元帅与张作相将军不和的谣言。然而，据沈阳来电，这些谣言毫无根据。……”
路透社，1931年1月15日。
“这些宣传代理人所做的任何陈述均无事实依据。……”
——《字林西报》，1931年1月25日。

这些传闻中的政治变动从未发生。

1931年1月16日，北平。
“王正廷博士今晨从天津抵达此间（北平）。……在离开之前，他将拜访此间的外国外交代表，请他们将公使馆迁往南京，那里已为各外交机构选定了地点。”

“关于公使馆迁往南京的问题，既然首都已为他们选定并预留了地点，他们可以在觉得方便的时候随时搬迁。”
《北平导报》，1931年1月18日。
“外交部正在将如此指定（用于容纳各外国公使馆）的土地地图发送给各位公使，以便他们从中做出选择。”
《国民新闻》，1931年1月19日。

王正廷博士从未拜访过外交代表。

1931年3月2日，南京。
“总司令蒋介石将立法院院长胡汉民先生拘禁在汤山。胡先生昨晚11点访问将军总部时被扣押。”

“中央执行委员会常务委员会今晨决定，将采纳‘约法’（即在宪政时期永久宪法颁布之前，训政时期的临时宪法）的问题列入5月5日国民大会讨论的紧急措施之中。
“任命了一个由10名成员组成的委员会，包括吴稚晖先生和王宠惠博士，负责起草这部‘约法’（临时宪法）。
“然而，胡汉民先生持相反意见，并提交了辞呈。
“中执委常委会认为采纳‘约法’严格符合孙中山博士的观点，并接受了胡汉民先生辞去国务委员和立法院院长等职务的申请……
“胡汉民先生将留在南京协助政府。”
——官方公报，南京，1931年3月2日。

1931年3月3日，南京
“有谣言称，胡汉民先生……已开始绝食抗议，作为他挑战总司令的唯一剩余武器。”

胡先生于3月8日星期日返回其在市内（南京）的私宅。
刘恒瑞博士于3月6日检查了胡先生，并断然否认有关胡先生有任何昏厥发作的报道。他对胡先生绝食的说法嗤之以鼻。后者似乎患有高血压，这肯定已持续数月或数年，不可能是突然引发的。

has been promoted to Manager of the Domei News Agency.

February 2, 1937.    Morning Reference.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated Feb.1:

THE THREE JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS IN SHANGHAI

The three Japanese newspapers in Shanghai are the "Shanghai Mainichi," the "Shanghai Nippo" and the "Shanghai Nichi Nichi." The "Shanghai Mainichi" is connected with the "Osaka Mainichi," the "Shanghai Nippo" is related to the "Osaka Asahi."
In Shanghai the Japanese population is about 30,000; yet there are three independent Japanese newspapers. These papers are working at a loss.
The "Shanghai Mainichi" is supported by the Japanese War Office. Not long ago, this newspaper published an article written by Murobushi criticising the War Office. This gave great offence to the War Office. Later, the newspaper re-established itself with the War Office. A subsidy of about $500 a month is now being given the newspaper by the Military Officers Department.
The "Shanghai Nippo" has the support of the Japanese Foreign Office. The Editor of this newspaper is known as a "China expert." The newspaper is given a secret subsidy of from $500 to $1,000 a month by the Japanese Embassy.
Until last winter, the "Shanghai Nichi Nichi" was not in receipt of any subsidy, but since it began the publication of the Chinese edition, it has entered into relations with "Manchukuo." The amount of the subsidy is unknown.
After the unification of the news agencies by the Domei News Agency, the Japanese Central Department came to the conclusion that the existence of the three newspapers in Shanghai is liable to obstruct Japan's policy towards China. Therefore, an order for an investigation has been issued.
Two of the editors of the Japanese newspapers regard themselves as "China experts." They are Mr. Fukamachi of the "Shanghai Mainichi" and Mr. Hata of the "Shanghai Nippo." They are the heads of rival papers. Therefore, in case of the amalgamation of the three newspapers, the selection of a chief will not be an easy task.
Of late, owing to financial difficulties, the question of amalgamating the three newspapers has been raised. Various official organs are studying the problem. The amalgamation of these three newspapers will probably be effected after the political crisis in Japan has been settled.

（批：Sp. Br. Quite useful information if true. MB）
pages.zh:
1937年2月2日。    晨间参考译文。

2月1日《华美晚报》：

上海的三家日本报纸

上海的三家日本报纸是《上海每日新闻》、《上海日报》和《上海日日新闻》。《上海每日新闻》与《大阪每日新闻》有关联，《上海日报》与《大阪朝日新闻》有关联。
在上海，日本人口约为30,000人；然而却有三家独立的日本报纸。这些报纸均在亏损运营。
《上海每日新闻》得到日本陆军省的支持。不久前，该报发表了一篇由 Murobushi 撰写的批评陆军省的文章。这引起了陆军省的极大不满。后来，该报与陆军省重修旧好。目前，军官部每月给予该报约500美元的津贴。
《上海日报》得到日本外务省的支持。该报编辑被称为“中国通”。日本大使馆每月秘密给予该报500至1,000美元的津贴。
直到去年冬天，《上海日日新闻》还未收到任何津贴，但自从开始出版中文版以来，它已与“满洲国”建立关系。津贴金额不详。
在同盟通讯社统一各新闻机构后，日本中央部门得出结论，认为上海这三家报纸的存在可能会阻碍日本对华政策。因此，已发布调查命令。
两家日本报纸的编辑自视为“中国通”。他们是《上海每日新闻》的 Fukamachi 先生和《上海日报》的 Hata 先生。他们是竞争对手报纸的负责人。因此，如果三家报纸合并，选拔主管并非易事。
最近，由于财务困难，提出了合并三家报纸的问题。各官方机构正在研究这一问题。这三家报纸的合并可能会在日本政治危机平息后进行。

（批注：特科。如果属实，这是非常有用的信息。MB）

The three Japanese newspapers in Shanghai are the "Shanghai Mainichi," the "Shanghai Nippo" and the "Shanghai Nichi Nichi." The "Shanghai Mainichi" is connected with the "Osaka Mainichi," the "Shanghai Nippo" is related to the "Osaka Asahi."

In Shanghai the Japanese population is about 30,000; yet there are three independent Japanese newspapers. These papers are working at a loss.

The "Shanghai Mainichi" is supported by the Japanese War Office. Not long ago, this newspaper published an article written by Murobushi criticising the War Office. This gave great offence to the War Office. Later, the newspaper re-established itself with the War Office. A subsidy of about $500 a month is now being given the newspaper by the Military Officers Department.

The "Shanghai Nippo" has the support of the Japanese Foreign Office. The Editor of this newspaper is known as a "China expert." The newspaper is given a secret subsidy of from $500 to $1,000 a month by the Japanese Embassy.

Until last winter, the "Shanghai Nichi Nichi" was not in receipt of any subsidy, but since it began the publication of the Chinese edition, it has entered into relations with "Manchukuo." The amount of the subsidy is unknown.

After the unification of the news agencies by the Domei News Agency, the Japanese Central Department came to the conclusion that the existence of the three newspapers in Shanghai is liable to obstruct Japan's policy towards China. Therefore, an order for an investigation has been issued.

Two of the editors of the Japanese newspapers regard themselves as "China experts." They are Mr. Fukamachi of the "Shanghai Mainichi" and Mr. Hata of the "Shanghai Nippo." They are the heads of rival papers. Therefore, in case of the amalgamation of the three newspapers, the selection of a chief will not be an easy task.

Of late, owing to financial difficulties, the question of amalgamating the three newspapers has been raised. Various official organs are studying the problem. The amalgamation of these three newspapers will probably be effected after the political crisis in Japan has settled.

1937年2月2日。    晨间译文。

2月1日《华美晚报》：

上海的三家日本报纸

上海的三家日本报纸是《上海每日新闻》、《上海日报》和《上海日日新闻》。《上海每日新闻》与《大阪每日新闻》有关联，《上海日报》与《大阪朝日新闻》有关联。

在上海，日本人口约为30,000人；然而却有三家独立的日本报纸。这些报纸均在亏损运营。

《上海每日新闻》得到日本陆军省的支持。不久前，该报发表了一篇由 Murobushi 撰写的批评陆军省的文章。这引起了陆军省的极大不满。后来，该报与陆军省重修旧好。目前，军官部每月给予该报约500美元的津贴。

《上海日报》得到日本外务省的支持。该报编辑被称为“中国通”。日本大使馆每月秘密给予该报500至1,000美元的津贴。

直到去年冬天，《上海日日新闻》还未收到任何津贴，但自从开始出版中文版以来，它已与“满洲国”建立关系。津贴金额不详。

在同盟通讯社统一各新闻机构后，日本中央部门得出结论，认为上海这三家报纸的存在可能会阻碍日本对华政策。因此，已发布调查命令。

两家日本报纸的编辑自视为“中国通”。他们是《上海每日新闻》的 Fukamachi 先生和《上海日报》的 Hata 先生。他们是竞争对手报纸的负责人。因此，如果三家报纸合并，选拔主管并非易事。

最近，由于财务困难，提出了合并三家报纸的问题。各官方机构正在研究这一问题。这三家报纸的合并可能会在日本政治危机平息后进行。

ANTI-JAPANESE CHINESE SOLDIERS RETURNING TO CHINA FROM
SOVIET RUSSIA

A telegram from Nanking dated
April 20 reports that the Nanking Government has decided

be given jobs. About 1,000 more of these soldiers are
returning soon and they will also be given employment..
The remainder of these soldiers will return to China
from Soviet Russia later.

警方当局将在五一节保持警惕

上海所有警方当局将在5月期间保持警惕，监视共产主义活动，因为除了五一节外，5月还有许多劳工纪念日和中国的国耻日。

我们，上海的日本报纸和新闻机构，特此发表声明，宣布我们已成立“上海日本报纸与新闻机构联盟”，旨在按照当前局势的要求，通过合作履行我们的重要使命。
联盟的成员报纸和新闻机构如下：-
日本电报新闻社、《东京读卖新闻》上海通讯员、《上海每日新闻》、《报知新闻》上海通讯员、上海泰道新闻社（Shanghai Taido News Agency）、《时事新报》上海通讯员、上海同盟通讯社、《满洲日报》上海通讯员、《大阪每日新闻》和《东京日日新闻》上海通讯员、《上海日报》、《东京和大阪朝日新闻》上海通讯员以及《上海日日新闻》。

杀害李英鲁的凶手被判处死刑

据报道，4月24日上午11时，在朝鲜京城上诉法院，一名30岁的朝鲜人 Aum Sho n Bong 因在1935年3月谋杀上海朝鲜人居留民团顾问李英鲁（Lee Young Ro）而被判处死刑。

反日中国士兵从苏俄返回中国

南京4月20日电称，南京政府决定向李杜支队中那些从满洲国逃往苏俄、目前陷入贫困境地的反日反满洲国士兵提供资金，助其返回中国。据报道，其中300人已返回中国，并将获得工作机会。另有约1,000名此类士兵即将返回，他们也将获得就业安排。其余士兵稍后将从苏俄返回中国。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, May 1, 1936

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH ...）

Japanese Newspapermen
Form Press Association

The city's leading Japanese newspapermen joined forces on Wednesday to form the Japanese Press Association of Shanghai, the local Nipponese papers report.

The inaugural meeting, held at the Japanese Club on Wednesday morning, was attended by representatives of 12 newspapers and news agencies.

The aims of the new organization, according to its sponsors, include the raising of the standards of Japanese journalism and the protection of newspapermen. Under the body's rules, all decisions would have to be unanimous.

The member-organizations of the Association include the Nippon Dempo News Agency, the Domei News Agency, The Osaka Mainichi and the Tokyo Nichi-Nichi, The Osaka and Tokyo Asahi, The Yomiuri, The Daito News Agency, The Manshu Nichi-Nichi, The Shanghai Nippo, The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi, The Shanghai Mainichi, the Jiji Shimpo.

The representative of the Osaka Mainichi and the Tokyo Nichi-Nichi will be appointed on the arrival here of a successor of Mr. Nobukazu Tachibara, former manager of the agency here, who suddenly left for Japan last week.

March 31, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Eastern Daily News (東方日報) dated Mar. 29,30 & 31.

JAPANESE OWNED NEWSPAPERS IN CHINA

It is estimated that some 100 newspapers managed by Japanese have been established in China. Most of them are supported with funds from the Japanese Government. Their mission is to carry out propaganda work abroad. We publish the following details of our investigations into 46 Japanese newspapers:

In Shanghai

The first issue of the "Shanghai Mainichi" appeared in the 9th Moon of the 7th Year of Taisho. It is a private undertaking with a capital of 70,000 Yen. It publishes a daily paper of 8 pages for the morning edition and 4 pages for the evening edition. It has a circulation of about 7,000 copies. The president of the paper is Fukamachi.

The first issue of the "Shanghai Nippo," which is privately owned, and has a capital of 150,000 Yen, appeared in the 26th Year of Meiji. It publishes a morning edition of 8 pages and an evening edition of 4 pages, and has a circulation of about 4,500 copies. The president is Hata.

The "Shanghai Nichi Nichi" is also a private paper with a capital of 100,000 Yen. Its first issue appeared in the 10th Moon of the 3rd Year of Taisho. It publishes a morning edition of 8 pages and an evening edition of 4 pages. The president is Miyaji.

The "Kiangnan Tseng Pao" (江南正報 Chinese edition) made its first appearance in the 2nd Year of Showa. The president was Yamada and the Editor-in-Chief was a Chinese named Li Ying Han. (李英漢).

In Tientsin

The "Peking-Tientsin Nichi Nichi" is a private undertaking, with Morikawa as president. It has 40 Chinese compositors. Its first issue appeared in the 10th Moon of the 7th Year of Taisho.

The "Tientsin Nippo" made its first appearance in the 1st Moon of 43rd Year of Meiji. It is a private paper and publishes a morning and an evening edition of 4 pages each. The president is Shindo.

The first issue of the "Chung Mei Wan Pao" (中美晚報 Chinese edition) made its first appearance in the 4th Moon of the 8th Year of Showa. It has a circulation of 9,000 copies. The president is Mitani with a Chinese named Liu Zou Ching (劉修景) as Editor-in-Chief.

The "Tientsin Pao" came into existence in the 7th Year of Showa. It publishes a morning and an evening edition. The president is Ando.

In Peiping

The first issue of the "Peking-Shin Bun" appeared in the 12th Year of Taisho. The president is Morikawa. It is a Peiping Branch of the "Peking-Tientsin Nichi Nichi."

在华日办报纸

据估计，由日本人管理的报纸在中国已创办约100家。其中大多数由日本政府提供资金支持。其使命是在海外开展宣传工作。现将我们对46家日本报纸的调查结果详情刊登如下：

在上海

《上海每日新闻》首期发行于大正七年九月。这是一家私营企业，资本为7万日元。它出版日报，早版8页，晚版4页。发行量约为7,000份。该报社长为深町（Fukamachi）。

《上海日日新闻》也是一家私人报纸，资本为10万日元。其首期发行于大正三年十月。它出版早版8页和晚版4页。社长为宫地（Miyaji）。

《江南正报》（中文版）首期发行于昭和二年。社长为山田（Yamada），主编为一名叫李英汉的中国人。

在天津

《京津日日新闻》是一家私营企业，社长为森川（Morikawa）。它有40名中国排字工人。其首期发行于大正七年十月。

Tokyo, Dec. 17.
The inaugural meeting of the Domei
Tsushin Sha, the newly-organized
Japanese national news agency, took
place this afternoon. It was decided
to start business on January 1, 1935.
The organizing committee, which
comprises representatives of the lead-
ing newspapers and the Japan Broad-
casting Association, has been active
since last May in organizing the
agency.
Shimbun Rengo, the great Japanese
news agency, is to be merged into
the Domei Tsushin Sha, and it is
confidently expected that Nippon
Dempo, the other principal Japanese
agency, will follow suit.—Reuter.

The first telegraphic information received by the local newspapers about the disturbances created by the traitorous elements in Tientsin was supplied by the Rengo News Agency, a Japanese concern. C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O...9121/10

NEW NEWS AGENCY
FOR JAPAN

To Merge Facilities Of
Shimbun Rengo And
Nippon Dempo

TOKYO, Nov. 7.—Permission to form a new news agency, which will become the major distributor of news in Japan, was issued today by the Ministry of Communications.

The new corporation, to be known as the Domei Tsushin-sha, will merge the facilities of the Shimbun Rengo and Nippon Dempo News Agencies.

Under the terms of the plan, which has been the subject of a two-year controversy, the Nippon Dempo will be purchased by the state-owned Japan Broadcasting Association, which will become a partner in the new concern.

Permission to form the new enterprise was handed by Mr. Keisuke Mochizuki, Minister of Communications, to Mr. Takichi Tanaka, former Ambassador to Moscow and the head of the preparatory committee, and other members of the body.

The newspapers sponsoring the new agency immediately dispatched invitations to all papers, at present not subscribing to the Rengo Service, to join the Domei Tsushin-sha.

The list of sponsoring newspapers includes the "Asahi," "Kokumin Shimbun," "Yomiuri Shimbun" and "Chugai Shogyo," all of Tokyo; the Osaka "Mainichi"; the Hokkai "Times"; the "Kahoku Shimbun," "Sendai"; and the "Chugoku Shimbun," Okayama.

Representatives of these papers will meet on November 11 to discuss the details of the plan at the Tokyo Kaikan.

In preparing the project, Mr. Mochizuki was assisted by Mr. Mamoru Shigemitsu, Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs, and Mr. Eiji Amau, Director of the Gaimusho's Bureau of Information. The War and Navy have also placed themselves on record in favour of the project.

Under the plan, Rengo will form the backbone of the new organization, while the facilities of the Nippon Dempo will be contributed by the Ministry of Communications, through the Broadcasting Association.—Rengo.

日本新通讯社

日本电报通讯社之设施

东京，11月7日电。——交通部今日颁发许可，准予成立一家新的通讯社，该社将成为日本主要的新闻分发机构。

这家新公司名为“同盟通信社”（Domei Tsushin-sha），将合并联合新闻社（Shimbun Rengo）和日本电报通讯社（Nippon Dempo）的设施。

根据这项已引发两年争议的计划的条款，日本电报通讯社将由国有的日本广播协会收购，后者将成为新企业的合作伙伴。

交通大臣望月圭介先生向驻莫斯科前大使、筹备委员会主席田中隆吉先生及其他委员会成员颁发了成立新企业的许可证。

赞助新通讯社的报纸立即向目前尚未订阅联合新闻社服务的所有报纸发出邀请，请其加入同盟通信社。

赞助报纸名单包括：东京的《朝日新闻》、《国民新闻》、《读卖新闻》和《中外商业新报》；大阪的《每日新闻》；北海道的《时报》；仙台的《河北新报》；以及冈山的《中国新闻》。

这些报纸的代表将于11月11日在东京会馆开会，讨论计划细节。

在筹备该项目时，望月先生得到了外务次官重光葵先生和外务省情报局局长天羽英二先生的协助。陆军省和海军省也已记录在案，表示支持该项目。

根据该计划，联合新闻社将构成新组织的骨干，而日本电报通讯社的设施则由交通部通过广播协会提供。——联合社。

Ta Mei Jan Pao published the following article on May 23.

JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS AND NEWS AGENCIES IN SHANGHAI

The "Shanghai Nippo", a Japanese daily, located at the corner of Barchet and North Szechuen Roads, was established in 1904. It is a private commercial concern with a capital of $150,000. It has branches at Tokyo, Osaka, Tsingtao, Hankow, Nanking, etc. The managing director is K. Hata. It publishes two pages in the morning and one page in the evening. It is supported by the Japanese navy.

The "Shanghai Nichi Nichi Shimbun", a Japanese daily, established in 1914, is a private commercial concern with a capital of $100,000. The managing director is K. Miyaji. It publishes two issues every day, morning and evening, the combined issues consisting of three pages.

The "Shanghai Mainichi Shimbun", a Japanese daily, was established in 1918 and is located at the corner of Thorne and Woosung Roads. It is a commercial limited concern with a capital of $70,000. The managing director is S. Fukamachi. It publishes two pages in the morning and one page in the evening.

The "Kiangnan Tsen Pao" is a Japanese daily published in the Chinese language, located on Range Road. It was formerly the "Kiangnan Evening Post", established in 1927 and ceased publishing in 1930. In 1932 the name of the paper was changed to the "Kiangnan Tsen Pao". This paper has a capital of $100,000. The managing director is J. Yamada. The principal object of this paper is to foment internal disturbances and to create rumours regarding China.

The Dentsu News Agency was organized by S. Mitsunaga in 1901 with a capital of $1,000,000, but this figure has now been increased to $10,000,000. Its head office is in Tokyo, with branches in Shanghai, Peiping, Tientsin, Tsingtao, Hankow, Tsinan, Canton, Harbin and Dairen. The principal object of this news agency is to propagate news disadvantageous to China but beneficial to Japan.

The Rengo News Agency was established in 1926 and was formerly known as the Eastern News Agency and the International News Agency. The organization of this news agency is similar to that of the United Press. This news agency receives the support of more than 50 Japanese newspapers in addition to a large subsidy from the Foreign Office of the Japanese Imperial Government. Branches have been established in Nanking, Tientsin, Peiping, Shanghai, Hankow, Canton, Harbin, Kwenchentsu and Dairen. The agency propagates news disadvantageous to China.

THE RISE AND FALL OF (the) JAPANESE PRESS IN CHINA HAD A
CLOSE RELATIONSHIP WITH THE POLITICAL SITUATION IN THIS

IN 1911 THE OLDEST OF EMPIRES BECAME THE YOUNGEST OF
REPUBLICS. FOR NEARLY SEVENTEEN YEARS, UNTIL THE
UNIFICATION OF THE COUNTRY UNDER THE KUOMINTANG RULE
IN JUNE, 1928, THE COUNTRY HAD NEITHER UNITY NOR PEACE.
IT IS NEEDLESS HERE TO TRACE THE FORTUNES OF THE RIVAL
MILITARY LEADERS AND THEIR POLITICAL PUPPETS. AFTER THE
DEATH OF YUAN SHIH-KAI, GENERALS LI YUAN-HUNG, TUAN CHI-
JUI, TSAO KUN, WU PEI-FU, FENG YU-HSIANG AND CHANG TSO-
LIN EACH DOMINATED THE SO-CALLED PEKING GOVERNMENT FOR
A TIME. THESE RIVALS, IN SHIFTING COMBINATIONS, ALTERNATED
AS MASTERS OF THE GOVERNMENT.

THE CIVIL WAR IN CHINA AFFORDED A SPLENDID OPPORTUNITY
FOR JAPANESE NEWS AGENCIES AND NEWSPAPERS HERE TO
ESTABLISH A NEWS MONOPOLY WHICH LASTED MORE THAN A
DECADE AND WHICH WAS ONLY BROUGHT TO AN END BY THE
COLLAPSE OF THE PEKING GOVERNMENT. DURING THESE YEARS
OF BLOOD AND FIRE, THE PROVINCIAL MILITARY GOVERNORS,
"TUCHUNS" THEY WERE CALLED, MAINTAINED SEPARATE ARMIES,
and MADE WAR ON ONE ANOTHER OR ON THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT.

在华日本报刊的兴衰与
本国的政治局势有着密切的关系。

1911年，最古老的帝国变成了最年轻的共和国。在近十七年的时间里，直到1928年6月在国民党统治下实现国家统一之前，这个国家既没有统一也没有和平。此处无需追溯各派军事领袖及其政治傀儡的命运。袁世凯死后，黎元洪、段祺瑞、曹锟、吴佩孚、冯玉祥和张作霖等将军曾先后主导所谓的北京政府。这些对手通过不断变化的组合，轮流担任政府的主宰。

中国的内战为在此地的日本通讯社和报纸提供了一个绝佳的机会，以建立一种持续了十多年的新闻垄断，这种垄断直到北京政府垮台才告结束。在这些血与火的岁月里，各省的军事督军（即所谓“督军”）维持着各自的军队，并相互交战或与中央政府交战。

PLACE HAD NO WAY OF GETTING ACCURATE INFORMATION ABOUT

THOSE DAYS AND MEN LIKE GENERAL CHANG CHUNG-CHANG HAD

日本方面---2.

由于审查如此严格，一地的本土报业无法获取关于另一省份活动的准确信息。即使他们确实收到了一些有趣的新闻电讯，也不敢发布这些电讯。当时没有所谓的新闻法，像张宗昌将军这样的人对新闻自由毫无尊重。因此，中国报纸依靠外国通讯社来获取有关政治和军事发展的最新信息。北平日报的编辑们过去常在新闻文章的开头写道：“据外籍消息来源获悉”。编辑们认为，插入这一条款可以使他们不被指控为谣言制造者，此外，这一条款还会给读者留下新闻源自独立因而可靠来源的印象。

很少有外国通讯社在中国定期分发新闻。诚然，英国路透社在其常规新闻服务中刊载来自中国各地的电讯，但当时的中国日报在中文新闻方面依赖的是日本通讯社，即东洋通讯社（Toho）和日本电报通讯社（Nippon Denpo）。这些竞争对手

pages.en:
JAPANESE---3.

"TUCHUNS" ALL HAD JAPANESE ADVISORS. ARMS COULD BE
PURCHASED FROM JAPAN AND IN SOME CASES FINANCIAL AID
WAS ALSO FORTHCOMING FROM OUR NEIGHBOUR. AS A RESULT
EVERY POLITICAL OR MILITARY MOVE THE CHINESE "TUCHUNS"
MADE WAS INSTANTANEOUSLY REPORTED TO THE JAPANESE
LEGATION AT PEIPING. MR. KENKICHI YOSHIZAWA, AT ONE
TIME JAPANESE MINISTER TO CHINA, USED TO GRANT WEEKLY
INTERVIEWS TO JAPANESE CORRESPONDENTS AT PEIPING GIVING
BRIEF SUMMARIES OF THE POLITICAL SITUATION IN CHINA.

THE BOMBING OF MARSHAL CHANG TSO-LIN'S TRAIN AT
HUANGKUTUN ON JUNE 4, 1928, WAS ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT
NEWS EVENTS IN CHINA'S RECENT HISTORY. THE JAPANESE NEWS
AGENCIES HAD OTHERS BEATEN BY A MILE. ON JUNE 3, IN VIEW
OF THE RAPID ADVANCE OF THE SHANSI FORCES UNDER GENERAL
YEN HSI-SHAN, KUOMINCHUN UNDER MARSHAL FENG YU-HSIANG
AND NATIONALIST ARMIES UNDER GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK
TOWARDS PEIPING AND TIENTSIN, MARSHAL CHANG TSO-LIN
LEFT FOR MUKDEN, NOW KNOWN AS LIAOLING. TWO JAPANESE
MILITARY ADVISERS WERE ON BOARD THE SPECIAL TRAIN. ONE
LEFT THE TRAIN AT TIENTSIN. THE OTHER WAS WITH MARSHAL
CHANG TSO-LIN WHEN THE MYSTERIOUS BOMB EXPLODED AND
FATALLY INJURED THE "STRONG MAN" OF THE THREE EASTERN
PROVINCES. WHEN THE CHINESE OFFICERS WERE BUSILY OCCUPIED
pages.zh:
日本方面---3.

“督军”们都拥有日本顾问。武器可以从日本购买，在某些情况下，我们的邻国还提供财政援助。结果，中国“督军”采取的每一项政治或军事行动都会立即报告给驻北京的日本公使馆。曾任日本驻华公使的芳泽谦吉先生，过去每周在北京接受日本记者的采访，简要介绍中国的政治局势。

1928年6月4日，张作霖元帅的列车在皇姑屯被炸，是中国近代史上最重要的新闻事件之一。日本通讯社远远领先于其他同行。6月3日，鉴于阎锡山将军率领的晋军、冯玉祥元帅率领的国民军以及蒋介石将军率领的国民党军队迅速向北京和天津推进，张作霖元帅启程前往沈阳（现称辽宁）。两名日本军事顾问登上了专列。其中一人在天津下车。当神秘的炸弹爆炸并致命地伤害了这位“东北三省强人”时，另一名顾问正与张作霖元帅在一起。当中国军官们忙于

pages.en:
JAPANESE---4.

IN THE TASK OF BRINGING THE DYING LEADER INTO THE CITY,
THE JAPANESE ADVISER WALKED TO THE NEAREST TELEPHONE AND
REPORTED EVERYTHING THAT HAD HAPPENED TO THE JAPANESE
CONSUL-GENERAL AT MUKDEN. THE JAPANESE CORRESPONDENTS
AT MUKDEN HAD THE STORY, AND NOBODY ELSE. WHAT WAS MORE
STARTLING WAS THAT THE WORLD HAD TO GO TO TOKYO DURING
THE FOLLOWING DAYS FOR the LATEST NEWS ABOUT CHANG TSO-LIN'S
CONDITION.

AT ONE TIME THE CHINESE PEOPLE IN NORTH CHINA WENT TO
JAPANESE-OWNED CHINESE LANGUAGE NEWSPAPERS FOR NEWS. THE
MUKDEN SHEN CHIH SHIH PAO HAD A DAILY CIRCULATION OF
16,000 COPIES. THE SAME COMPANY HAD A DAILY PAPER IN
PEIPING, SHIH TIEN SHIH PAO, WHICH HAD A CIRCULATION OF
12,000 COPIES. THE SHIH TIEN SHIH PAO WAS VERY POPULAR
AT PEIPING FOR IT WAS THE ONLY PAPER THAT DARED TO
PUBLICLY DENOUNCE YUAN SHIH-KAI FOR HIS ATTEMPT TO RESTORE
THE MONARCHY, WITH HIMSELF AS EMPEROR. THE JAPANESE
PAPERS COULD PUBLISH ANYTHING THEY LIKED AND GET AWAY
WITH IT.

THE COLLAPSE OF THE PEKING GOVERNMENT, HOWEVER, IN
1928 MARKED THE END OF the JAPANESE NEWS MONOPOLY IN THIS
COUNTRY. A POWERFUL CENTRAL GOVERNMENT WAS ESTABLISHED
AT NANKING, DIRECTLY UNDER THE CENTRAL EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE
pages.zh:
日本方面---4.

将垂死的领导人抬进城时，那位日本顾问走到最近的电话旁，向驻沈阳的日本总领事报告了发生的一切。沈阳的日本记者独家掌握了这一故事，其他人均不知情。更令人震惊的是，在接下来的几天里，全世界不得不去东京获取关于张作霖状况的最新消息。

一度，华北的中国民众从日本人拥有的中文报纸获取新闻。《盛京时报》的日发行量为16,000份。同一家公司在北平拥有一份日报《实报》，发行量为12,000份。《实报》在北平非常受欢迎，因为它是唯一敢于公开谴责袁世凯企图复辟帝制、自立为皇帝的报纸。日本报纸可以刊登任何它们喜欢的内容而免受惩罚。

然而，1928年北京政府的垮台标志着日本在这个国家的新闻垄断的终结。一个强大的中央政府在南京建立，直接隶属于中央执行委员会

pages.en:
JAPANESE---5.

OF THE KUOMINTANG, A PUBLICITY DEPARTMENT WAS ORGANIZED
EXERCISING A COMPLETE CONTROL OVER THE EDITORIAL POLICY
OF THE NATIVE NEWSPAPERS, NEWS AGENCIES, AND PERIODICALS.
THE NEW PRESS LAW PROMULGATED BY THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT
ON DECEMBER 16, 1930, CLEARLY STATES THAT PUBLICATIONS
SHALL NOT PUBLISH THE FOLLOWING:
(1) ARTICLES ATTACKING THE KUOMINTANG OR THREE PEOPLES
PRINCIPLES.
(2) ARTICLES ATTEMPTING TO SUBVERT THE NATIONAL GOVERN-
MENT AND PREJUDICIAL TO INTERESTS OF THE REPUBLIC OF CHINA.
(3) ARTICLES ENDANGERING PUBLIC PEACE AND ORDER.
(4) ARTICLES PREJUDICIAL TO GOOD MORALS.
IN ORDER TO SEND PRESS MESSAGES BY CHINESE TELEGRAPH
AND RADIO ADMINISTRATIONS, THE FOREIGN PRESS CORRESPONDENTS
IN CHINA HAVE TO APPLY FOR REGISTRATION CERTIFICATES AT
THE PUBLICITY DEPARTMENT OF THE MINISTRY FOR FOREIGN
AFFAIRS. ONLY AFTER A FOREIGN PRESS CORRESPONDENT RECEIVES
A CERTIFICATE FROM THE MINISTRY FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS CAN
HE OBTAIN A REGULAR PRESS CARD FROM THE MINISTRY OF
COMMUNICATIONS. THIS ENABLES THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT TO
EXERCISE A CERTAIN AMOUNT OF CONTROL OVER FOREIGN PRESS
CORRESPONDENTS IN THIS COUNTRY. FURTHERMORE, THE GOVERNMENT
CENSORS AT THE VARIOUS TELEGRAPH AND TELEPHONE OFFICES
pages.zh:
日本方面---5.

国民党之下，组建了一个宣传部，对本土报纸、通讯社和期刊的编辑方针实行全面控制。国民政府于1930年12月16日颁布的新新闻法明确规定，出版物不得刊登以下内容：
(1) 攻击国民党或三民主义的文章。
(2) 企图颠覆国民政府并有损中华民国利益的文章。
(3) 危害公共治安与秩序的文章。
(4) 有伤风化的文章。
为了通过中国电信和无线电管理部门发送新闻稿件，在华的外国记者必须向外务部宣传处申请注册证书。只有在外籍记者从外务部获得证书后，才能从交通部获得正式的记者证。这使得国民政府能够对在华的外国记者行使一定程度的控制。此外，各地电报和电话局的政府审查员

pages.en:
JAPANESE---6.

CAN ALWAYS SUPPRESS ANY NEWS DESPATCHES WHICH THEY THINK
ARE PREJUDICIAL TO THE INTERESTS OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT.
IN THE WINTER OF 1929 GENERAL SHIH YU-SAN'S TROOPS
MUTINIED AT PUKOW. NANKING WAS DENUDED OF LOYAL TROOPS AT
THE TIME. THE THIRD DIVISION UNDER GENERAL MAO PING-WEN
AND THE EIGHTH DIVISION UNDER GENERAL CHU SHAO-LIANG WERE
SENT TO CANTON TO DEFEND THAT IMPORTANT CITY AGAINST THE
FAMOUS "IRONSIDES" UNDER GENERAL CHANG FA-KWEI. THE SIXTH
DIVISION UNDER GENERAL KU CHU-TUNG AND THE NINTH DIVISION
UNDER GENERAL CHIANG TING-WEN WERE SENT TO HANKOW. THE
CADETS OF THE CENTRAL MILITARY ACADEMY ALSO JOINED THE
DEFENCE FORCE OF HANKOW. THERE WAS A REPORT AT THE TIME
THAT MARSHAL FENG YU-HSIANG'S TROOPS WERE PREPARING TO
MARCH DOWN FROM HONAN ALONG THE PEIPING-HANKOW RAILWAY.
THE MUTINY OF SHIH'S TROOPS, ABOUT 30,000 WELL EQUIPPED
SOLDIERS, NATURALLY MADE THINGS LOOK BAD FOR NANKING. TO
MAKE MATTERS WORSE, THE SHANGHAI-NANKING RAILWAY WAS CUT
AT SEVERAL PLACES BY IRREGULAR TROOPS. SOME ALARMIST
SPREAD THE NEWS THAT GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK HAD ESCAPED
FROM NANKING TO SHANGHAI BY AIRPLANE. THE NANKING
CORRESPONDENT OF NIPPON DEMPO TOOK THIS RUMOUR SERIOUSLY
AND SENT A LONG-DISTANCE TELEPHONE MESSAGE TO SHANGHAI
STATING THAT GENERAL CHIANG HAD "DISAPPEARED IN THE AIR."
pages.zh:
日本方面——6.

他们总是可以压制任何他们认为有损国民政府利益的新闻电讯。1929年冬，石友三部队在浦口哗变。当时南京缺乏忠于政府的部队。毛炳文将军指挥的第三师和朱绍良将军指挥的第八师被派往广州，以保卫这座重要城市，抵御张发奎将军麾下著名的“铁军”。顾祝同将军指挥的第六师和蒋鼎文将军指挥的第九师被派往汉口。中央陆军军官学校的学员也加入了汉口的防卫部队。当时有报告称，冯玉祥元帅的部队正准备沿平汉铁路从河南南下。石部约三万名装备精良的士兵发生哗变，自然使南京方面的形势显得十分严峻。更糟糕的是，沪宁铁路多处被非正规部队切断。一些危言耸听者散布消息，称蒋介石将军已乘飞机从南京逃往上海。《日本电报》（Nippon Dempo）驻南京记者将此谣言当真，并向上海打长途电话，称蒋将军已“在空中失踪”。

pages.en:
JAPANESE---7.

FOR THIS, THE NIPPON DEMPO CORRESPONDENTS IN CHINA
WERE DEPRIVED OF THE PRIVILEGE OF USING CHINESE TELEGRAPH,
RADIO AND LONG-DISTANCE TELEPHONE FACILITIES. THE NEWS-
PAPERS WHICH PUBLISHED THIS SENSATIONAL REPORT WERE DENIED
THE USE OF THE CHINESE POST. THIS PROVED TO BE AN EFFECTIVE
DISCIPLINARY MEASURE. IT STOPPED ALL THE OUTPORT CIRCULA-
TION OF SUCH PAPERS. THE MATTER WAS SOON SETTLED AFTER however who...
THE NIPPON DEMPO CORRESPONDENT AT NANKING OFFICIALLY
EXPRESSED HIS REGRET FOR THE DESPATCH OF THE ABOVE NEWS
ITEM.

THE RENGO CORRESPONDENT AT NANKING ALSO HAD HIS TROUBLES.
IN MARCH, 1931, MR. HU HAN-MIN, PRESIDENT OF THE LEGISLA-
TIVE YUAN, RESIGNED AS A RESULT OF HIS DISPUTE WITH
GENERAL CHIANG KAI-SHEK, CHAIRMAN OF THE NATIONAL GOVERN-
MENT, OVER THE PROVISIONAL CONSTITUTION ISSUE. THE RENGO
NANKING REPORT WAS THAT MR. HU WAS DETAINED BY GENERAL
CHIANG AT TANGSHAN, A HEALTH RESORT NEAR THE CAPITAL. ON
THE FOLLOWING DAY, RENGO HAD ANOTHER REPORT STATING THAT
MR. HU HAD GONE ON HUNGER STRIKE.

THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES PROMPTLY TOOK ACTION.
THE RENGO CORRESPONDENT AT NANKING WAS NOT ALLOWED TO USE
THE SHANGHAI-NANKING LONG-DISTANCE TELEPHONE. OF COURSE,
HE COULD NOT SEND EITHER TELEGRAPH OR RADIO MESSAGES. A
pages.zh:
日本方面——7.

为此，在华的“日本电报通讯社”（Nippon Dempo）记者被剥夺了使用中国电信、无线电及长途电话设施的特权。刊登这一耸人听闻报道的报纸被禁止使用中国邮政系统。事实证明，这是一项有效的惩戒措施。它阻止了此类报纸在所有外埠的发行。然而，此事很快得以解决……驻南京的“日本电报通讯社”记者正式就发送上述新闻稿件表示歉意。

驻南京的“联合通讯社”（Rengo）记者也遇到了麻烦。1931年3月，立法院院长胡汉民先生因在临时宪法问题上与国民政府主席蒋介石将军发生争执而辞职。“联合通讯社”从南京发出的报道称，胡先生被蒋介石将军拘禁于首都附近的疗养胜地汤山。次日，“联合通讯社”又发出一则报道，称胡先生已开始绝食抗议。

中国政府当局迅速采取行动。驻南京的“联合通讯社”记者被禁止使用上海至南京的长途电话。当然，他也无法发送任何电报或无线电消息。一

pages.en:
JAPANESE---8.

FOREIGN CORRESPONDENT IN NANKING DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON THE
LONG-DISTANCE TELEPHONE TO GET ANY NEWS OUT OF THE CHINESE
CAPITAL WITH REASONABLE SPEED. IT GENERALLY TAKES FROM
FOUR TO SIX HOURS TO GET A RADIO OR TELEGRAPH MESSAGE
THROUGH FROM NANKING TO SHANGHAI. THERE IS NO USE OF
SENDING ANY TELEGRAMS AFTER 9 O'CLOCK AT NIGHT. AN EXPRESS
LETTER WILL REACH SHANGHAI IN TEN HOURS. THE AIR MAIL IS
NOT DEPENDABLE. NEWS DOES NOT ALWAYS BREAK WHEN THERE
IS FINE WEATHER. FURTHERMORE, THESE AIR MAIL LETTERS HAVE
TO BE SENT IN BEFORE 10 O'CLOCK IN THE MORNING IN ORDER
TO CATCH THE AIRPLANE FOR SHANGHAI WHICH LEAVES NANKING
AT NOON . THERE IS NOT MUCH DOING IN THE CAPITAL EARLY
IN THE MORNING.

THIS GOVERNMENT DECISION TO DEPRIVE THE RENGO CORRES-
PONDENT OF THE PRIVILEGE OF USING THE LONG-DISTANCE
TELEPHONE WAS, THEREFORE, QUITE A SERIOUS MATTER. IT PUT
HIM IN A DIFFICULT POSITION. THERE WAS NO WAY FOR HIM TO
GET A NEWS DESPATCH THROUGH TO SHANGHAI WITH ANY REASON-
ABLE SPEED.

THE JAPANESE NEWS MONOPOLY IN CHINA WAS BROUGHT TO AN
END BY ANOTHER IMPORTANT FACTOR. ASIDE FROM EXERCISING
CERTAIN AMOUNT OF CONTROL OVER THE JAPANESE NEWS AGENCIES
AND NEWSPAPERS IN CHINA, THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AUTHORITIES
pages.zh:
日本方面——8.

名驻南京的外国记者完全依赖长途电话，才能以合理的速度将任何新闻从中国首都传出。通常，从南京向上海发送无线电或电报讯息需要四到六个小时。晚上九点以后发送任何电报都无济于事。快信需十小时才能抵达上海。航空邮件并不可靠。新闻并不总是在天气良好时爆发。此外，这些航空邮件必须在上午十点之前寄出，才能赶上中午从南京起飞前往上海的飞机。清晨时分，首都并无多少活动。

因此，政府决定剥夺联合通讯社记者使用长途电话的特权，是一件相当严重的事情。这使他陷入了困境。他无法以任何合理的速度将新闻电讯发送至上海。

日本在中国的新闻垄断局面因另一个重要因素而终结。除了对在华日本新闻机构和报纸行使一定程度的控制外，国民政府当局

pages.en:
JAPANESE---9.

GAVE EVERY FACILITY TO A CHINESE CORRESPONDENT FOR
GATHERING NEWS AT THE VARIOUS GOVERNMENT OFFICES.
THERE IS A FIXED SCHEDULE FOR GOVERNMENT MEETINGS. THE
CENTRAL EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE OF THE KUOMINTANG MEET ON
THURSDAYS, THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT COUNCIL ON FRIDAYS,
THE CENTRAL POLITICAL COUNCIL ON WEDNESDAYS, THE STATE
COUNCIL ON TUESDAYS AND THE LEGISLATIVE YUAN ON SATURDAYS.
THE DECISIONS OF THE ABOVE MEETINGS WERE RELEASED TO THE
PRESS BY THE SECRETARIATS OF THE RESPECTIVE BODIES. DR.
C. T. WANG, MINISTER FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS, GENERALLY GAVE
INTERVIEWS TO CHINESE CORRESPONDENTS ON FRIDAY MORNINGS.
AS A RESULT ONE SEES A STEADY DROP IN THE AMOUNT OF
COLUMN SPACE THE JAPANESE NEW AGENCIES GET IN THE CHINESE
NEWSPAPERS. THE PUBLICATION OF A NUMBER OF IMPORTANT
JAPANESE-OWNED NEWSPAPERS IN THIS COUNTRY HAS BEEN
DISCONTINUED. THE DISAPPEARANCE OF THE SHUN TIEN SHIH PAO
AND NORTH CHINA STANDARD FROM THE PEIPING NEWSPAPER LIST
QUICKLY FOLLOWED THE FALL OF THE NORTHERN CAPITAL INTO
THE HANDS OF THE NATIONALIST FORCES. ON JULY 31, 1929,
RENGO OFFICIALLY CAME IN TO TAKE THE PLACE OF TOHO, THE
RECOGNIZED OFFICIAL ORGAN OF THE JAPANESE FOREIGN OFFICE
IN CHINA. THE NEW POLICY OF RENGO AND NIPPON DEMPO IN
CHINA APPEARS TO BE ONE OF CONCENTRATING THEIR WORK TOWARDS
pages.zh:
日本方面——9.

为中国记者在各个政府机关采集新闻提供了各种便利。政府会议有固定的时间表。国民党中执委于周四开会，国民政府委员会于周五开会，中央政治委员会于周三开会，国务会议于周二开会，立法院于周六开会。上述会议的决定由各机构秘书处向新闻界发布。外交部长王正廷博士通常在周五上午接受中国记者的采访。结果，人们看到日本新闻机构在中国报纸上所占的版面稳步减少。本国多家重要的日资报纸已停刊。随着北方首都落入国民革命军手中，《顺天时报》和《华北标准报》（North China Standard）很快便从北平报纸名单中消失。1929年7月31日，联合通讯社正式接手，取代东方通讯社（Toho），成为日本外务省在华公认的官方机构。联合通讯社和《日本电报》在华的新政策似乎是将其工作集中于

pages.en:
JAPANESE---10.

THE GATHERING OF NEWS FROM VARIOUS CENTRES IN CHINA FOR
THE CONSUMPTION OF THEIR HOME PAPERS. THE WORK OF NEWS
DISTRIBUTION IN CHINA TAKES A RELATIVELY UNIMPORTANT
ROLE.

THE SAME THING, HOWEVER, CANNOT BE SAID ABOUT THE
JAPANESE PRESS IN THE THREE EASTERN PROVINCES AND THE
LEASED TERRITORY OF KWANTUNG, WHERE JAPAN HAS SPECIAL
INTERESTS. THE JAPANESE POPULATION IN THAT PART OF CHINA
TOTALS MORE THAN 200,000, THE CHINESE POPULATION THERE
BEING 694,806. THE JAPANESE-OWNED SOUTH MANCHURIA
RAILWAY RUNS FROM CHANGCHUN TO DAIREN, A DISTANCE OF
ABOUT 698.4 MILES. THE SHARE-CAPITAL OF THE RAILWAY NOW
REPRESENTS A TOTAL OF MORE THAN 400,000,000 YEN. THE
NET PROFIT OF THE RAILWAY FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 1929-1930
IS ESTIMATED TO TOTAL NEARLY 35,000,000 YEN.

AS CAN BE EXPECTED, THE SOUTH MANCHURIA RAILWAY
COMPANY PUBLISHES A DAILY NEWSPAPER IN DAIREN, THE
PRINCIPAL PORT OF NORTH CHINA. THE PAPER IN DAIREN,
MANSHU NIPPO, HAS A DAILY CIRCULATION OF 30,000 COPIES.
IT IS CLEARLY THE LARGEST AND MOST INFLUENTIAL JAPANESE
NEWSPAPER IN CHINA. THERE USED TO BE THREE JAPANESE
DAILIES IN DAIREN. THEY WERE: MANSHU NIPPO, SHIMPO RYOTO,
AND DAIREN SHIMBUN. THE SHIMPO RYOTO WAS OWNED BY PRIVATE
pages.zh:
日本方面——10.

从中国各地收集新闻，供其国内报纸使用。新闻分发在中国的工作相对处于次要地位。

然而，在日本拥有特殊利益的东三省和关东租借地，情况并非如此。该地区的日本人口总数超过20万，当地中国人口为694,806人。日资南满铁路从长春运行至大连，距离约为698.4英里。该铁路的股份资本目前总额超过4亿日元。预计1929-1930财政年度该铁路的净利润总额接近3,500万日元。

正如预期的那样，南满铁路公司在华北主要港口大连出版了一份日报。大连的《满洲日日新闻》（Manshu Nippo）日发行量为3万份。它显然是中国在最大且最具影响力的日文报纸。大连曾有三家日文日报，分别是：《满洲日日新闻》、《辽东新报》（Shimpo Ryoto）和《大连新闻》（Dairen Shimbun）。《辽东新报》由私人

pages.en:
JAPANESE---11.

INTERESTS AND THE ONE EDITORIAL POLICY IT HAD WAS TO
MAKE THE SOUTH MANCHURIA RAILWAY COMPANY UNCOMFORTABLE.
THE PAPER DID IT SO SUCCESSFULLY THAT THE RAILWAY
AUTHORITIES DECIDED TO BUY THE PAPER AT A HANDSOME
PRICE. THE FIGURE IS REPORTED TO BE FROM $200,000 TO
$300,000.

THE COMPANY THEN BEGAN THE TASK OF FINDING A PROPER

利益集团拥有，其唯一的编辑方针就是让南满铁路公司感到难堪。该报做得非常成功，以至于铁路当局决定以高价收购该报。据报道，收购金额在20万至30万美元之间。

随后，公司开始着手寻找合适的人选来经营合并后的日报《满洲□□□》。高柳将军被任命为新报纸的总经理。这位被选中的高管是田中首相的密友，并于1917年协约国干涉西伯利亚期间，被日本政府派往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）担任帝国情报局负责人。当时日本正注视着幅员辽阔、人口稀少且矿产丰富的东西伯利亚。高柳将军在符拉迪沃斯托克的工作表现出色，日本天皇特赐两枝御用香烟给他，以表彰他对皇室的宝贵服务。鉴于当时符拉迪沃斯托克盛行酒色之风，这位将军也是一位“美食家”，经常光顾妓院。在一时的欢愉中，他将御赐香烟送给了一位日本艺伎。此举引发了日本新闻界的强烈抗议，声势之大，使得田中将军发现有必要

FOREMOST AUTHORITIES ON RUSSIAN AFFAIRS IN JAPAN, AND HE
WAS SUBSEQUENTLY ENGAGED BY THE SOUTH MANCHURIA RAILWAY
AS ITS HIGH ADVISER.
WITH THE SEIYUKAI PARTY IN POWER, TAKAYANAGI, A
FRIEND OF PREMIER TANAKA, WAS LOGICALLY THE MAN FOR
THE MANSHU NIPPO POST, MR. CHIRO SATO WAS APPOINTED
CHIEF EDITOR OF THE PAPER. THE FALL OF THE TANAKA
GOVERNMENT AND THE COMING INTO POWER OF THE MINSEITO
PARTY CALLED FOR A REORGANIZATION OF THE SOUTH MANCHURIA
RAILWAY COMPANY. IN FEBRUARY, 1931, GENERAL TAKAYANAGI
RESIGNED. THE FORMER POLICY TO HAVE A PARTY MAN AT THE
HEAD OF THE MANSHU NIPPO WAS A SUBJECT OF ADVERSE
CRITICISM. FREQUENT CHANGES IN THE PERSONNEL OF THE
TOKYO GOVERNMENT GREATLY INCONVENIENCED THE PROGRESS
OF THE PAPER IN DAIREN. IT WAS FINALLY DECIDED TO PUT
AT THE HEAD OF THE PAPER AN INDEPENDENT JOURNALIST, A
MAN WHO KNEW THE PROFESSION AND HAD NO POLITICAL
AFFILIATIONS. MR. CHUJIRO MATSUYAMA, FORMER EDITOR OF
TOKYO ASAHI, WAS BROUGHT TO DAIREN TO EDIT THE PAPER.
WITH THE PURCHASE OF THE SHIMPO KYOTO BY THE MANSHU

将高柳免职。他是日本研究俄国事务的首要权威之一，随后被南满铁路聘为高级顾问。

随着政友会掌权，作为田中首相朋友的高柳自然是担任《满洲日日新闻》职位的合适人选。佐藤千代郎先生被任命为该报主编。田中内阁倒台和民政党上台执政，要求对南满铁路公司进行重组。1931年2月，高柳将军辞职。此前由政党人士掌管《满洲日日新闻》的政策受到了批评。东京政府人员的频繁变动给大连报纸的发展带来了极大不便。最终决定由一位独立的新闻工作者担任报纸负责人，此人懂行且无政治派系背景。前《东京朝日新闻》编辑松山忠次郎先生被带到大连主持该报编辑工作。随着《满洲日日新闻》收购《辽东新报》，大连有了容纳一份反对派报纸的空间。《大连新闻》是一份发行量小且几乎

NO FINANCIAL BACKING, LEAPED INTO PROMINENCE BY TAKING
THE PLACE OF SHINPO PYOTO AS A FAULT-FINDER OF THE SOUTH
MANCHURIA RAILWAY COMPANY.

ANOTHER JAPANESE-OWNED PAPER OF IMPORTANCE IN THE
THREE EASTERN PROVINCES IS A DAILY PUBLISHED IN CHINESE
IN LIAOLING (MUKDEN). MR. SHINYU NAGAJIMA, THE MAN WHO
FOUNDED THE FAMOUS SHUN TIEN SHIH PAO IN PEIPING IN 1901,
WAS THE FOUNDER OF THE SHEN CHIN SHIH PAO IN LIAOLING
IN 1906. IT HAS A DAILY CIRCULATION OF 14,000 COPIES.
IN 1925 A CORPORATION WAS FORMED AND MR. TORUSKI SAHARA,
A WELL-KNOWN JAPANESE JOURNALIST, WAS ELECTED PRESIDENT
OF THE NEW SHEN CHIN SHIH PAO CORPORATION.

THERE ARE THREE OTHER JAPANESE-OWNED NEWSPAPERS IN
LIAOLING. THE FENGTIEN HSINWEN WAS ORGANIZED IN 1917.
IT CLAIMS TO HAVE A DAILY CIRCULATION OF 9,000 COPIES.
THE MANAGING EDITOR OF THE PAPER IS MR. YOSHINO SATO.
THE OTHER TWO PAPERS HAVE COMPARATIVELY SMALLER CIRCULA-
TION. THE FENGTIEN NICHI NICHI WAS FORMERLY KNOWN AS
MAN LANG JIH PAO. THE REORGANIZATION OF THE PAPER TOOK
PLACE IN 1926 AND ITS PRESENT MANAGING EDITOR IS MR.
JIN IOTANI. THE FENGTIEN MAINICHI SHIMBUN WAS FOUNDED
IN 1920. THE FOUNDER OF THE PAPER, MR. MOTOKI MATSUMIA,
IS NOW DEAD.

没有财力支持的报纸，它通过取代《辽东新报》成为南满铁路公司的挑剔者而崭露头角。

东三省另一家重要的日资报纸是在辽阳（奉天/沈阳）出版的中文日报。1901年在北平创办著名《顺天时报》的新岛真雄先生，也是1906年在辽阳创办《盛京时报》的人。该报日发行量为1.4万份。1925年成立了一家股份公司，著名日本记者佐原虎之助先生当选为新成立的《盛京时报》股份公司总裁。

辽阳还有另外三家日资报纸。《奉天新闻》成立于1917年。声称日发行量为9,000份。该报经理是佐藤吉野先生。另外两家报纸的发行量相对较小。《奉天日日新闻》以前被称为《满浪日报》。该报于1926年重组，现任经理是大谷仁先生。《奉天每日新闻》成立于1920年。该报创始人松宫基树先生现已去世。

JAPANESE---14.

THERE ARE JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS IN TWO OTHER PRINCIPAL
PORTS OF THE SOUTH MANCHURIA RAILWAY, ANTUNG AND YINKOW.
THE PAPER IN ANTUNG IS ANTING HSIN PAO. IT WAS FOUNDED
IN 1906 AND HAS NOW A DAILY CIRCULATION OF 2,500 COPIES.
ITS MANAGING EDITOR IS ATSUSHI KAWAMATA. ASIDE FROM
HAVING A WIDE CIRCULATION IN ANTUNG, THE PAPER IS
ALSO READ BY A LARGE JAPANESE POPULATION LIVING IN
THE HSINGISHU DISTRICT OF KOREA. MANCHU HSIN PAO AT
YINKOW WAS FOUNDED IN 1908. THE PRESENT HEAD OF THE
PAPER IS MR. YOSHIKASU OGAWA.

IN RECENT YEARS TWO JAPANESE PAPERS APPEARED IN
HARBIN. THE HARBIN NICHI NICHI SHIMBUN MADE ITS FIRST
APPEARANCE IN THAT CITY IN 1922. THE PAPER, WHICH HAS
NOW A DAILY CIRCULATION OF 1,200 COPIES, WAS FOUNDED
BY MR. UJI KOTAMA. ITS MANAGING EDITOR IS MR. SHIRO
SATO. ABOUT A YEAR LATER MR. KOJIN OGARA FOUNDED THE
HARBIN JIHO WHICH NOW HAS A DAILY CIRCULATION OF ABOUT
600 COPIES.

THE JAPANESE PRESS IN PEIPING HAVE SEEN BETTER
DAYS. THE SHUN TIEN SHIH PAO PUBLISHED IN CHINESE,
FOR MANY YEARS WAS THE LEADING DAILY IN THE NORTHERN

HAGAJIMA WHO LATER ALSO FOUNDED THE SHEN CHING SHIH PAO

在南满铁路的另外两个主要港口安东和营口也有日文报纸。安东的报纸是《安东新报》。它成立于1906年，目前日发行量为2,500份。其经理是川俣笃氏。除了在安东拥有广泛的发行量外，该报还被居住在朝鲜兴义区的大量日本人口阅读。营口的《满洲新报》成立于1908年。该报现任负责人是小川义胜先生。

近年来，哈尔滨出现了两份日文报纸。《哈尔滨日日新闻》于1922年首次在该市出现。该报由儿玉宇治先生创办，目前日发行量为1,200份。其经理是佐藤史郎先生。大约一年后，小柄古人先生创办了《哈尔滨时报》（Harbin Jiho），目前日发行量约为600份。

北平的日文报纸曾有过辉煌的日子。中文版《顺天时报》多年来一直是北方首都的主要日报。该报由长岛真雄先生于1901年创办，他后来还创办了《盛京时报》

IN LIAOLING. ITS FEARLESS EXPOSURE OF POLITICAL
INTRIGUES THEN GOING ON IN THE PEKING GOVERNMENT AND
ITS EXCLUSIVE WAR NEWS BROUGHT SUCH POPULARITY TO THE
PAPER THAT IT WAS NEVER EQUALLED BY ANY OTHER JAPANESE
NEWSPAPER NOR ANY OF ITS NATIVE COMPETITORS IN THAT
CITY. ITS DAILY CIRCULATION REACHED A HIGH MARK OF
12,000 COPIES DURING THE TIME WHEN GENERAL YUAN SHIH-
KAI PLANNED TO MAKE HIMSELF THE EMPEROR OF CHINA. THE
PAPER EXPRESSED ITS VIGOROUS OPPOSITION TO THE PLOT
THROUGH ITS EDITORIAL COLUMNS AND THROUGH THE PUBLICA-
TION OF NEWS DESPATCHES UNFAVOURABLE TO THE CAUSE. THE
PAPER HAD SO MUCH INFLUENCE AT THE TIME THAT YUAN SHIH-
KAI'S SUPPORTERS WENT SO FAR AS TO GIVE THE PAPER
$30,000 FOR THE PRINTING OF ONE BOGUS COPY OF THE PAPER
IN WHICH THE PAPER ENDORSED THE PROPOSAL TO MAKE YUAN
THE EMPEROR! THIS BOGUS COPY OF THE PAPER WAS SHOWN
TO YUAN SHIH-KAI WHO WAS THUS CONVINCED THAT HIS
AMBITIOUS MOVE HAD THE SUPPORT OF THE WHOLE NATION.
THE NORTH CHINA STANDARD WAS ANOTHER JAPANESE ORGAN
IN PEIPING. THIS PAPER, PUBLISHED IN ENGLISH, WAS
STARTED TO AIR THE JAPANESE VIEWS ON DOINGS IN CHINA
AND TO FORCE, IF POSSIBLE, THE AMERICAN-OWNED PEKING

CATS AND DOGS. A CUT-THROAT COMPETITION BEGAN FOR

在辽阳。该报无畏地揭露当时北京政府内部正在进行的政治阴谋，并独家发布战争新闻，使其受欢迎程度在该市任何其他日本报纸或本地竞争对手中均无出其右。在袁世凯将军策划称帝期间，该报的日发行量高达12,000份。该报通过社论栏目以及刊登不利于其事业的新闻电讯，强烈反对这一阴谋。当时该报影响力巨大，以至于袁世凯的支持者竟出资30,000美元印制一份该报的伪造版，在其中该报表示支持拥戴袁世凯为皇帝的提议！这份伪造的报纸被展示给袁世凯看，从而使他相信其野心勃勃的举动得到了全国的支持。《华北标准报》（North China Standard）是北平的另一家日本机构。该报以英文出版，创办旨在宣扬日本对中国时事的观点，并试图（如果可能的话）迫使美资《北京导报》（Peking Leader）停业。这两家报纸势同水火，展开了激烈的

SUBSCRIPTIONS AND ADVERTISEMENTS. THE NORTH CHINA
STANDARD WITH ITS ANTI-CHINESE VIEWS SOON GAINED
IMMENSE POPULARITY IN THE SO-CALLED LEGATION QUARTER
AND AMONG THE FOREIGN "DIE-HARD" BUSINESS MEN. MR.
GROVER CLARK, EDITOR OF THE AMERICAN PAPER, AND MR.
GORMAN, EDITOR OF THE JAPANESE ORGAN, FILLED THEIR
RESPECTIVE FRONT PAGES WITH VIGOROUS EDITORIALS FOR
DAYS FOLLOWING THE NOTORIOUS TSINAN INCIDENT IN MAY,
1928. THE FORMER ARGUED THAT THE JAPANESE TROOPS HAD
NO BUSINESS TO GO TO SHANTUNG AND THE LATTER DID HIS
LEVEL BEST TO JUSTIFY THE JAPANESE BOMBARDMENT.
BOTH THE SHUN TIEN SHIH PAO AND THE NORTH CHINA
STANDARD DISAPPEARED FROM THE PEIPING NEWSPAPER
DIRECTORY SHORTLY AFTER THE COLLAPSE OF THE PEKING
GOVERNMENT. THEY HAD ENDLESS TROUBLES WITH THE LOCAL
KUOMINTANG AUTHORITIES. ONCE THE PAPERS WERE BOYCOTTED
BY CHINESE NEWS BOYS. THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A STRONG
CENTRAL GOVERNMENT AT NANKING MADE PEIPING PRACTICALLY
A DEAD CITY. THE OLD CAPITAL WAS HIT BY A SERIOUS
BUSINESS DEPRESSION. THE JAPANESE INTERESTS CONCERNED

PAPERS. THIS LEFT ONLY TWO VERY UNIMPORTANT JAPANESE
DAILIES IN PEIPING. ONE IS PEKING SHIMBUN ORGANIZED
IN 1923, WHICH HAS A DAILY CIRCULATION OF FROM 400 TO

订阅和广告争夺战。《华北标准报》因其反华观点，很快在所谓的使馆区以及外国“顽固派”商人中获得了极大的人气。美国报纸编辑格罗弗·克拉克（Grover Clark）先生和日本机构编辑戈尔曼（Gorman）先生，在1928年5月臭名昭著的济南惨案发生后的数日内，都在各自的头版刊登了措辞激烈的社论。前者论证日军无权进入山东，后者则竭尽全力为日本的炮击行为辩护。在北京政府垮台后不久，《顺天时报》和《华北标准报》都从北平报纸目录中消失了。它们与当地国民党当局有着无尽的麻烦。有一次，这些报纸遭到了中国报童的抵制。南京强势中央政府的建立，使得北平实际上成为了一座死城。旧都遭受了严重的商业萧条打击。相关的日本利益方决定停止出版这两份报纸。这使得北平只剩下两份非常不重要的日本日报。一份是1923年创办的《北京新闻》（Peking Shimbun），其日发行量为400至

500 COPIES. THE PAPER USED TO BE SUBSIDIZED BY THE
SOUTH MANCHURIA RAILWAY COMPANY. THIS SUBSIDY HAS
HOWEVER, BEEN DISCONTINUED SINCE THE REMOVAL OF THE
POLITICAL CENTRE FROM PEIPING TO NANKING. ITS FORMER
CHIEF EDITOR, MR. SATOMI, IS NOW IN NANKING ACTING AS
THE REPRESENTATIVE OF THE SOUTH MANCHURIA RAILWAY
COMPANY. HIS SUCCESSOR IS MR. D. SAKAMOTO. THE OTHER
PAPER IS IF IN CHINA WHICH WAS FOUNDED IN 1913 AND
WHICH NOW HAS A DAILY CIRCULATION OF ABOUT 20 COPIES.
ITS MANAGING EDITOR IS MR. MANICHI ONDO.

THE HISTORY OF THE JAPANESE PRESS IN SHANGHAI DATES
BACK TO THE TIME OF THE RUSSO-JAPANESE WAR. BY ALLYING
HERSELF WITH ENGLAND, IN 1902, WITH THE DECLARED OBJECT
OF PRESERVING AGAINST RUSSIA THE INTEGRITY OF CHINA
AND THE INDEPENDENCE OF KOREA, JAPAN CHOSE WAR WITH
RUSSIA. THE FORMAL DECLARATION OF WAR CAME ON FEBRUARY 9,
1905. IT WAS FELT AT THE TIME IN JAPAN THAT JAPAN MUST
HAVE SOME CHANNEL OF EXPRESSING ITS VIEWS FOR THE
CONSUMPTION OF EUROPEANS AND AMERICANS IN CHINA. MR.
TOFUSKI SAHARA, WHO HAD MANY FRIENDS IN FOREIGN CIRCLES,
BACKED BY POWERFUL FINANCIAL INTERESTS IN JAPAN
ACQUIRED A CONTROLLING INTEREST IN THE SHANGHAI MERCURY,
A BRITISH EVENING NEWSPAPER IN SHANGHAI. THIS PAPER
WAS PURCHASED IN 1931 BY THE SHANGHAI EVENING POST.

500份。该报曾由南满洲铁道株式会社资助。然而，自政治中心从北平迁至南京以来，这项资助已被取消。其前任主编里见（Satomi）先生现在南京担任南满洲铁道株式会社的代表。他的继任者是坂本（D. Sakamoto）先生。另一份报纸是1913年创办的《在华日报》（If in China），目前的日发行量约为20份。其主编是大野万ichi（Manichi Ondo）先生。

上海日本报业的历史可追溯至日俄战争时期。日本于1902年与英国结盟，宣称目的是维护中国领土完整和朝鲜独立以对抗俄国，从而选择了与俄国开战。正式宣战发生在1905年2月9日。当时日本方面认为，日本必须拥有某种渠道，向在中国的欧洲人和美国人表达其观点。佐原藤辅（Tofuski Sahara）先生在外国圈子中朋友众多，并在日本强大金融势力的支持下，收购了上海一家英文晚报《上海信使报》（Shanghai Mercury）的控股权。该报于1931年被《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）收购。

pages.en:
JAPANESE---18.

THE OLDEST JAPANESE DAILY IN SHANGHAI, SHANGHAI
NIPPO, WAS FOUNDED IN 1904 BY MR. SABURO IDE WHO WAS
TWICE ELECTED MEMBER OF THE JAPANESE DIET AND WHO
LIVED IN CHINA FOR MORE THAN FORTY-THREE YEARS. THIS
PAPER WAS PURCHASED BY MR. H. HATA IN DECEMBER, 1929.
MR. HATA WAS A GRADUATE OF THE FAMOUS JAPANESE TUNG WEN
ACADEMY IN SHANGHAI. HE WAS ONCE CONNECTED WITH THE
EDITORIAL STAFF OF THE SHUN TIEN SHIH PAO AT PEIPING
AND FOUNDED THE ORIGINAL TOHO NEWS AGENCY IN 1914.
FOLLOWING THE REORGANIZATION OF TOHO, MR. HATA WAS
APPOINTED SHANGHAI MANAGER OF THIS POWERFUL NEWS AGENCY.
WHEN TOHO WAS TAKEN OVER BY RINGO ON JULY 31, 1929,
MR. HATA RESIGNED AND DEVOTED HIS ENTIRE TIME TO SHANGHAI
NIPPO. MR. SABURO IDE ORIGINALLY DEMANDED $100,000 FOR
HIS PAPER, BUT THE PRICE WAS FINALLY FIXED AT $45,000.
THE PAPER HAS A DAILY CIRCULATION OF 3,500 COPIES. THIS
FIGURE IS ALREADY REMARKABLE CONSIDERING THE FACT THAT
THERE ARE ONLY 30,000 JAPANESE NATIONALS IN THAT PORT.

THERE ARE TWO OTHER JAPANESE DAILIES IN SHANGHAI. THE
SHANGHAI MAINICHI WAS FOUNDED IN 1918. THE PRESIDENT OF
THE PAPER IS MR. FUKUMACHI SAKUJIRO. MR. KANDO MIYAJI
IS THE PRESIDENT OF THE OTHER PAPER, SHANGHAI NICHI
NICHI, WHICH WAS FOUNDED IN 1914. WHILE THE JAPANESE
NEWSPAPERS AT SHANGHAI DEPENDED MAINLY ON LOCAL SUPPORT,
pages.zh:
日本——18.

上海最古老的日文日报《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）由井手三郎（Saburo Ide）先生于1904年创办，他曾两次当选为日本国会议员，并在中国生活了四十三年之久。该报于1929年12月被畑（H. Hata）先生收购。畑先生毕业于上海著名的日本同文书院。他曾任北平《顺天时报》编辑部成员，并于1914年创立了最初的东方通讯社（Toho News Agency）。在东方通讯社重组后，畑先生被任命为该强大新闻机构的上海经理。当东方通讯社于1929年7月31日被联合通讯社（Ringo）接管时，畑先生辞职，将全部精力投入到《上海日报》的工作中。井手三郎先生最初为其报纸索要100,000美元，但最终价格定为45,000美元。该报日发行量为3,500份。考虑到该港口仅有30,000名日本国民，这一数字已属可观。

上海还有另外两家日文日报。《上海每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi）创办于1918年。该报社长是福町作次郎（Fukumachi Sakujiro）先生。另一份报纸《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nichi Nichi）创办于1914年，其社长是神宫寺（Kando Miyaji）先生。虽然上海的日本报纸主要依赖本地支持，

THERE IS A GROWING TENDENCY OF THESE PAPERS SPECIALIZING
IN COMMERCIAL NEWS. THE IDEA IS TO INCREASE THEIR
CIRCULATION IN JAPAN. THEY HAVE NO SPECIAL STAFF
CORRESPONDENTS AT VARIOUS PLACES IN CHINA. THE JAPANESE
NEWS AGENCIES, REIGO AND NIPPON DENPO, SUPPLY THEM WITH
POLITICAL AND COMMERCIAL NEW . IT IS BELIEVED THAT IF
MORE SPACE IS DEVOTED TO REVIEWS OF COMMERCIAL PROBLEMS
IN CHINA, THE PAPERS WILL PROVE TO BE VERY ATTRACTIVE TO
THE JAPANESE BUSINESS MEN IN NAGASAKI, OSAKA AND OTHER
IMPORTANT PORTS WHERE THEY PAY GREAT ATTENTION TO
COMMERCIAL POSSIBILITIES IN THIS COUNTRY.

WITH A JAPANESE POPULATION OF ONLY 2,000 AT HANKOW,
A JAPANESE DAILY THERE CANNOT BE EXPECTED TO HAVE VERY
LARGE CIRCULATION. THE HANKOW NIPPO WAS FOUNDED BACK
IN THE DAYS OF THE MANCHU DYNASTY, 1907. IT HAD A
CIRCULATION OF 1,000 COPIES. NOT ONLY THE PAPER WAS
READ AT HANKOW, IT ALSO HAD SUBSCRIBERS IN CHANGSHA,
HUNAN; CHUNGKING, SZECHUEN; ICHANG, HUPEH; AND OTHER
PLACES UP RIVER. THE MANAGING EDITOR OF THE PAPER, MR.
KOSHIJIRO OKA, DIED TWO YEARS AGO, AND THE PAPER DIS-
APPEARED WITH HIM.

NOW THERE IS ONLY ONE JAPANESE DAILY IN HANKOW, HANKOW
NICHI NICHI SHIMBUN. IT WAS FOUNDED IN 1918. THE MANAGING
EDITOR OF THE PAPER IS MR. GORO UTZNOMIA, AND ITS DAILY

但这些报纸越来越倾向于专门报道商业新闻。其目的是增加在日本国内的发行量。它们在中国各地没有专门的驻外记者。日本新闻机构“联合”（Reigo，音译，应指后来的同盟通信社前身之一或相关机构）和“日本电报”（Nippon Denpo，音译）向它们提供政治和商业新闻。人们认为，如果 devote 更多版面评论中国的商业问题，这些报纸将对长崎、大阪以及其他重要港口的日本商人极具吸引力，因为这些地方的商人非常关注在这个国家的商业机会。

汉口只有2,000名日本人口，因此那里的日文日报不可能有很大的发行量。《汉口日报》（Hankow Nippo）创办于清朝末年的1907年。其发行量为1,000份。该报不仅在汉口被阅读，在湖南长沙、四川重庆、湖北宜昌以及其他沿江地区也有订阅者。该报主编冈浩次郎（Koshijiro Oka）先生两年前去世，该报也随他一同消失。

现在汉口只有一份日文日报，《汉口日日新闻》（Hankow Nichi Nichi Shimbun）。它创办于1918年。该报主编是宇都宫五郎（Goro Utznomia，原文拼写可能有误，通常为Utsunomiya）先生，其日

pages.en:
JAPANESE---20.

CIRCULATION RANGES FROM 400 TO 1,000 COPIES.

THERE ARE TWO DISTINCT GROUPS AMONG THE JAPANESE
NATIONALS IN TIENTSIN. These are ENTIRELY LOCAL IN
CHARACTER AND have NO RELATIONSHIP WITH THE POLITICAL
ISSUES IN JAPAN. ONE GROUP CONSISTS OF PERSONS WHO HAVE
THEIR OWN BUSINESS INTERESTS IN TIENTSIN, WHEREAS THE
MEMBERS OF THE OPPOSING GROUP ARE PERSONS WHO HAVE BEEN
SENT TO TIENTSIN FROM JAPAN TO REPRESENT SOME FIRMS BACK
HOME. THE LOGICAL OUTCOME OF THIS IS THAT THERE ARE
TWO JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS IN TIENTSIN. THE KEISHIN NICHI
NICHI WAS FOUNDED IN 1918 AND HAS A DAILY CIRCULATION
OF 1,200 COPIES. ITS MANAGING EDITOR IS MR. TERUDA
NOIKAWA. THERE USED TO BE TWO JAPANESE DAILIES IN
TIENTSIN KNOWN AS HOKUSHIN JIHO AND KITASHIN NICHIICHI.
IN 1910, THESE TWO DAILIES WERE COMBINED TO FORM THE
TIENTSIN NIPPO. THE FORMER PRESIDENT OF THE PAPER, MR.
HIROSHI NISHIMURA, DIED TWO YEARS AGO, AND MR. KISHI
CHINDO SUCCEEDED HIM.

THE GREAT WAR OF 1914 GAVE JAPAN AN OPPORTUNITY TO
TIGHTEN ITS HOLD ON SHANTUNG. AS THE ALLY OF ENGLAND,
JAPAN ON AUGUST 15, 1914, GAVE "ADVICE" TO GERMANY TO
WITHDRAW ALL GERMAN WARSHIPS FROM THE FAR EAST AND TO
DELIVER THE KIAOCHOW BAY LEASED TERRITORY TO JAPAN.
RECEIVING NO REPLY, JAPAN DECLARED WAR ON GERMANY ON

发行量在400至1,000份之间。

天津的日本国民中有两个截然不同的群体。这些群体完全具有地方性质，与日本国内的政治议题无关。一个群体由在天津拥有自身商业利益的人士组成，而对立群体的成员则是从日本被派往天津代表国内某些公司的人员。由此产生的自然结果是，天津有两家日本报纸。《庆星日日新闻》（Keishin Nichi Nichi，音译）创办于1918年，日发行量为1,200份。其主编是野川照田（Teruda Noikawa，音译）先生。天津曾经有两家名为《北辰时报》（Hokushin Jiho，音译）和《北新日日》（Kitashin Nichiichi，音译）的日文日报。1910年，这两家日报合并成立了《天津日报》（Tientsin Nippo）。该报前社长西村博（Hiroshi Nishimura）先生两年前去世，岸镇东（Kishi Chindo，音译）先生继任。

1914年的世界大战给了日本加紧控制山东的机会。作为英国的盟友，日本于1914年8月15日向德国提出“建议”，要求德国将所有德国军舰撤出远东，并将胶州湾租借地移交给日本。由于未得到答复，日本于

pages.en:

AUGUST 23 AND PROCEEDED TO CAPTURE THE GERMAN TERRITORY.
SHORTLY AFTER THE OCCUPATION OF TSINGTAO BY JAPANESE
FORCES, THE TSINGTAO SHIMPO CAME INTO EXISTENCE. THE
FOUNDER OF THE PAPER WAS MR. TAMANA KITO. ITS PRESENT
MANAGING EDITOR IS MR. CHETSEWO KOTANI. THE DAILY
CIRCULATION OF THE SHIMPO IS ABOUT 2,000 COPIES. IN
TSINAN, THE SHANTUNG JIHO WAS FOUNDED IN 1919 BY MR.
ITARO OKA. IT NOW HAS A BRANCH OFFICE IN TSINGTAO AND
PUTS OUT A SPECIAL DAILY TSINGTAO EDITION OF ABOUT TWO
PAGES.
ONE OF THE OLDEST EXISTING JAPANESE DAILIES IN CHINA
IS THE MIN PAO, PUBLISHED IN FOOCHOW, FUKIEN PROVINCE.
THE FOUNDER OF THE PAPER, MR. HYO HAYADA, IS NOW DEAD.
THE PAPER WAS FOUNDED IN 1897. THE REGULAR EDITION OF
THE PAPER IS IN CHINESE, BUT IT CARRIES A TWO-PAGE
JAPANESE SUPPLEMENT. DURING THE PAST FEW YEARS, THE
LOCAL AUTHORITIES AT FOOCHOW WERE HIGHLY DISPLEASED
WITH THE ANTI-CHINESE ATTITUDE OF THE PAPER.
THERE IS ONE JAPANESE DAILY IN CANTON, CANTON NIPPO.
ITS CIRCULATION IS SMALL AND OCCUPIES A VERY UNIMPORTANT
PLACE IN THE AFFAIRS OF THAT PORT.
PUBLISHERS OF JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS IN THIS COUNTRY
ARE HAVING SERIOUS APPREHENSIONS AS TO THE FUTURE OF
THEIR ENTERPRISES IN CHINA. IN THE PAST, THEY RECEIVED

8月23日对德宣战，并着手占领德国领土。日军占领青岛后不久，《青岛新报》（Tsingtao Shimpo）应运而生。该报创始人是喜多玉名（Tamana Kito，音译）先生。现任主编是小谷节夫（Chetsewo Kotani，音译，可能为Setsuo Kotani）先生。《新报》的日发行量约为2,000份。在济南，《山东时报》（Shantung Jiho，音译）由冈伊太郎（Itaro Oka）先生于1919年创办。该报目前在青岛设有分社，并出版一份约两页的青岛特别日刊。

中国现存最古老的日文日报之一是福建省福州出版的《闽报》（Min Pao）。该报创始人早田兵卫（Hyo Hayada，音译）先生现已去世。该报创办于1897年。该报常规版为中文，但附有两页的日文增刊。在过去几年中，福州地方当局对该报的反华态度极为不满。

广州有一家日文日报，《广州日报》（Canton Nippo）。其发行量很小，在该港事务中占据非常不重要的地位。

在华日本报纸出版商对其企业在中国的未来感到严重担忧。过去，他们收到

pages.en:
JAPANESE---22.

SUPPORT FROM THE POWERFUL SOUTH MANCHURIA RAILWAY COMPANY
AND OTHER BIG JAPANESE BUSINESS FIRMS IN CHINA LIKE the
YOKOHAMA SPECIE BANK, MITSUI BUSSAN KAISHA, NISSHIN
KISEN KABUSHIKI KAISHA, ETC. WHEN SHANGHAI NIPPON was
FIRST ORGANIZED, IT RECEIVED FROM $20,000 TO $30,000
FROM THE JAPANESE STOCK EXCHANGE AT SHANGHAI. SINCE THE
SERIOUS ECONOMIC DEPRESSION IN JAPAN IN 1930 AND THE
DEMORALIZATION OF CHINA'S IMPORT TRADE IN 1930 DUE TO
THE FALL OF SILVER CURRENCY TO UNPRECEDENTED LOW LEVELS,
THE VARIOUS FIRMS FOUND IT NECESSARY TO CUT DOWN THEIR
ADVERTISING BUDGETS. MOST OF THE JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS IN
CHINA WILL BE UNABLE TO GO ON UNLESS BUSINESS CONDITIONS
IN JAPAN AND IN THIS COUNTRY BEGIN TO SHOW SIGNS OF
IMPROVEMENT.

THE HISTORY OF JAPANESE NEWS AGENCIES IN CHINA DATES
BACK TO THE TIME OF THE GREAT WAR. MR. GENICHIRO TATAI,
A PROMINENT JOURNALIST IN JAPAN, WENT TO THE VERSAILLES
CONFERENCE AND WAS GREATLY IMPRESSED BY THE WORK OF
REUTERS OF ENGLAND AND THE ASSOCIATED PRESS OF AMERICA.
WHEN HE RETURNED TO TOKYO HE DISCUSSED THE MATTER WITH
THE JAPANESE FOREIGN OFFICE. IT WAS MR. TATAI'S IDEA
THAT JAPAN'S RELATIONS WITH CHINA WERE OF VITAL IMPOR-
TANCE TO THE IMPERIAL GOVERNMENT, AND IN ORDER TO AIR
TOKYO'S VIEWS IN CHINA, IT WAS NECESSARY TO ESTABLISH A
pages.zh:
日本——22.

来自强大的南满洲铁道株式会社以及横滨正金银行、三井物产株式会社、日清汽船株式会社等在华大型日本商业公司的支持。当《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippon）最初组建时，它从上海日本股票交易所获得了20,000至30,000美元的资金。自从1930年日本出现严重经济衰退，以及1930年因银价跌至前所未有的低位导致中国进口贸易萎靡不振以来，各公司发现有必要削减广告预算。除非日本和中国的商业状况开始显示出改善迹象，否则大多数在华日本报纸将无法维持下去。

日本在华新闻机构的历史可追溯至世界大战时期。日本著名记者田代源一郎（Genichiro Tatai，音译，可能为Tadai或类似发音）先生前往凡尔赛会议，并对英国路透社和美国美联社的工作印象深刻。当他回到东京后，与日本外务省讨论了此事。田代先生认为，日本与中国的关系对帝国政府至关重要，为了在中国宣扬东京的观点，有必要为此目的建立一个

pages.en:
JAPANESE---23.

SPECIAL NEWS AGENCY IN CHINA FOR THAT PURPOSE. HIS
SUGGESTIONS MET THE APPROVAL OF THE GOVERNMENT LEADERS.
IN 1920 MR. TATAI WAS ASKED TO COME TO CHINA TO ORGANIZE
THE PROPOSED NEWS AGENCY.
    THERE WAS A JAP NESE NEWS AGENCY AT THAT TIME IN
SHANGHAI WHICH WAS FOUNDED BY MR. H. HATA IN 1914. IT
HAD BRANCH OFFICES AT PEIPING, CANTON, HANKOW AND LIAO-
LING (MUKDEN). AFTER A SERIES OF CONFERENCES BETWEEN
MR. TATAI AND MR. HATA, A REORGANIZATION OF THE OLD
AGENCY WAS AFFECTED AND THE NEW TOHO NEWS AGENCY CAME
INTO EXISTENCE. BEING THE OFFICIAL ORGAN IN CHINA OF THE
JAPANESE FOREIGN OFFICE, IT RECEIVED A REGULAR SUBSIDY
FROM TOKYO. ITS NEWS SERVICES WERE SOLD TO THE NEWSPAPERS
IN JAPAN AT 400 YEN A MONTH. THE AMOUNT OF SUBSIDY FROM
THE JAPANESE FOREIGN OFFICE, HOWEVER, LATER STEADILY
DECREASED UNTIL THE CONTINUANCE OF THE ENTERPRISE WAS
FOUND TO BE ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE. IN 1926, TOHO COMBINED
WITH KOKUSAI AND FORMED ANOTHER NEW AGENCY WHICH IS
KNOWN THROUGHOUT THE WORLD AS RENGO. THE FULL TITLE OF
THE ORGANIZATION IS NIPPON SHIMBUN RENGO-SHA. BY REASON
OF ITS CONTRACT WITH REUTERS, RENGO WAS UNABLE TO DIS-
TRIBUTE NEWS IN CHINA, SO THE NEW ORGANIZATION CONTINUED
TO ISSUE ITS NEWS SERVICES IN CHINA UNDER THE NAME OF
TOHO. THE REVISION OF THE CONTRACT BETWEEN REUTERS AND

专门的新闻机构。他的建议得到了政府领导人的批准。1920年，田代先生受邀来华组建拟议中的新闻机构。

当时上海有一家日本新闻机构，由畑（H. Hata）先生于1914年创办。它在北平、广州、汉口和辽阳（沈阳）设有分社。经过田代先生和畑先生的一系列会议，旧机构进行了重组，新的东方通讯社（Toho News Agency）由此成立。作为日本外务省在华的官方机构，它定期接受来自东京的资助。其新闻服务以每月400日元的价格出售给日本的报纸。然而，来自日本外务省的资助金额后来稳步减少，直到该企业的继续经营几乎变得不可能。1926年，东方通讯社与国际通讯社（Kokusai）合并，组成了另一家新的机构，即闻名世界的联合通讯社（Rengo）。该组织的全称是日本新闻联合社（Nippon Shimbun Rengo-sha）。由于与路透社的合同限制，联合通讯社无法在中国分发新闻，因此新组织继续以“东方”（Toho）的名义在中国发布其新闻服务。路透社与

pages.en:
JAPANESE---24.

RENGO IN 1929 MADE THE USE OF TOHO'S NAME IN CHINA UN-
NECESSARY, AND ON JULY 31, 1929, THE NAME OF TOHO WAS
DEFINITELY DROPPED AND RENGO OFFICIALLY MADE ITS FIRST
APPEARANCE IN CHINA.

RENGO, OR ITS PARENT ORGANIZATION KOKUSAI, WAS THE
FIRST JAPANESE NEWS AGENCY TO HANDLE INTERNATIONAL
PUBLICITY.

MORE THAN THIRTY YEARS AGO, MR. JAMES RUSSELL KENNEDY
WHO WAS AT THE TIME REUTERS' TOKYO CORRESPONDENT
SUGGESTED TO THE JAPANESE LEADERS THE IDEA OF FORMING A
NATIONAL NEWS AGENCY IN JAPAN FOR THE HANDLING OF INTERNA-
TIONAL PUBLICITY. FOR A NUMBER OF YEARS, HOWEVER, NO
MATERIAL PROGRESS WAS MADE. THE PROPOSAL LATER RECEIVED
THE ATTENTION OF PRINCE ITO, PRINCE KATSURA AND COUNT
SHIBUZAWA. PRINCE ITO WAS THE MOST INFLUENTIAL POLITICAL
LEADER OF HIS TIME AND COUNT SHIBUZAWA HAD GREAT INFLUENCE
IN JAPAN'S FINANCIAL CIRCLES. IN 1913, DEFINITE PROGRESS
WAS MADE AND A YEAR LATER KOKUSAI WAS ORGANIZED. IN
THE EARLY YEARS JAPAN HAD NO EXPERIENCED NEWSPAPER MEN
WHO COULD HANDLE EFFICIENTLY SUCH A NEWS AGENCY, SO MR.
KENNEDY WAS MADE ITS MANAGING EDITOR. HISTORY HAS SHOWN
THAT APT PUPILS THE JAPANESE HAVE PROVED IN THIS AND
OTHER ENTERPRISES. IN 1872, A NUMBER OF AUSTRIAN OFFICERS
WERE UNDER ENGAGEMENT TO THE GOVERNMENT OF JAPAN TO TRAIN
pages.zh:
日本---24.

联合通讯社（Rengo）于1929年成立，使得在中国使用东邦通讯社（Toho）之名变得不再必要。1929年7月31日，东邦通讯社之名被正式弃用，联合通讯社首次正式亮相中国。

联合通讯社，或其母组织国际通讯社（Kokusai），是第一家处理国际宣传事务的日本新闻机构。

三十多年前，时任路透社东京记者的詹姆斯·拉塞尔·肯尼迪（James Russell Kennedy）先生向日本领导人提出了在日本组建一家国家新闻机构以处理国际宣传的想法。然而，在随后的数年里，此事并未取得实质性进展。该提议后来引起了伊藤博文亲王、桂太郎亲王和涩泽荣一伯爵的关注。伊藤亲王是当时最具影响力的政治领袖，而涩泽伯爵在日本金融界拥有巨大影响力。1913年，此事取得了明确进展，一年后，国际通讯社正式成立。在早期，日本缺乏能够高效运营此类新闻机构的经验丰富的报人，因此肯尼迪先生被任命为其主编。历史表明，日本人在这项及其他事业中证明了自己是聪颖的学生。1872年，一批奥地利军官受聘于日本政府，负责训练

pages.en:
JAPANESE---25.

THEIR CITIZENS IN THE ART OF WARFARE, A TASK WHICH THEY
SO SUCCESSFULLY CARRIED OUT THAT, WITHIN A VERY BRIEF
TIME, THEIR SERVICES WERE ENTIRELY DISPENSED WITH. THE
ORGANIZATION OF THE JAPANESE NAVY WAS LARGELY ENTRUSTED
TO BRITISH OFFICERS, BUT THEIR SERVICES WERE ALSO FOUND
TO BE NO LONGER NECESSARY AFTER A FEW YEARS. AS CAN BE
EXPECTED, THE MANAGEMENT OF KOKUSAI SOON PASSED INTO
THE HANDS OF ABLE NATIVE JOURNALISTS. THE AGENCY HAD NO
SPECIAL BUREAUX OF ITS OWN IN FOREIGN COUNTRIES. A
CONTRACT WAS CONCLUDED BETWEEN KOKUSAI AND REUTERS WHERE-
BY REUTERS NEWS DESPATCHES FROM ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD
WOULD BE DISTRIBUTED IN JAPAN THROUGH KOKUSAI.

IN 1926 KOKUSAI COMBINED WITH TOPO, AND THE OFF SPRING
OF THIS COMBINATION WAS RENGO WHICH WAS ORGANIZED MORE
OR LESS AFTER THE MODEL OF THE ASSOCIATED PRESS OF
AMERICA, BEING A COMBINATION OF A GROUP OF LARGE NEWS-
PAPERS IN JAPAN. THIS GROUP INCLUDES SUCH PAPERS LIKE
HOCHI SHIMBUN, TOKYO NICHI NICHI, TOKYO ASAHI, CHUGAI
SHOGYO SHIMPO, OSAKA MAINICHI, OSAKA ASAHI, JIJI, OTARU
SHIMBUN, KOBE YUFIN, KYOTO SHIMBUN, SANNO SHIMPO, KINSHIN
NIPPO, AND SHIKOKU NICHI. THE PRESIDENT OF THE ORGANIZA-
TION IS MR. UYKISHI IWANAGA. EACH MEMBER PAPER PAYS
2,000 YEN MONTHLY FOR THE RENGO NEWS SERVICES. THE
COMMERCIAL NEWS SERVICE DEPARTMENT OF THE AGENCY AT OSAKA
pages.zh:

其公民掌握战争艺术。他们极其成功地完成了这项任务，以至于在很短的时间内，他们的服务就不再被需要了。日本海军的组织工作主要委托给英国军官，但几年后，人们也发现不再需要他们的服务了。不出所料，国际通讯社的管理权很快便移交给了能干的日本本土记者。该机构在外国没有设立专门的分局。国际通讯社与路透社签订了一项合同，规定路透社来自世界各地的新闻电稿将通过国际通讯社在日本分发。

1926年，国际通讯社与东邦通讯社合并，其产物便是联合通讯社。联合通讯社大致仿照美国美联社的模式组建，由日本一群大型报纸联合而成。该集团包括《报知新闻》、《东京日日新闻》、《东京朝日新闻》、《中外商业新报》、《大阪每日新闻》、《大阪朝日新闻》、《时事新报》、《小樽新闻》、《神户又新日报》、《京都新闻》、《山阴新报》、《金泽日报》和《四国日报》等报刊。该组织的总裁是岩永宇吉氏（Uykishi Iwanaga，音译）。每家成员报社每月支付2,000日元以获取联合通讯社的新闻服务。该机构位于大阪的商业新闻服务部

HAS AN ANNUAL INCOME OF ABOUT 500,000 YEN. THE REVENUES
OF THE ORGANIZATION ARE NOT BELIEVED TO BE SUFFICIENT TO

1931年2月，联合通讯社上海分局向东京发送了150多封电文，约4,000字。上海每天向其日本总社发送约五封电文。这一数字包括了其南京分局发送的部分电文。南京记者经常通过长途电话将电文发往上海，再由上海转发至日本。上海与日本之间新闻电报的电报费率约为

SHANGHAI AND JAPAN IS ABOUT 8 CENTS GOLD PER WORD,
AND 30 CENTS GOLD PER WORD FOR ORDINARY MESSAGES.
THE SHANGHAI BUREAU OF RENGO IS ITS LARGEST BUREAU
IN CHINA. IT COSTS THE ORGANIZATION FOR $4,000 TO
$5,000 TO MAINTAIN ITS SHANGHAI OFFICE WHILE THE
EXPENSES AT THE OTHER BUREAUX TOTAL ABOUT $1,500 EACH
PER MONTH. THE REGULAR RENGO NEWS SERVICES CAN BE
HAD AT SHANGHAI FOR $70 A MONTH, AND ITS CHINESE
SERVICE FOR $20.

THERE ARE ONLY TWO OUTSTANDING JAPANESE NEWS
AGENCIES IN CHINA. ONE IS RENGO AND THE OTHER IS NIPPON
DENPO. THE LATTER'S FULL TITLE IS NIPPON DENPO TSUSHIN,
OR TELEGRAPH NEWS AGENCY. THE ORGANIZATION WAS FOUNDED
IN 1900 BY MR. HOSHIRO MITSUNAGA. TO BE EXACT, THE
ORGANIZATION DID NOT START OUT AS A NEWS AGENCY. FOR
SOMETIME, IT ACTED AS AN ADVERTISING AGENCY. LATER ON
IT ENTERED THE NEWS AGENCY FIELD. UNDER THE LEADERSHIP
OF MR. MITSUNAGA, A MAN OF GREAT VISION AND ENERGY,
THE ORGANIZATION GREW. IT COLLECTS DOMESTIC NEWS
THROUGH A COUNTRY-WIDE SERVICE WITH CORRESPONDENTS IN
ALL LEADING TOWNS. CONNECTIONS HAVE ALSO BEEN ESTABLISHED
WITH FOREIGN NEWS AGENCIES, LIKE THE UNITED PRESS OF
AMERICA, AND IT NOW HANDLES INTERNATIONAL CABLE REPORTS.

每字8美分金币，普通电文为每字30美分金币。联合通讯社上海分局是其在中国最大的分局。维持其上海办事处的费用为4,000至5,000美元，而其他各分局的费用每月总计约为1,500美元。在上海，每月支付70美元即可订阅联合通讯社的常规新闻服务，其中文服务则为20美元。

在中国只有两家杰出的日本新闻机构。一家是联合通讯社，另一家是日本电报通讯社（Nippon Denpo）。后者的全称是日本电报通信社（Nippon Denpo Tsushin），即电报新闻社。该组织由光长博四郎先生（Hoshiro Mitsunaga，音译）于1900年创立。确切地说，该组织起初并非作为新闻机构起步。在一段时间内，它充当广告代理机构。后来才进入新闻机构领域。在富有远见和活力的光长先生领导下，该组织得以发展壮大。它通过遍布全国的服务网络收集国内新闻，在所有主要城镇均设有通讯员。它还与外国新闻机构建立了联系，如美国合众社（United Press），目前处理国际电缆报道。

JAPANESE---29.

THE FIRST APPEARANCE OF NIPPON DENPO IN CHINA WAS
IN 1919. WITHIN A FEW YEARS, BRANCH OFFICES WERE
ESTABLISHED IN DAIREN, LIAOLING (LUKDEN), PEIPING,
HANKOW, TIENTSIN, AND SHANGHAI. IT HAS SPECIAL STAFF
CORRESPONDENTS IN NANKING, TSINGTAO, CANTON, TSINAN,
CHUNKING, AND HARBIN. THE REGULAR NEWS AND COMMERCIAL
SERVICES OF NIPPON DENPO CAN BE HAD AT DAIREN, LIAO-
LING, PEIPING, HANKOW, TIENTSIN AND SHANGHAI. THERE IS
A REPORT RECENTLY THAT IT PLANS TO ESTABLISH TWO MORE
BRANCH OFFICES IN CHINA AND TO DISTRIBUTE ITS NEWS
SERVICE IN NANKING. IF THE LAST MENTIONED PROJECT IS
SUCCESSFUL, NIPPON DENPO WILL BE THE FIRST FOREIGN
NEWS AGENCY TO DISTRIBUTE ITS NEWS SERVICE IN THE
CHINESE CAPITAL. ALTHOUGH REUTERS, HAVAS, AND UNITED
PRESS OF AMERICA ALSO HAVE REPRESENTATIVES IN NANKING,
THEY DO NOT DISTRIBUTE THEIR NEWS SERVICES THERE.
SOMETIME AGO, THE CENTRAL DAILY NEWS, OFFICIAL ORGAN
OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT, MADE OVERTURES TO REUTERS
ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF OBTAINING REUTERS NEWS SERVICE
IN NANKING, AND ABOUT A YEAR AGO, THE CENTRAL NEWS
AGENCY, OFFICIAL ORGAN OF THE CENTRAL KUOMINTANG, ALSO
NEGOTIATED FOR THE RIGHT TO DISTRIBUTE REUTERS NEWS
IN THE CAPITAL. BOTH THESE PROJECTS WERE, HOWEVER,
UNSUCCESSFUL,

日本电报通讯社首次出现在中国是在1919年。几年内，它在大连、辽阳（此处原文为Lukden，疑为Mukden之误）、北平、汉口、天津和上海设立了分支机构。它在南京、青岛、广州、济南、重庆和哈尔滨派驻有专职记者。在大连、辽阳、北平、汉口、天津和上海可以获取日本电报通讯社的常规新闻和商业服务。近期有报告称，该社计划在中国再增设两个分支机构，并在南京分发其新闻服务。如果上述计划成功，日本电报通讯社将成为第一家在中国首都分发其新闻服务的外国新闻机构。尽管路透社、哈瓦斯社和美国合众社也在南京设有代表，但它们并不在那里分发新闻服务。不久前，国民政府官方机关报《中央日报》曾就路透社在南京提供新闻服务的可能性向路透社接洽；大约一年前，中国国民党中央官方机关中央通讯社也就在首都分发路透社新闻的权利进行了谈判。然而，这两项计划均未成功，

JAPANESE---30.

A COMMERCIAL NEWS AGENCY HAS TO SELL ITS NEWS IN
ORDER TO EXIST. ASIDE FROM RECEIVING A POWERFUL
FINANCIAL BACKING FROM THE LEADING NEWSPAPERS IN JAPAN,
DENDO BEING THE GOVERNMENT ORGAN, CAN ALWAYS COUNT
ON THE GOVERNMENT FOR SUPPORT IF SUCH IS NECESSARY.
THE POSITION OF NIPPON DENPO IS DIFFERENT. A "SCOOP"
BY ITS COMPETING NEWS AGENCIES [illegible] BE DISASTROUS. THE
NATURAL OUTCOME OF THIS IS THAT NIPPON DENPO IS APT

THIS POLICY IS MISINTERPRETED IN CHINESE OFFICIAL
CIRCLES. THIS AGENCY IS CHARACTERIZED IN CHINA AS BEING
ANTI-NANKING.

MANY NEWSPAPERS AND NEWS AGENCIES IN EUROPE AND AMERICA
HAVE DONE THE SAME THING. THE NEW YORK WORLD IN ITS

DAILY NEWS, EVENING GRAPHIC AND DAILY MIRROR FILLED
THE VACANCY LEFT BY THE OLD WORLD, now a Cons. Dep

商业新闻机构为了生存必须出售其新闻。除了得到日本主要报纸的有力财政支持外，作为政府机构的同盟社（Dendo，此处应指Domei/联合通讯社或相关政府背景机构，原文如此）在必要时总是可以指望政府的支持。日本电报通讯社的地位则不同。竞争对手新闻机构的“独家新闻”[原文不清]可能是灾难性的。由此产生的自然结果是，日本电报通讯社在其新闻报道中往往倾向于耸人听闻。这种政策经常在中国官方圈子中被误解。该机构在中国被形容为“反南京”。

日本电报通讯社所采用的策略并非新鲜事。欧洲和美国的许多报纸和新闻机构都曾做过同样的事情。《纽约世界报》在早期并不被纽约最优质的读者群所阅读。但随着其发行量的迅速增长并确立了作为纽约主要日报之一的地位，其编辑方针逐渐发生了改变。它不再是一份耸人听闻的小报。其他报纸如《纽约美国人日报》、《每日新闻》、《晚间画报》和《每日镜报》填补了旧《世界报》留下的空缺，现为 Cons. Dep

pages.en:
JAPANESE---31.

THE MAJORITY OF THE NEWSPAPERS IN JAPAN DEPEND ON
RENGO AND NIPPON DENPO FOR THEIR CHINESE NEWS. IT IS
TOO EXPENSIVE TO MAINTAIN SPECIAL BUREAUX IN DIFFERENT
PARTS OF CHINA. SOME OF THE LEADING NEWSPAPERS IN
TOKYO AND OSAKA, HOWEVER, HAVE THEIR OWN STAFF
CORRESPONDENTS IN VARIOUS POLITICAL CENTRES IN THIS
COUNTRY. PAPERS LIKE OSAKA ASAHI, OSAKA MAINICHI, AND
JIJI ARE REPRESENTED AT NANKING, SHANGHAI, PEIPING,
TIENTSIN, HANKOW AND LIAOLING (MUKDEN).

ONE CAN WITNESS AT NANKING A STRIKING ILLUSTRATION
OF THE ENERGETIC MANNER IN WHICH THE JAPANESE
CORRESPONDENTS COVER NEWS EVENTS IN CHINA. WHEN MR.
SHICHTARO YADA, FORMER JAPANESE CONSUL-GENERAL AT
SHANGHAI, CAME TO NANKING IN 1928 TO DISCUSS WITH DR.
C. T. WANG, CHINESE MINISTER FOR FOREIGN AFFAIRS,
VARIOUS OUTSTANDING SINO-JAPANESE ISSUES---LIKE THE
TSINAN INCIDENT, NANKING AND HANKOW INCIDENTS, SINO-
JAPANESE TARIFF AGREEMENT, AND OTHER---THE JAPANESE
CORRESPONDENTS FLOODED THE NANKING TELEGRAPH, RADIO
AND TELEPHONE OFFICES WITH MESSAGES ABOUT THE CONVER-
SATIONS BETWEEN THE TWO DIPLOMATS. THEY BOOKED UP ALL
THE LONG-DISTANCE TELEPHONE CALLS BETWEEN SHANGHAI AND
NANKING FROM 9 O'CLOCK IN THE MORNING TO MIDNIGHT AT
URGENT RATE. THE CHARGE WAS ABOUT a DOLLAR A MINUTE.
pages.zh:
日本---31.

日本大多数报纸依赖联合通讯社和日本电报通讯社获取关于中国的新闻。在中国不同地区维持专门分局费用过于高昂。然而，东京和大阪的一些主要报纸在该国的各个政治中心拥有自己的专职记者。像《大阪朝日新闻》、《大阪每日新闻》和《时事新报》这样的报纸在南京、上海、北平、天津、汉口和辽阳（沈阳）均有代表。

在南京，人们可以目睹日本记者报道中国新闻事件的精力充沛方式的惊人例证。1928年，当日本驻上海前总领事矢田七太郎先生（Shichtaro Yada，音译）来到南京，与中国外交部长王正廷博士讨论各种突出的中日问题——如济南惨案、南京和汉口事件、中日关税协定等——时，日本记者用关于两位外交官会谈的消息淹没了南京的电报、无线电和电话局。他们以加急费率预订了从早上9点到午夜所有上海至南京的长途电话。费用约为每分钟一美元。

pages.en:
JAPANESE---32.

EVERY MOVEMENT OF MR. YADA AND EVERY GOSSIP ABOUT THE
CONVERSATIONS WERE REPORTED TO NEWSPAPERS IN JAPAN.
IN THE DAYS OF THE OLD PEKING GOVERNMENT, WHENEVER
ANY INTERVIEWS WERE GRANTED TO NEWSPAPER MEN BY
GOVERNMENT LEADERS, THERE WERE ALWAYS INTERPRETERS
AT THE INTERVIEWS FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE JAPANESE
CORRESPONDENTS. VERY OFTEN THE CHINESE OFFICIALS WOULD
REFUSE TO RECEIVE A NATIVE NEWSPAPERMAN, BUT WOULD SEE
A JAPANESE CORRESPONDENT. BUT NOT SO IN NANKING. IT IS
EXTREMELY DIFFICULT FOR A JAPANESE CORRESPONDENT TO
GO AROUND NANKING FOR NEWS. NOT MANY OF THEM CAN SPEAK
CHINESE FLUENTLY AND THERE ARE NO JAPANESE ADVISERS
IN THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT TO GIVE THEM 'TIPS' ON
POLITICAL DEVELOPMENTS. IN FACT, NEARLY EVERY ONE OF
THE JAPANESE CORRESPONDENTS IN THE CHINESE CAPITAL
ENGAGES CERTAIN CHINESE REPORTERS TO KEEP THEM INFORMED
OF THE LATEST DOINGS IN THE GOVERNMENT. SINCE THE
TYPE OF CHINESE NEWSPAPER MEN WHO ARE WILLING TO
PERFORM SUCH WORK IS NOT NECESSARILY OF THE BEST, THE
NEWS OBTAINED BY THE JAPANESE CORRESPONDENTS ABOUT
POLITICAL DOINGS IN CHINA ARE SOMETIMES INACCURATE OR
MUTILATED.
HERE IS A CLASSICAL ILLUSTRATION OF THE SITUATION.
THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT ON DECEMBER 29, 1930, PROMULGATED
pages.zh:
日本---32.

矢田先生的一举一动以及关于会谈的每一则流言蜚语都被报道给日本的报纸。在旧北京政府时期，每当政府领导人接受报界采访时，总会有译员在场，以便日本记者受益。中国官员常常拒绝接见本国记者，但却会见日本记者。但在南京情况并非如此。日本记者在南京四处采访新闻极其困难。他们中没多少人能流利地说中文，而且国民政府中没有日本顾问向他们提供政治发展的“内幕消息”。事实上，几乎每一位在中国首都的日本记者都雇佣某些中国记者，让他们随时了解政府的最新动向。由于愿意从事此类工作的中国报人类型未必是最优秀的，日本记者获得的关于中国政治活动的消息有时不准确或被歪曲。
以下是一个典型的例子。国民政府于1930年12月29日颁布

pages.en:
JAPANESE---33.

THE NEW IMPORT TARIFF SCHEDULE. MONTHS BEFORE IT WAS
PROMULGATED, EVERY CHINESE AND FOREIGN NEWSPAPER MAN
IN NANKING TRIED EVERY MEANS TO OBTAIN A COPY OF THE
NEW SCHEDULE. THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE AND THE LEGISLA-
TIVE YUAN, WHICH HANDLED THE MATTER, REFUSED TO GIVE
OUT ANY INFORMATION ON THIS SUBJECT. BUSINESS FIRMS
IN JAPAN WERE ESPECIALLY ANXIOUS TO HAVE SOME ADVANCE
INFORMATION ABOUT THE NEW IMPORT DUTIES, FOR THEY
WOULD BE SERIOUSLY AFFECTED BY ANY SWEEPING INCREASE.
SOME JAPANESE CORRESPONDENT IN THE CAPITAL BOUGHT A
BOGUS COPY OF THE SCHEDULE AT A PRICE OF $500. IMAGINE
HIS DISAPPOINTMENT WHEN HE DISCOVERED ON DECEMBER 29,
WHEN THE FULL SCHEDULE WAS OFFICIALLY PROMULGATED BY
THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT, THAT THE COPY HE HAD WAS
MERELY THE FIRST DRAFT PREPARED BY THE TARIFF COMMISSION
OF THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE! THE RATES HAD BEEN CHANGED
CONSIDERABLY BY THE LEGISLATIVE YUAN.

ANOTHER DRAW BACK THE JAPANESE CORRESPONDENTS HAVE
IN THEIR WORK IS THAT BEFORE THEY CAN SETTLE DOWN AT
ONE PLACE, THEY ARE SENT BY THEIR HOME OFFICES TO SOME
OTHER CITY WHERE THEY HAVE TO START ALL OVER AGAIN.
THE OSAKA ASAHI CHANGED THEIR CORRESPONDENT IN NANKING
THREE TIMES IN THAT MANY YEARS, AND THE RENGO TWICE.
pages.zh:
日本人---33.

新进口税则。在该税则颁布前的数月间，南京的每一位中外报人都千方百计试图获取一份新税则的副本。负责处理此事的财政部和立法院拒绝透露任何相关信息。日本的商号尤其渴望获得关于新进口关税的一些提前信息，因为任何大幅度的增加都将对它们产生严重影响。首都的一名日本记者以500美元的价格购买了一份伪造的税则副本。想象一下，当他在12月29日国民政府正式颁布完整税则时，发现自己手中的副本仅仅是财政部税则委员会 prepared 的初稿时，他是多么失望！税率已被立法院大幅修改。

日本记者在工作中面临的另一个不利条件是，在他们尚未在一个地方安顿下来之前，就被其国内总部派往其他城市，不得不从头开始。《大阪朝日新闻》在那几年里三次更换了其驻南京记者，《联合通讯社》（Rengo）则更换了两次。

JAPANESE---34.

IT IS DIFFICULT ENOUGH TO FAMILIARIZE ONESELF WITH one's
HIS SURROUNDINGS, ESPECIALLY IN A FOREIGN COUNTRY.
a Japanese correspondent
JUST WHEN one BEGINS TO HAVE FRIENDS AND TO ESTABLISH
CONNECTIONS, SO THAT HE CAN MOVE AROUND THE PLACE A
LITTLE, HE IS SENT TO A NEW PLACE. NOT ONLY IS IT HARD
ON THE MAN WHO IS LEAVING. IT IS EQUALLY HARD ON THE
his
MAN WHO IS COMING IN TO TAKE THE FORMER'S PLACE.

EDITORS OF JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS IN CHINA AND
CORRESPONDENTS HERE REPRESENTING NEWSPAPERS IN JAPAN
HAVE IMPORTANT RESPONSIBILITIES ON THEIR SHOULDERS.
THE PART THEY PLAY IN THE BRINGING ABOUT OF A CLOSER
FRIENDSHIP BETWEEN THE TWO NATIONS CAN BE MORE EFFEC-
played by
TIVE THAN THAT OF THE DIPLOMATS. IT MUST BE REMEMBERED
THAT THE JAPANESE NEWSPAPER MEN IN CHINA ARE HERE TO
RECORD FOR THE JAPANESE PUBLIC AND TO INTERPRET TO THE
JAPANESE PUBLIC THAT WHICH IS GOING ON IN THIS COUNTRY.
BARON SHIDEHARA HAS REPEATEDLY DECLARED IN HIS DIS-
CUSSIONS ON SINO-JAPANESE RELATIONS:

THERE IS NO OTHER COURSE OPEN TO THE TWO NATIONS
THAN TO PURSUE THE PATH OF MUTUAL ACCORD AND CO-
OPERATION IN ALL THEIR RELATIONS, POLITICAL AND
ECONOMIC. THEIR REAL AND LASTING INTERESTS, WHICH
IN NO WAY CONFLICT BUT HAVE MUCH IN COMMON, WITH
EACH OTHER, OUGHT TO BE A SUFFICIENT ASSURANCE OF
THEIR GROWING RAPPROCHEMENT.
pages.zh:
日本人---34.

熟悉周围环境本就困难重重，尤其是在异国他乡。一名日本记者刚刚开始结交朋友并建立关系网，从而能够在这个地方稍微自由活动时，却被派往一个新的地方。这不仅对离开的人很艰难，对前来接替前者职位的人同样艰难。

在华日本报纸的编辑以及代表日本报纸驻此地的记者肩负着重要的责任。他们在促进两国之间更紧密友谊方面所发挥的作用，可能比外交官更为有效。必须记住，在华的日本报人是来为日本公众记录并向日本公众解读这个国家正在发生的事情。币原喜重郎男爵（Baron Shidehara）在讨论中日关系时曾多次声明：

两国在所有政治和经济关系中，除了追求相互协调与合作的道路外，别无他途。他们真正且持久的利益不仅毫无冲突，而且有许多共同之处，这应当足以保证他们日益接近。

pages.en:
JAPANESE---35.

JAPANESE TRADE IN CHINA HAS SUFFERED AT DIFFERENT
TIMES FOR POLITICAL REASONS. JAPANESE GOODS WERE
BOYCOTTED HERE IN 1915, 1919, AND FROM 1919 TO 1922.
THE MOST RECENT ANTI-JAPANESE TROUBLES WERE OVER THE
TSINAN INCIDENT. THIS IMPEDIMENT TO SINO-JAPANESE
TRADE HAS, HOWEVER, GRADUALLY DISAPPEARED. JAPANESE
TRADE IS ON THE ASCENDANT AND JAPANESE GOODS HAVE AN
ADVANTAGE OVER SIMILAR EUROPEAN AND AMERICAN PRODUCTS
BECAUSE OF PROPINQUITY TO THE China MARKET.

AS ALL GOOD JOURNALISTS ARE PERSUADERS OF THE WORLD,
IN THE LANGUAGE OF THOMAS CARLYLE, THE JAPANESE PRESS
IN CHINA is EXPECTED TO PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE
TASK OF REMOVING ALL OBSTACLES TO A CLOSER SINO-JAPANESE
UNDERSTANDING AND to the of CEMENTING A LASTING SINO-
JAPANESE FRIENDSHIP.

--------
pages.zh:
日本人---35.

日本对华贸易曾因政治原因在不同时期遭受损失。日本货物曾于1915年、1919年以及1919年至1922年间在此遭到抵制。最近一次的反日风波是围绕济南惨案发生的。然而，这种对中日贸易的阻碍已逐渐消失。日本贸易正处于上升期，由于靠近中国市场，日本商品相比类似的欧美产品具有优势。

正如托马斯·卡莱尔（Thomas Carlyle）所言，所有优秀的新闻记者都是世界的说服者，因此，在华日本报界被期望在消除阻碍中日更紧密理解的障碍以及巩固持久中日友谊的任务中发挥重要作用。

(C.I.D.) Office Notes
June 25, 1930.

REPORT ON JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS IN SHANGHAI

Sir,
The Shanghai Nippo, No. 3 Barchet Road, the oldest Japanese newspaper in Shanghai, was established 26 years ago. It is the official organ of the Japanese Consulate-General in Shanghai and publishes all its notifications. All business advertisements, announcements and notices, to be legal, must appear in this paper. For its service to the Japanese Consulate, the Nippo is given a subsidy the amount of which cannot be ascertained.
The present value of the paper is estimated at $70,000 000. It has a circulation of 2,000 local and 1,000 outports.
The Nippo has no definite policy beyond the general one of promoting Japanese interests and commerce in China. It has no connection with any of the political parties in Japan.
The founder of the Nippo was Mr. S. Ide, a member of the House of Representatives of Japan who owned the paper until November, 1929, when he sold his interests to Mr. H. Hata (Address: No. 619 Dixwell Road). Mr. Hata was formerly connected with the Toho News Agency of which he was the founder. During the Great War, Mr. Hata succeeded in securing a controlling interest in the "Shanghai Times", an interest which he still holds. Three years ago, when the Associated Press of Japan (a news distribution service like that of Reuter's or the Associated Press of America) was established, the Toho News Agency was merged with the larger institution. The Nippo is the only Japanese paper in China which is a member of the Associated Press of Japan.
The paper publishes two editions daily; one in the morning and one in the evening.
The officials of the company are:-
Mr. H. Hata, President and Proprietor.
Mr. T. Akaboshi, Chief Editor.
Mr. S. Okunomiya, Manager.
There are seven reporters and 47 Chinese compositors and printers.
------------------
Although it was established only 11 years ago, the Shanghai Mainichi is the largest Japanese paper in China, excluding Manchuria. Its circulation is 7,000 local and 1,000 outports, and among its subscribers are 1,000 Chinese mostly of the official and student class.
The present value of the Mainichi is estimated at $70,000. The policy of the paper is to promote Sino-Japanese friendship and for this reason it is widely read by Chinese when disputes arise between China and Japan. It is the only Japanese paper in Shanghai which is a member of the Japanese Press Association. It is not connected with any of the Japanese political parties.
The paper publishes two editions daily; one in the morning and one in the evening.
The officers of the paper are:-
Mr. S. Fukamachi, Managing Director, Chief Editor, and Proprietor.
Mr. S. Matsui, Manager.
There are also 20 Japanese reporters, photographers, etc. and 100 Chinese compositors and printers.
Address: No. 77 Woosung Road.
------------------

关于上海日本报纸的报告

先生，
《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo），位于巴切特路3号，是上海最古老的日本报纸，成立于26年前。它是日本驻上海总领事馆的官方机关报，刊登其所有通告。所有商业广告、公告和通知，若要具有法律效力，必须在该报刊登。鉴于其为日本领事馆提供的服务，《上海日报》获得了一笔补贴，具体金额无法查明。
该报目前的估值约为70,000美元。其发行量为本地2,000份，外埠1,000份。
除了促进日本在华利益和商业这一总体方针外，《上海日报》没有明确的政策。它与日本的任何政党均无关联。
《上海日报》的创始人是S. Ide先生，他是日本众议院议员，拥有该报直至1929年11月，当时他将权益出售给了H. Hata先生（地址：狄思威路619号）。Hata先生此前与东邦通讯社有关联，他是该社的创始人。大战期间，Hata先生成功获得了《字林西报》（Shanghai Times）的控股权，该权益他至今仍持有。三年前，当日本联合通讯社（一家类似路透社或美国美联社的新闻分发机构）成立时，东邦通讯社并入该大型机构。《上海日报》是中国唯一一家加入日本联合通讯社的日本报纸。
该报每日出版两版；一版在早晨，一版在晚上。
公司职员如下：-
H. Hata先生，社长兼业主。
T. Akaboshi先生，主编。
S. Okunomiya先生，经理。
有七名记者和47名中国排字工及印刷工。
------------------
虽然《上海每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi）仅成立了11年，但它是除满洲以外中国最大的日本报纸。其发行量为本地7,000份，外埠1,000份，在其订阅者中有1,000名中国人，大多属于官员和学生阶层。
《每日新闻》目前的估值约为70,000美元。该报的宗旨是促进中日友好，因此当中日发生争端时，它被中国人广泛阅读。它是上海唯一一家加入日本报业协会的日本报纸。它与日本的任何政党均无关联。
该报每日出版两版；一版在早晨，一版在晚上。
报社职员如下：-
S. Fukamachi先生，常务董事、主编兼业主。
S. Matsui先生，经理。
此外还有20名日本记者、摄影师等，以及100名中国排字工和印刷工。
地址：吴淞路77号。
------------------

The Shanghai Shuho Sha, a Japanese monthly magazine, was established 20 years ago by a number of prominent Japanese residents amongst whom were the late Mr. Naizu, President of Tun Wen College, the late Mr. Shimida, Editor of the Shanghai Nippo, the late Mr. Endo, the correspondent of the Osaka Mainichi, Mr. K. Yamada, a Professor of Tun Wen College, Mr. Ide, a member of the Japanese House of Representatives and former owner of the Shanghai Nippo(q.v.), Mr. H. Hata, the present proprietor of the Shanghai Nippo, Mr. T. Sahara, formerly Editor of the Shanghai Mercury and now Proprietor of the Shun Tien Jih Pao, a Chinese paper published in Mukden, Mr. Kamio, the Correspondent of the Osaka Asahi, and several others.
The name of the paper originally was "Shuho Shanghai" but was changed to its present name eight years ago.
As the object of the promoters is not to derive monetary profit from the publication, there is therefore no capital. The paper has been self-supporting and when for any reason it is short of funds the promoters make voluntary contributions.
The policy of the paper is to place before its readers, especially those in Japan, the true political, economic, and educational situation in China. The paper is not connected with any of the political parties in Japan. Articles have been contributed to its pages by prominent merchants, officials, and journalists.
The circulation is 1,000 local and 500 outports, mostly to Japan and Manchuria. The paper has 200 Chinese subscribers, mostly officials and returned students.
The paper is printed by the Ashizawa Printing Co., No. 14 Haining Road, and is sold at 20 cents a copy.
Mr. T. Mimura is the Editor and representative of the board of trustees. He took over the paper two years ago from Mr. T. Swara who had been in charge since its existence. However, as most of the promoters are no longer resident in Shanghai, some having died and others having gone abroad, a plan is under consideration for the reorganization of the magazine.
Address: 1086 Yung An Lee, North Szechuen Road.
------------------
The Shanghai Jiron, a Japanese weekly magazine, was started 12 years ago. Prior to 1925 the paper was known by the name of "Shanghai-to-Nippon Jin".
