"ORIENTAL AFFAIRS" (British Monthly)

"Oriental Affairs", No. 19 Avenue Edward VII,
established in December, 1930, is owned and published
by Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead, a British subject. It has a
circulation of 1,200.

The journal is a strong supporter of British
policy and interests in China. It is an impartial
critic of Far Eastern affairs and deals with politics,
trade, science, etc. After the State of Manchukuo was
established in 1932, Mr. Woodhead published, off and on,
a series of articles on this subject not only in
"Oriental Affairs" but also in the "Shanghai Evening Post
& Mercury". The Chinese Government took exception to the
tenor of these articles which were regarded as being anti-
Chinese and pro-Manchukuo as well as being in favour of
Japan's action in Manchukuo. In June, 1934, the
National Government placed a ban on "Oriental Affairs"
and the interdiction is still in force. Mr. Woodhead
asserts that he has still to hear from the Chinese
Government regarding the cause of the ban. Several
protests have been lodged by the British authorities
but all, so far, without effect.

The policy of "Oriental Affairs" towards the
local authorities, Chinese and Municipal, is one of friendly
and constructive criticism.

Among Chinese, the journal is regarded as
being pro-Japanese and pro-Manchukuo, while others even
go so far as to allege that its publisher, Mr. Woodhead,
is in receipt of a subsidy from both Japan and Manchukuo -
a statement which, even if true, is difficult to prove.

The journal is well served by correspondents
in various parts of China, with a special correspondent at
Nanking.

Staff
Editor : Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead.

《东方事务》（英国月刊）

《东方事务》，地址为爱德华七世路19号，于1930年12月创办，由英国臣民H.G.W. Woodhead先生拥有并出版。其发行量为1,200份。

该刊物是英国在华政策和利益的坚定支持者。它是远东事务的公正评论者，内容涉及政治、贸易、科学等。1932年满洲国建立后，Woodhead先生不仅在《东方事务》上，也在《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）上断续发表了一系列关于此主题的文章。中国政府对这些文章的基调表示异议，认为这些文章反华、亲满洲国，并支持日本在满洲国的行动。1934年6月，国民政府禁止《东方事务》发行，该禁令至今仍然有效。Woodhead先生声称，他尚未收到中国政府关于禁令原因的通知。英国当局已提出多次抗议，但迄今为止均无效果。

《东方事务》对当地中国当局和工部局当局的 policy 是进行友好且建设性的批评。

在中国人眼中，该刊物被视为亲日和亲满洲国，甚至有人进一步指控其出版人Woodhead先生接受来自日本和满洲国的津贴——这一说法即使属实，也难以证实。

该刊物在中国各地拥有良好的通讯员网络，并在南京设有特约通讯员。

职员
编辑：H.G.W. Woodhead先生。

"THE FAR EASTERN REVIEW" (American Monthly)

"The Far Eastern Review", No. 21 and
21B Yokohama Specie Bank Building, No. The Bund,
was established in 1906. It is published by Mr. G.
Bronson Rea, an American citizen.

The "Review", which claims to be the pioneer
trade journal of Eastern Asia, specializes in articles
dealing with general engineering, and commerce,
but it also writes on political affairs especially on
matters appertaining to the Far East. Subscribers
are to be found in China, Japan, and Siberia,
Indo-China, Siam, the Philippines, Straits Settlements,
Malay States, Dutch East Indies, as well as in Europe
and America.

the State of Manchukuo, the "Review" published
several articles in favour of the new State and
extolling the constructive work carried out by Japan
in that territory. These articles were naturally
regarded with great disfavour by the National Government.
Furthermore, during the past two and a half years,
Mr. Rea has been travelling in Europe and America as

《远东评论》（美国月刊）

《远东评论》，地址为外滩横滨正金银行大楼21及21B室，创办于1906年。由美国公民G. Bronson Rea先生出版。

《评论》自称是东亚先驱性贸易期刊，专门刊登有关一般工程和商业的文章，但也撰写政治事务，特别是涉及远东的事务。其订户分布在中国、日本和西伯利亚、印度支那、暹罗、菲律宾、海峡殖民地、马来邦、荷属东印度，以及欧洲和美洲。

满洲国成立后，《评论》发表了几篇支持新国家的文章，赞扬日本在该地区进行的建设工作。这些文章自然受到国民政府的极大反感。此外，在过去两年半中，Rea先生作为满洲国代表在欧洲和美洲旅行，并在国际联盟审议承认满洲国问题时出席日内瓦会议。此后，Rea先生被任命为满洲国外交部顾问，其在华盛顿特区的办公室设在专属的肖勒姆酒店（Shoreham Hotel）。

《远东评论》（美国月刊）

《远东评论》，地址为外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼21及21B室，创办于1906年。由美国公民G. Bronson Rea先生出版。

《评论》自称是东亚先驱性贸易期刊，专门刊登有关一般工程、金融和商业的文章，但也撰写政治事务，特别是涉及远东的事务。其订户分布在中国、日本、东西伯利亚、印度支那、暹罗、菲律宾、海峡殖民地、马来邦、荷属东印度，以及欧洲和美洲。

1932年12月19日，Rea先生收到国民政府交通部的一封信，通知对《评论》实施禁令，并将拒绝提供邮政和电报服务，但未说明采取此行动的原因。满洲国成立后，《评论》发表了几篇支持新国家的文章，赞扬日本在该地区进行的建设工作。这些文章自然受到国民政府的极大反感。此外，在过去两年半中，Rea先生作为满洲国代表在欧洲和美洲旅行，并在国际联盟审议承认满洲国问题时出席日内瓦会议。此后，Rea先生被任命为满洲国外交部顾问，其在华盛顿特区的办公室设在专属的肖勒姆酒店（Shoreham Hotel）。

pages.en:
(2)

In view of these facts, the action of the Chinese
Government in placing the "Review" under a ban was
not altogether unexpected.

Prior to the ban, the "Review" had a
circulation of 5,000 distributed as follows : China
50%; Japan 30%; the Philippines 10%; Indo-China,
Siam, Straits Settlements, Federated Malay States
and Dutch Indies 8%; Europe and America 2% The
circulation to-day has dropped to 3,500, the fall
being attributed partly to the ban and partly to the
world trade depression. The several protests
lodged by the American Minister to China against the
ban have had no result.

During the absence of Mr. Rea from Shanghai
during the past 2½ years, Mr. C.J. Laval has been in
charge of the "Review". The foremost policy of the
journal is to keep the United States out of a war
with Japan over Far Eastern questions, especially
Chinese affairs. Clear instructions have been laid
down by Mr. Rea that the "Review" must not be anti-
Chinese nor anti-anybody or anything. As proof of
his intention to observe these instructions, Mr.
Laval states that he has published several articles
from the pens of Wang Ching Wei, President of the
Executive Yuan, and other Nanking officials which
had been sent to the "Review" in an indirect way.

The attitude of the "Review" towards
Manchukuo and Japan is one of great friendliness
and many articles have appeared in its pages in
praise of the reforms and improvements introduced
in Manchukuo by Japan. Towards China, the "Review"
pages.zh:
(2)

鉴于上述事实，中国政府对《评论》实施禁令的行动并不完全出人意料。

在禁令实施之前，《评论》的发行量为5,000份，分布如下：中国50%；日本30%；菲律宾10%；印度支那、暹罗、海峡殖民地、马来联邦和荷属东印度8%；欧洲和美洲2%。目前的发行量已降至3,500份，下降部分归因于禁令，部分归因于世界贸易萧条。美国驻华公使针对该禁令提出的几次抗议均未取得结果。

在Rea先生过去两年半离开上海期间，《评论》由C.J. Laval先生负责。该刊物的首要政策是让美国避免因远东问题，特别是中国事务，而与日本发生战争。Rea先生已下达明确指示，《评论》不得反华，也不得反对任何人或任何事物。为了证明其遵守这些指示的意图，Laval先生声明，他已发表了几篇来自行政院院长汪精卫及其他南京官员的文章，这些文章是以间接方式寄给《评论》的。

《评论》对满洲国和日本的态度非常友好，其版面上刊登了许多文章，赞扬日本在满洲国推行的改革和改进。对中国，《评论》

pages.en:
(3)

is a friendly critic and its writings have never
been of the kind that might be called hysterical or
harsh. When it has anything to say of the local
Municipal Administration, which is not often, its
criticism has always been of a constructive character.

Staff

Associate Editor : C.J. Laval.
Cashier : E.E. Wilson.
Advertising Manager : S.O. Christy

是一位友好的批评者，其文章从未带有可被称为歇斯底里或严厉的性质。当它谈及当地工部局行政时（这种情况并不多见），其批评总是具有建设性。

副编辑：C.J. Laval。
出纳：E.E. Wilson。

pages.en:
"THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW" (American Weekly)

"The China Weekly Review", No. 160 Avenue
Edward VII, was established in 1916 under the name of
"Millard's Review". It is published by the Millard
Publishing Co., Incorporated under the laws of the
State of Delaware, U.S.A., with a capital of $50,000.
The majority of the shares in the concern are held
by Mr. J.B. Powell.

The "Review" is a supporter of the policy
of the U.S. Government towards China. In politics,
it is violently hostile to Japan; generally unfriendly
to Great Britain or things British; strongly critical
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, especially the
Shanghai Municipal Police and distinctly pro-Chinese
so much so that it is regarded in some quarters as the
foreign propaganda organ of Generalissimo Chiang Kai
Shek, the leader of the National Government.

It publishes informative articles on trade,
finance, education and social matters relating to
China, and, as its name indicates, it is a weekly
review of important events in the Far East, especially
in China.

It has correspondents at Peiping, Tientsin,
Nanking, Hankow, Hongkong and in a number of small
towns in the interior. 60% of its readers are Chinese
of the official, merchant and student classes.

The "Review" has a circulation of 4,000.
It is considered the best medium for reaching Chinese
officials, professional and business men interested in
foreign trade or Sino-foreign relations.
pages.zh:
《中国每周评论》（美国周刊）

《中国每周评论》，地址为爱德华七世路160号，于1916年以《密勒氏评论报》（Millard's Review）之名创办。由密勒出版公司（Millard Publishing Co.）出版，该公司根据美国特拉华州法律注册，资本为50,000美元。该公司的大部分股份由J.B. Powell先生持有。

《评论》支持美国政府对华政策。在政治上，它强烈敌视日本；通常对英国或英国事物不友好；严厉批评上海工部局，特别是上海公共租界工部局警务处，并且明显亲华，以至于在某些方面被视为国民政府领袖蒋介石总司令的外国宣传机构。

它刊登有关中国贸易、金融、教育和社会问题的资讯性文章，并且如其名所示，它是远东重要事件，特别是中国重要事件的每周回顾。

它在北平、天津、南京、汉口、香港以及内地许多小城镇设有通讯员。其读者中有60%是官方、商界和学生阶层的中国人。

《评论》的发行量为4,000份。它被认为是接触对中国对外贸易或中外关系感兴趣的中国官员、专业人士和商人的最佳媒介。

pages.en:
(2)

                  Boh Chih Hsiang.

pages.en:
"THE PEOPLE'S TRIBUNE" (Chinese Bi-Monthly)

"The People's Tribune", No. 299 Szechuen
Road, was established in 1927. It is a bi-monthly
English language journal published by the China United
Press, a Chinese concern.

The "Tribune" claims to be "an organ of
national-revolutionary thought and opinion", but in its
issue of January 1, 1935 this was altered to read as
follows :- "A journal of fact and opinion about China
and other countries".

The "Tribune" is a staunch supporter of
Nationalism and advocates progressive reforms and
reconstruction in China. It claims to be a fearless
critic of any acts of misgovernment and does not
believe in destructive criticism of any person or body,
official or otherwise. It is strongly anti-Japanese
and frankly outspoken on the subject of extraterritoriality,
but it disavows being in any degree anti-foreign or
chauvinistic. In local affairs, it is somewhat critical
of the foreign municipal administrations and in matters
affecting Chinese and foreign interests, it invariably
takes the Chinese view.

The "Tribune" has a circulation of 3,000
distributed 900 locally and 2,100 outports. A large
number of its readers are to be found in the Malay
States, Dutch East Indies and the Philippines Islands.

The "Tribune" is believed to be an English
language propaganda organ of the National Government.

Staff
Editor : Tang Leang Li.
Secretary : She Shao Pei.
Legal Advisor : T.K. Sun.
pages.zh:
《人民论坛》（中文双月刊）*注：原文标题注明Chinese Bi-Monthly，但正文描述为English language journal，此处依正文翻译*

《人民论坛》，地址为四川路299号，创办于1927年。这是一本由华人企业联合出版社（China United Press）出版的英文双月刊。

《论坛》自称是“民族革命思想和舆论的机关”，但在1935年1月1日的那一期中，这一表述被改为：“一本关于中国和其他国家的事实与意见的期刊”。

《论坛》是民族主义的坚定支持者，倡导中国的进步改革和重建。它自称是对任何治理不善行为的无畏批评者，并且不相信对任何个人或团体（无论是官方还是其他）进行破坏性批评。它强烈反日，并在治外法权问题上坦率直言，但它否认有任何程度的排外或沙文主义倾向。在地方事务上，它对外国市政当局持一定批评态度，在涉及中外利益的事项上，它 invariably 采取中方观点。

《论坛》的发行量为3,000份，其中本地分发900份，外埠分发2,100份。其大量读者分布在马来邦、荷属东印度和菲律宾群岛。

《论坛》被认为是国民政府的英文宣传机构。

职员
编辑：Tang Leang Li（唐良礼/唐良李，音译）。
秘书：She Shao Pei（佘少佩，音译）。
法律顾问：T.K. Sun（音译）。

pages.en:
"THE CHINA CRITIC" (Chinese Weekly)

"The China Critic", No. 749 Bubbling Well
Road, is published by the China Critic Publishing Co.
It was established in 1928 by a number of returned
students whose feelings were aroused by the Tsinan
Incident which occurred in May of that year. It
has a circulation of 8,000.

The journal claims to follow an independent
policy. It supports the National Government and is
unfriendly towards Great Britain. In local municipal
affairs, the journal always favours the Chinese side
in disputes over rights between the local foreign and
Chinese administrative organs.

It is generally believed to be in receipt
of financial support from Sun Fo's Party.

Staff

Associate Editors : Liu Yu and T.K. Chuan.

Chien Chung Shu, P.C.Kuo,

《中国评论周报》（中文周刊）*注：原文标题注明Chinese Weekly，但通常The China Critic为英文周刊，此处依原文结构翻译*

《中国评论周报》，地址为静安寺路749号，由中国评论周报出版公司出版。它由一群归国学生于1928年创办，这些学生的情感因当年5月发生的济南惨案而被激发。其发行量为8,000份。

该刊物声称奉行独立政策。它支持国民政府，并对英国不友好。在地方市政事务中，在当地外国和中国行政机构之间的权利纠纷中，该刊物总是偏向中方。

人们普遍认为它接受孙科派系的财政支持。

职员
编辑：Kwei Chung Hsu（桂中枢，音译）。
副编辑：Liu Yu（刘宇，音译）和 T.K. Chuan（音译）。
特约编辑：V.T. Bang（音译）、L.T. Chen（音译）、Chien Chung Shu（音译）、P.C. Kuo（音译）、Edward T.K. Kwang（音译）、Kan Lee（音译）、Yuen Li Tang（音译）、D.K. Lieu（音译）、Li Yu Tang（音译）、Lowe Chuan Hua（音译）、Francis K. Pan（音译）、Quentin Pan（音译）和 Wen Yuan Ming（音译）。

pages.en:
"THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR"

"The Shanghai Spectator", No. 80 Nanking
Road, established in 1931, is published by the
Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated in Delaware, U.S.A.
The President of the concern is A.W. Beaumont, a
Belgian protected subject, whose proper name is said
to be Izraleiwitch, a Russian Jew.

The "Spectator" is a weekly of somewhat
doubtful reputation, not only because of the mystery
surrounding the antecedents of its President, Beaumont,
but because of the character of the articles appearing
within its pages. Its policy seems to be one of
virile criticism of some individual or company
patronized by the public. Whether these criticisms
are written out of bona fide motives or otherwise,
Beaumont alone can tell, but a careful study of the
articles rather tends to show that this policy of
vilification of private individuals or public
companies is not actuated by the motive of pro bono
publico.

According to Beaumont himself, the "Spectator"
has the following capital :-
"6,000 common shares, no par value --- voting.
"Tls. 100,000 Preferred of Tael$ 10 each ---
non-voting." (These figures are somewhat doubtful)

The journal has a circulation of 3,000.
edition
10,000 copies of the Chinese/are printed weekly.

Staff
President : A.W. Beaumont (Belgian)
Editor : C.D. Alcott (American).
pages.zh:
《上海观察家》

《上海观察家》，地址为南京路80号，创办于1931年，由上海观察家公司出版，该公司在美国特拉华州注册。该公司总裁为A.W. Beaumont，一名受比利时保护的人员，据说其真名为Izraleiwitch，是一名俄罗斯犹太人。

《观察家》是一份声誉颇可疑的周刊，这不仅是因为其总裁Beaumont的背景充满神秘色彩，还因为其刊登文章的性质。其政策似乎是对某些受公众惠顾的个人或公司进行猛烈批评。无论这些批评是出于真诚动机还是其他原因，只有Beaumont本人知道，但对文章的仔细研究往往表明，这种诋毁个人或公共公司的政策并非出于公共利益（pro bono publico）的动机。

据Beaumont本人称，《观察家》拥有以下资本：
“6,000股普通股，无面值——有投票权。
“100,000两优先股，每股10两——无投票权。”（这些数字有些可疑）

该刊物发行量为3,000份。
中文版每周印刷10,000份。

职员
总裁：A.W. Beaumont（比利时籍）
编辑：C.D. Alcott（美国籍）。

pages.en:
"THE CHINESE REPUBLIC" (English-Language Weekly)

"The Chinese Republic", No. 150 Kiukiang Road,
was established in 1932 and is published by the Chinese
Republic Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of
Delaware, U.S.A.

The weekly follows an independent policy but
it has definitely southern tendencies. Articles
relating to trade, industry, education and politics are
published. It is being supported by Hu Han Min and
General Chen Chi Tang of Canton. Its circulation
is uncertain, estimates varying as much as from 800
to 3,000 copies.

Staff

Editor-in-Chief : Edward Bing Shuey Lee.
Associate Editors : J.T. Huang, Lemuel C.C. Jen
and H.C. Wang.
General Manager : Fang Yu Fang.
pages.zh:
《中华民国》（英文周刊）

《中华民国》，地址九江路150号，创刊于1932年，由中华民国出版公司（Chinese Republic Publishing Co.）出版，该公司依据美国特拉华州法律注册。

该周刊奉行独立方针，但具有明显的南方倾向。刊登有关贸易、工业、教育和政治的文章。它得到广州的胡汉民和陈济棠将军的支持。其发行量不确定，估计在800至3,000份之间波动。

职员

总编辑：Edward Bing Shuey Lee。
副编辑：J.T. Huang、Lemuel C.C. Jen 和 H.C. Wang。
总经理：Fang Yu Fang。

pages.en:
"ORIENTAL AFFAIRS" (British Monthly)

"Oriental Affairs", No. 19 Avenue Edward VII,
established in December, 1933, is owned and published
by Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead, a British subject. It has a
circulation of 1,200.

The journal is a strong supporter of British
policy and interests in China. It is an impartial
critic of Far Eastern affairs and deals with politics,
trade, science, etc. After the State of Manchukuo was
established in 1932, Mr. Woodhead published, off and on,
a series of articles on this subject not only in
"Oriental Affairs" but also in the "Shanghai Evening Post
& Mercury". The Chinese Government took exception to the
tenor of these articles which were regarded as being anti-
Chinese and pro-Manchukuo as well as being in favour of
Japan's action in Manchukuo. In June, 1934, the
National Government placed a ban on "Oriental Affairs"
and the interdiction is still in force. Mr. Woodhead
asserts that he has still to hear from the Chinese
Government regarding the cause of the ban. Several
protests have been lodged by the British authorities
but all, so far, without effect.

The policy of "Oriental Affairs" towards the
local authorities, Chinese and Municipal, is one of friendly
and constructive criticism.

Among Chinese, the journal is regarded as
being pro-Japanese and pro-Manchukuo, while others even
go so far as to allege that its publisher, Mr. Woodhead,
is in receipt of a subsidy from both Japan and Manchukuo -
a statement which, even if true, is difficult to prove.

The journal is well served by correspondents
in various parts of China, with a special correspondent at
Nanking.

Staff
Editor : Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead.
pages.zh:
《东方事务》（英国月刊）

《东方事务》，地址爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）19号，创刊于1933年12月，由英籍人士 H.G.W. Woodhead 先生拥有并出版。其发行量为1,200份。

该刊物是英国在华政策和利益的坚定支持者。它是远东事务的公正评论者，涉及政治、贸易、科学等领域。1932年满洲国成立后，Woodhead 先生不仅在《东方事务》上，也在《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）上断断续续发表了一系列关于此主题的文章。中国政府对这些文章的基调表示异议，认为这些文章反华、亲满洲国，并支持日本在满洲国的行动。1934年6月，国民政府禁止《东方事务》，该禁令至今仍然有效。Woodhead 先生声称，他尚未收到中国政府关于禁令原因的通知。英国当局已提出多次抗议，但迄今为止均无效果。

《东方事务》对当地中国当局和工部局当局的 policy 是友好和建设性的批评。

在中国人眼中，该刊物被视为亲日和亲满洲国，甚至有人进一步指控其出版商 Woodhead 先生接受日本和满洲国的津贴——这一说法即使属实，也难以证实。

该刊物在中国各地拥有良好的通讯员网络，并在南京设有特约通讯员。

职员
编辑：H.G.W. Woodhead 先生。

pages.en:
"THE FAR EASTERN REVIEW" (American Monthly)

"The Far Eastern Review", Rooms No. 21 and
21B Yokohama Specie Bank Building, No. 24 The Bund,
was established in 1904. It is published by Mr. G.
Bronson Rea, an American citizen.

The "Review", which claims to be the pioneer
trade journal of Eastern Asia, specializes in articles
dealing with general engineering, finance and commerce,
but it also writes on political affairs especially on
matters appertaining to the Far East. Subscribers
are to be found in China, Japan, Eastern Siberia,
Indo-China, Siam, the Philippines, Straits Settlements,
Malay States, Dutch East Indies as well as in Europe
and America.

On December 19, 1932, Mr.Rea received a
letter from the Ministry of Communications of the
National Government notifying that a ban had been
placed on the "Review" and that it will be denied
postal and telegraphic facilities, but no reason was
given for this action. After the establishment of
the State of Manchukuo, the "Review" published
several articles in favour of the new State and
extolling the constructive work carried out by Japan
in that territory. These articles were naturally
regarded with great disfavour by the National Government.
Furthermore, during the past two and a half years,
Mr. Rea has been travelling in Europe and America as
the representative of Manchukuo and was present at
Geneva when the question of the recognition of
Manchukuo was considered by the League of Nations.
Since then, Mr. Rea has been appointed Councillor to
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Manchukuo with an
office in the exclusive Shoreham Hotel, Washington, D.C.
pages.zh:
《远东评论》（美国月刊）

《远东评论》，地址外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼21及21B室，创刊于1904年。由美籍人士 G. Bronson Rea 先生出版。

《评论》自称是东亚先驱性贸易期刊，专门刊登有关一般工程、金融和商业的文章，但也撰写政治事务，特别是涉及远东的事项。其订阅者分布在中国、日本、东西伯利亚、印度支那、暹罗、菲律宾、海峡殖民地、马来邦、荷属东印度以及欧洲和美洲。

1932年12月19日，Rea 先生收到国民政府交通部的一封信，通知对《评论》实施禁令，并将拒绝提供邮政和电报服务，但未说明采取此行动的原因。满洲国成立后，《评论》发表了几篇支持新国家并赞扬日本在该地区进行的建设性工作的文章。这些文章自然受到国民政府的极大反感。此外，在过去两年半中，Rea 先生作为满洲国的代表在欧洲和美洲旅行，并在国际联盟审议承认满洲国问题时出席日内瓦会议。此后，Rea 先生被任命为满洲国外交部顾问，并在华盛顿特区高档的 Shoreham 酒店设有办公室。

pages.en:
(2)

In view of these facts, the action of the Chinese
Government in placing the "Review" under a ban was
not altogether unexpected.

Prior to the ban, the "Review" had a
circulation of 5,000 distributed as follows : China
50%; Japan 30%; the Philippines 10%; Indo-China,
Siam, Straits Settlements, Federated Malay States
and Dutch Indies 8%; Europe and America 2% The
circulation to-day has dropped to 3,500, the fall
being attributed partly to the ban and partly to the
world trade depression. The several protests
lodged by the American Minister to China against the
ban have had no result.

During the absence of Mr. Rea from Shanghai
during the past 2½ years, Mr. C.J. Laval has been in
charge of the "Review". The foremost policy of the
journal is to keep the United States out of a war
with Japan over Far Eastern questions, especially
Chinese affairs. Clear instructions have been laid
down by Mr. Rea that the "Review" must not be anti-
Chinese nor anti-anybody or anything. As proof of
his intention to observe these instructions, Mr.
Laval states that he has published several articles
from the pens of Wang Ching Wei, President of the
Executive Yuan, and other Nanking officials which
had been sent to the "Review" in an indirect way.

The attitude of the "Review" towards
Manchukuo and Japan is one of great friendliness
and many articles have appeared in its pages in
praise of the reforms and improvements introduced.
in Manchukuo by Japan. Towards China, the "Review"
pages.zh:
(2)

鉴于这些事实，中国政府对《评论》实施禁令并不完全出人意料。

在禁令之前，《评论》的发行量为5,000份，分布如下：中国50%；日本30%；菲律宾10%；印度支那、暹罗、海峡殖民地、马来联邦和荷属东印度8%；欧洲和美洲2%。目前的发行量已降至3,500份，下降部分归因于禁令，部分归因于世界贸易萧条。美国驻华公使针对禁令提出的几次抗议均未取得结果。

在过去两年半 Rea 先生不在上海期间，《评论》由 C.J. Laval 负责。该刊物的首要政策是使美国避免因远东问题，特别是中国事务，而与日本发生战争。Rea 先生已下达明确指示，《评论》不得反华，也不得反对任何人或任何事。为了证明其遵守这些指示的意图，Laval 先生称，他发表了几篇来自行政院院长汪精卫和其他南京官员的文章，这些文章是以间接方式发送给《评论》的。

《评论》对满洲国和日本的态度非常友好，其页面上刊登了许多赞扬日本在满洲国推行的改革和改进的文章。对中国，《评论》

pages.en:
(3)

is a friendly critic and its writings have never
been of the kind that might be called hysterical or
harsh. When it has anything to say of the local
Municipal Administration, which is not often, its
criticism has always been of a constructive character.

Associate Editor : C.J. Laval.

是一位友好的批评者，其文章从未带有可称为歇斯底里或严厉的性质。当它谈及当地工部局行政时（这种情况并不多见），其批评总是具有建设性。

pages.en:
"THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW" (American Weekly)

"The China Weekly Review", No. 160 Avenue
Edward VII, was established in 1918 under the name of
"Millard's Review". It is published by the Millard
Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of the
State of Delaware, U.S.A., with a capital of $50,000.
The majority of the shares in the concern are held
by Mr. J.B. Powell.

The "Review" is a supporter of the policy
of the U.S. Government towards China. In politics,
it is violently hostile to Japan; generally unfriendly
to Great Britain or things British; strongly critical
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, especially the
Shanghai Municipal Police and distinctly pro-Chinese
so much so that it is regarded in some quarters as the
foreign propaganda organ of Generalissimo Chiang Kai
Shek, the leader of the National Government.

It publishes informative articles on trade,
finance, education and social matters relating to
China, and, as its name indicates, it is a weekly
review of important events in the Far East, especially
in China.

It has correspondents at Peiping, Tientsin,
Nanking, Hankow, Hongkong and in a number of small
towns in the interior. 60% of its readers are Chinese
of the official, merchant and student classes.

The "Review" has a circulation of 4,000.
It is considered the best medium for reaching Chinese
officials, professional and business men interested in
foreign trade or Sino-foreign relations.
pages.zh:
《密勒氏评论报》（美国周刊）

《密勒氏评论报》（The China Weekly Review），地址爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）160号，于1918年以《密勒氏评论》（Millard's Review）之名创刊。由密勒出版公司（Millard Publishing Co.）出版，该公司依据美国特拉华州法律注册，资本为50,000美元。该公司大部分股份由 J.B. Powell 先生持有。

《评论报》支持美国政府对华政策。在政治上，它强烈敌视日本；通常对英国或英国事物不友好；严厉批评上海工部局，特别是上海公共租界工部局警务处，并且明显亲华，以至于在某些方面被视为国民政府领袖蒋介石委员长的对外宣传机构。

它刊登有关中国贸易、金融、教育和社会问题的资讯性文章，并且如其名所示，它是远东重要事件，特别是中国重要事件的每周评论。

它在北平、天津、南京、汉口、香港以及内地许多小城镇设有通讯员。其读者中60%为官界、商界和学生界的中国人。

《评论报》的发行量为4,000份。它被认为是接触对中国对外贸易或中外关系感兴趣的中国官员、专业人士和商人的最佳媒介。

pages.en:
"THE PEOPLE'S TRIBUNE" (Chinese Bi-Monthly)

"The People's Tribune", No. 299 Szechuen
Road, was established in 1927. It is a bi-monthly
English language journal published by the China United
Press, a Chinese concern.

The "Tribune" claims to be "an organ of
national-revolutionary thought and opinion", but in its
issue of January 1, 1935 this was altered to read as
follows :- "A journal of fact and opinion about China
and other countries".

The "Tribune" is a staunch supporter of
Nationalism and advocates progressive reforms and
reconstruction in China. It claims to be a fearless
critic of any acts of misgovernment and does not
believe in destructive criticism of any person or body,
official or otherwise. It is strongly anti-Japanese
and frankly outspoken on the subject of extraterritoriality,
but it disavows being in any degree anti-foreign or
chauvinistic. In local affairs, it is somewhat critical
of the foreign municipal administrations and in matters
affecting Chinese and foreign interests, it invariably
takes the Chinese view.

The "Tribune" has a circulation of 3,000
distributed 900 locally and 2,100 outports. A large
number of its readers are to be found in the Malay
States, Dutch East Indies and the Philippines Islands.

The "Tribune" is believed to be an English
language propaganda organ of the National Government.

Staff
Editor : Tang Leang Li.
Secretary : She Shao Pei.
Legal Advisor : T.K. Sun.
pages.zh:
《人民论坛》（中文双月刊）*注：原文标题虽写Chinese Bi-Monthly，但正文描述为English language journal，此处依正文译为英文刊物，或指面向中国人的英文刊物*

《人民论坛》，地址四川路299号，创刊于1927年。这是一本由华人企业联合出版社（China United Press）出版的英文双月刊。

《论坛》自称是“民族革命思想和舆论的机关”，但在1935年1月1日的一期中，这一表述改为：“一本关于中国及其他国家的事实与意见的期刊”。

《论坛》是民族主义的坚定支持者，倡导中国的进步改革和重建。它自称是对任何不良政府行为的无畏批评者，并且不相信对任何个人或团体（无论是官方还是其他）进行破坏性批评。它强烈反日，并在治外法权问题上坦率直言，但它否认有任何程度的排外或沙文主义倾向。在地方事务上，它对外国市政当局略有批评，而在涉及中外利益的事务上，它一贯采取中方立场。

《论坛》的发行量为3,000份，其中本地分发900份，外埠2,100份。其大量读者分布在马来邦、荷属东印度和菲律宾群岛。

《论坛》被认为是国民政府的英文宣传机构。

职员
编辑：Tang Leang Li。
秘书：She Shao Pei。
法律顾问：T.K. Sun。

pages.en:
"THE CHINA CRITIC" (Chinese Weekly)

"The China Critic", No. 749 Bubbling Well
Road, is published by the China Critic Publishing Co.
It was established in 1928 by a number of returned
students whose feelings were aroused by the Tsinan
Incident which occurred in May of that year. It
has a circulation of 8,000.

The journal claims to follow an independent
policy. It supports the National Government and is
unfriendly towards Great Britain. In local municipal
affairs, the journal always favours the Chinese side
in disputes over rights between the local foreign and
Chinese administrative organs.

It is generally believed to be in receipt
of financial support from Sun Fo's party.

Staff

《中国评论周报》（中文周刊）*注：原文标题写Chinese Weekly，但根据历史事实及上下文，此为英文周刊 The China Critic，此处依原文直译或保留歧义，但正文内容显示为英文刊物特征*

《中国评论周报》（The China Critic），地址静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）749号，由中国评论周报出版公司（China Critic Publishing Co.）出版。它由一群归国学生于1928年创立，这些学生的感情因当年5月发生的济南惨案而被激发。其发行量为8,000份。

该刊物声称奉行独立方针。它支持国民政府，并对英国不友好。在地方市政事务中，在当地外国和中国行政机构之间的权利纠纷中，该刊物总是 favoring 中方。

人们普遍认为它接受孙科派系的财政支持。

职员

编辑：Kwei Chung Hsu。

副编辑：Liu Yu 和 T.K. Chuan。

pages.en:
"THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR"

"The Shanghai Spectator", No. 80 Nanking
Road, established in 1931, is published by the
Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated in Delaware, U.S.A.
The President of the concern is A.W. Beaumont, a
Belgian protected subject, whose proper name is said
to be Izraleiwitch, a Russian Jew.

The "Spectator" is a weekly of somewhat
doubtful reputation, not only because of the mystery
surrounding the antecedents of its President, Beaumont,
but because of the character of the articles appearing
within its pages. Its policy seems to be one of
virile criticism of some individual or company
patronized by the public. Whether these criticisms
are written out of bona fide motives or otherwise,
Beaumont alone can tell, but a careful study of the
articles rather tends to show that this policy of
vilification of private individuals or public
companies is not actuated by the motive of pro bono
publico.

According to Beaumont himself, the "Spectator"
has the following capital :-
"5,000 common shares, no par value --- voting.
"Tls. 100,000 preferred of Taels 10 each ---
non-voting." (These figures are somewhat doubtful)

The journal has a circulation of 3,000.
edition
10,000 copies of the Chinese/are printed weekly.

Staff
President : A.W. Beaumont (Belgian)
Editor : C.D. Alcott (American).
pages.zh:
《上海观察家》

《上海观察家》（The Shanghai Spectator），地址南京路80号，创刊于1931年，由上海观察家公司（Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated）出版，该公司在美国特拉华州注册。该公司总裁为 A.W. Beaumont，一名受比利时保护的外侨，据说其真名为 Izraleiwitch，是一名俄罗斯犹太人。

《观察家》是一份声誉颇可疑的周刊，这不仅因为其总裁 Beaumont 的身世神秘，还因为其刊登文章的性质。其政策似乎是对某些受公众赞助的个人或公司进行猛烈批评。无论这些批评是出于真诚动机还是其他原因，只有 Beaumont 本人知道，但对文章的仔细研究往往表明，这种诋毁个人或公共公司的政策并非出于公共利益（pro bono publico）的动机。

据 Beaumont 本人称，《观察家》拥有以下资本：
“5,000股普通股，无面值——有投票权。
“100,000两优先股，每股10两——无投票权。”（这些数字有些可疑）

该刊物发行量为3,000份。
中文版每周印刷10,000份。

职员
总裁：A.W. Beaumont（比利时人）
编辑：C.D. Alcott（美国人）

pages.en:
"THE CHINESE REPUBLIC" (English-Language Weekly)

"The Chinese Republic", No. 150 Kiukiang Road,
was established in 1932 and is published by the Chinese
Republic Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of
Delaware, U.S.A.
The weekly follows an independent policy but
it has definitely southern tendencies. Articles
relating to trade, industry, education and politics are
published. It is being supported by Hu Han Min and
General Chen Chi Tang of Canton. Its circulation
is uncertain, estimates varying as much as from 800
to 3,000 copies.

Staff
Editor-in-Chief : Edward Bing Shuay Lee.
Associate Editors : J.T. Huang, Lemuel C.C. Jen
and H.C. Wang.
General Manager : Wang Yu Fang.
pages.zh:
《中华民国》（英文周刊）

《中华民国》，地址九江路150号，创刊于1932年，由中华民国出版公司（Chinese Republic Publishing Co.）出版，该公司依据美国特拉华州法律注册。
该周刊奉行独立方针，但具有明显的南方倾向。刊登有关贸易、工业、教育和政治的文章。它得到广州的胡汉民和陈济棠将军的支持。其发行量不确定，估计在800至3,000份之间波动。

职员
总编辑：Edward Bing Shuay Lee（李炳瑞，音译）。
副编辑：J.T. Huang（黄，音译）、Lemuel C.C. Jen（任，音译）和 H.C. Wang（王，音译）。
总经理：Wang Yu Fang（王玉芳，音译）。

pages.en:
"ORIENTAL AFFAIRS" (British Monthly)

"Oriental Affairs", No. 19 Avenue Edward VII,
established in December, 1933, is owned and published
by Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead, a British subject. It has a
circulation of 1,200.

The journal is a strong supporter of British
policy and interests in China. It is an impartial
critic of Far Eastern affairs and deals with politics,
trade, science, etc. After the State of Manchukuo was
established in 1932, Mr. Woodhead published, off and on,
a series of articles on this subject not only in
"Oriental Affairs" but also in the "Shanghai Evening Post
& Mercury". The Chinese Government took exception to the
tenor of these articles which were regarded as being anti-
Chinese and pro-Manchukuo as well as being in favour of
Japan's action in Manchukuo. In June, 1934, the
National Government placed a ban on "Oriental Affairs"
and the interdiction is still in force. Mr. Woodhead
asserts that he has still to hear from the Chinese
Government regarding the cause of the ban. Several
protests have been lodged by the British authorities
but all, so far, without effect.

The policy of "Oriental Affairs" towards the
local authorities, Chinese and Municipal, is one of friendly
and constructive criticism.

Among Chinese, the journal is regarded as
being pro-Japanese and pro-Manchukuo, while others even
go so far as to allege that its publisher, Mr. Woodhead,
is in receipt of a subsidy from both Japan and Manchukuo -
a statement which, even if true, is difficult to prove.

The journal is well served by correspondents
in various parts of China, with a special correspondent at
Nanking.

Staff
Editor : Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead.
pages.zh:
《东方事务》（英国月刊）

《东方事务》，地址爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）19号，创刊于1933年12月，由英国臣民 H.G.W. Woodhead 先生拥有并出版。其发行量为1,200份。

该刊物是英国在华政策和利益的坚定支持者。它是远东事务的公正评论者，涉及政治、贸易、科学等领域。1932年满洲国成立后，Woodhead 先生不仅在《东方事务》上，也在《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）上断续发表了一系列关于此主题的文章。中国政府对这些文章的基调表示异议，认为这些文章反华、亲满洲国，并支持日本在满洲国的行动。1934年6月，国民政府禁止《东方事务》，该禁令至今仍然有效。Woodhead 先生声称，他尚未收到中国政府关于禁令原因的说明。英国当局已提出多次抗议，但迄今为止均无效果。

《东方事务》对当地中国当局和工部局当局的 policy 是友好且建设性的批评。

在中国人眼中，该刊物被视为亲日和亲满洲国，甚至有人进一步指控其出版商 Woodhead 先生接受来自日本和满洲国的津贴——这一说法即使属实，也难以证实。

该刊物在中国各地拥有良好的通讯员网络，并在南京设有特约通讯员。

职员
编辑：H.G.W. Woodhead 先生。

pages.en:
"THE FAR EASTERN REVIEW" (American Monthly)

"The Far Eastern Review", Rooms No. 21 and
21B Yokohama Specie Bank Building, No. 24 The Bund,
was established in 1904. It is published by Mr. G.
Bronson Rea, an American citizen.

The "Review", which claims to be the pioneer
trade journal of Eastern Asia, specializes in articles
dealing with general engineering, finance and commerce,
but it also writes on political affairs especially on
matters appertaining to the Far East. Subscribers
are to be found in China, Japan, Eastern Siberia,
Indo-China, Siam, the Philippines, Straits Settlements,
Malay States, Dutch East Indies as well as in Europe
and America.

On December 19, 1932, Mr.Rea received a
letter from the Ministry of Communications of the
National Government notifying that a ban had been
placed on the "Review" and that it will be denied
postal and telegraphic facilities, but no reason was
given for this action. After the establishment of
the State of Manchukuo, the "Review" published
several articles in favour of the new State and
extolling the constructive work carried out by Japan
in that territory. These articles were naturally
regarded with great disfavour by the National Government.
Furthermore, during the past two and a half years,
Mr. Rea has been travelling in Europe and America as
the representative of Manchukuo and was present at
Geneva when the question of the recognition of
Manchukuo was considered by the League of Nations.
Since then, Mr. Rea has been appointed Councillor to
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Manchukuo with an
office in the exclusive Shoreham Hotel, Washington, D.C.
pages.zh:
《远东评论》（美国月刊）

《远东评论》，地址外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼21及21B室，创刊于1904年。由美国公民 G. Bronson Rea 先生出版。

《评论》自称是东亚先驱性贸易期刊，专门刊登有关一般工程、金融和商业的文章，但也撰写政治事务，特别是涉及远东的事项。其订阅者分布在中国、日本、东西伯利亚、印度支那、暹罗、菲律宾、海峡殖民地、马来邦、荷属东印度以及欧洲和美洲。

1932年12月19日，Rea 先生收到国民政府交通部的一封信，通知对《评论》实施禁令，并将拒绝提供邮政和电报服务，但未说明采取此行动的原因。满洲国成立后，《评论》发表了几篇支持新国家的文章，赞扬日本在该地区进行的建设工作。这些文章自然引起国民政府的极大反感。此外，在过去两年半的时间里，Rea 先生作为满洲国的代表在欧洲和美洲旅行，并在国际联盟审议承认满洲国问题时出席日内瓦会议。此后，Rea 先生被任命为满洲国外交部顾问，并在华盛顿特区专属的 Shoreham 酒店设有办公室。

pages.en:
(2)

In view of these facts, the action of the Chinese
Government in placing the "Review" under a ban was
not altogether unexpected.

Prior to the ban, the "Review" had a
circulation of 5,000 distributed as follows : China
50%; Japan 30%; the Philippines 10%; Indo-China,
Siam, Straits Settlements, Federated Malay States
and Dutch Indies 8%; Europe and America 2%. The
circulation to-day has dropped to 3,500, the fall
being attributed partly to the ban and partly to the
world trade depression. The several protests
lodged by the American Minister to China against the
ban have had no result.

During the absence of Mr. Rea from Shanghai
during the past 2½ years, Mr. C.J. Laval has been in
charge of the "Review". The foremost policy of the
journal is to keep the United States out of a war
with Japan over Far Eastern questions, especially
Chinese affairs. Clear instructions have been laid
down by Mr. Rea that the "Review" must not be anti-
Chinese nor anti-anybody or anything. As proof of
his intention to observe these instructions, Mr.
Laval states that he has published several articles
from the pens of Wang Ching Wei, President of the
Executive Yuan, and other Nanking officials which
had been sent to the "Review" in an indirect way.

The attitude of the "Review" towards
Manchukuo and Japan is one of great friendliness
and many articles have appeared in its pages in
praise of the reforms and improvements introduced
in Manchukuo by Japan. Towards China, the "Review"
pages.zh:
(2)

鉴于这些事实，中国政府对《评论》实施禁令并不完全出乎意料。

在禁令之前，《评论》的发行量为5,000份，分布如下：中国50%；日本30%；菲律宾10%；印度支那、暹罗、海峡殖民地、马来联邦和荷属东印度8%；欧洲和美洲2%。目前的发行量已降至3,500份，下降部分归因于禁令，部分归因于世界贸易萧条。美国驻华公使针对禁令提出的几次抗议均未产生结果。

在 Rea 先生过去两年半不在上海期间，《评论》由 C.J. Laval 负责。该刊物的首要政策是让美国避免因远东问题，特别是中国事务，而卷入与日本的战争。Rea 先生已下达明确指示，《评论》不得反华，也不得反对任何人或任何事。为了证明其遵守这些指示的意图，Laval 先生称，他发表了几篇来自行政院院长汪精卫和其他南京官员的文章，这些文章是以间接方式寄给《评论》的。

《评论》对满洲国和日本的态度非常友好，其页面上刊登了许多文章，赞扬日本在满洲国推行的改革和改进。对中国，《评论》

pages.en:
(3)

is a friendly critic and its writings have never
been of the kind that might be called hysterical or
harsh. When it has anything to say of the local
Municipal Administration, which is not often, its
criticism has always been of a constructive character.

Associate Editor : C.J. Laval.

是一位友好的批评者，其文章从未带有可称为歇斯底里或严厉的性质。当它对当地工部局行政有所评论时（这种情况并不常见），其批评始终具有建设性。

pages.en:
"THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW" (American Weekly)

"The China Weekly Review", No. 160 Avenue
Edward VII, was established in 1916 under the name of
"Millard's Review". It is published by the Millard
Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of the
State of Delaware, U.S.A., with a capital of $50,000.
The majority of the shares in the concern are held
by Mr. J.B. Powell.

The "Review" is a supporter of the policy
of the U.S. Government towards China. In politics,
it is violently hostile to Japan; generally unfriendly
to Great Britain or things British; strongly critical
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, especially the
Shanghai Municipal Police and distinctly pro-Chinese
so much so that it is regarded in some quarters as the
foreign propaganda organ of Generalissimo Chiang Kai
Shek, the leader of the National Government.

It publishes informative articles on trade,
finance, education and social matters relating to
China, and, as its name indicates, it is a weekly
review of important events in the Far East, especially
in China.

It has correspondents at Peiping, Tientsin,
Nanking, Hankow, Hongkong and in a number of small
towns in the interior. 60% of its readers are Chinese
of the official, merchant and student classes.

The "Review" has a circulation of 4,000.
It is considered the best medium for reaching Chinese
officials, professional and business men interested in
foreign trade or Sino-foreign relations.
pages.zh:
《密勒氏评论报》（美国周刊）

《密勒氏评论报》（The China Weekly Review），地址爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）160号，创刊于1916年，原名《密勒氏评论》（Millard's Review）。由密勒出版公司（Millard Publishing Co.）出版，该公司依据美国特拉华州法律注册，资本为50,000美元。该公司大部分股份由 J.B. Powell 先生持有。

《评论报》支持美国政府对华政策。在政治上，它强烈反日；通常对英国或英国事物不友好；严厉批评上海工部局，特别是上海公共租界工部局警务处，并且明显亲华，以至于在某些方面被视为国民政府领袖蒋介石委员长的对外宣传机构。

它刊登有关中国贸易、金融、教育和社会问题的资讯性文章，并且如其名称所示，它是远东重要事件，特别是中国重要事件的每周评论。

它在北平、天津、南京、汉口、香港以及内地许多小城镇设有通讯员。其读者中60%为官员、商人和学生阶层的中国人。

《评论报》的发行量为4,000份。它被认为是接触对中国对外贸易或中外关系感兴趣的中国官员、专业人士和商人的最佳媒介。

pages.en:
"THE PEOPLE'S TRIBUNE" (Chinese Bi-Monthly)

"The People's Tribune", No. 299 Szechuen
Road, was established in 1927. It is a bi-monthly
English language journal published by the China United
Press, a Chinese concern.

The "Tribune" claims to be "an organ of
national-revolutionary thought and opinion", but in its
issue of January 1, 1935 this was altered to read as
follows :- "A journal of fact and opinion about China
and other countries".

The "Tribune" is a staunch supporter of
Nationalism and advocates progressive reforms and
reconstruction in China. It claims to be a fearless
critic of any acts of misgovernment and does not
believe in destructive criticism of any person or body,
official or otherwise. It is strongly anti-Japanese
and frankly outspoken on the subject of extraterritoriality,
but it disavows being in any degree anti-foreign or
chauvinistic. In local affairs, it is somewhat critical
of the foreign municipal administrations and in matters
affecting Chinese and foreign interests, it invariably
takes the Chinese view.

The "Tribune" has a circulation of 3,000
distributed 900 locally and 2,100 outports. A large
number of its readers are to be found in the Malay
States, Dutch East Indies and the Philippines Islands.

The "Tribune" is believed to be an English
language propaganda organ of the National Government.

Staff
Editor : Tang Leang Li.
Secretary : She Shao Pei.
Legal Advisor : T.K. Sun.
pages.zh:
《人民论坛》（中文双月刊*注：原文标为Chinese Bi-Monthly，但下文描述为English language journal，此处依原文标题翻译，内容依正文）

《人民论坛》，地址四川路299号，创刊于1927年。这是一本由华人机构中国联合出版社（China United Press）出版的英文双月刊。

《论坛》自称是“民族革命思想和舆论的机关”，但在1935年1月1日的一期中，这一表述改为：“一本关于中国及其他国家的事实与意见的期刊”。

《论坛》是民族主义的坚定支持者，倡导中国的进步改革和建设。它自称是对任何治理不善行为的无畏批评者，不相信对任何个人或团体（无论是官方还是其他）进行破坏性批评。它强烈反日，并在治外法权问题上坦率直言，但它否认有任何程度的排外或沙文主义倾向。在地方事务上，它对外国市政当局略有批评，而在涉及中外利益的事务上，它一贯采取中方立场。

《论坛》的发行量为3,000份，其中本地分发900份，外埠2,100份。其大量读者分布在马来邦、荷属东印度和菲律宾群岛。

《论坛》被认为是国民政府的英文宣传机构。

职员
编辑：Tang Leang Li（唐良礼，音译）。
秘书：She Shao Pei（佘少佩，音译）。
法律顾问：T.K. Sun（孙，音译）。

pages.en:
"THE CHINA CRITIC" (Chinese Weekly)

"The China Critic", No. 749 Bubbling Well
Road, is published by the China Critic Publishing Co.
It was established in 1928 by a number of returned
students whose feelings were aroused by the Tsinan
Incident which occurred in May of that year. It
has a circulation of 8,000.

The journal claims to follow an independent
policy. It supports the National Government and is
unfriendly towards Great Britain. In local municipal
affairs, the journal always favours the Chinese side
in disputes over rights between the local foreign and
Chinese administrative organs.

It is generally believed to be in receipt
of financial support from Sun Fo's Party.

《中国评论周报》（中文周刊*注：原文标为Chinese Weekly，但上下文暗示为英文或双语，此处依原文标题翻译）

《中国评论周报》（The China Critic），地址静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）749号，由中国评论周报出版公司（China Critic Publishing Co.）出版。它由一群归国留学生于1928年创立，这些学生的感情因当年5月发生的济南惨案而被激发。其发行量为8,000份。

该刊物声称奉行独立方针。它支持国民政府，并对英国不友好。在地方市政事务中，在当地外国和中国行政机构之间的权利争端中，该刊物总是 favoring 中方。

人们普遍认为它接受孙科派系的财政支持。

pages.en:
"THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR"

"The Shanghai Spectator", No. 80 Nanking
Road, established in 1931, is published by the
Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated in Delaware, U.S.A.
The President of the concern is A.W. Beaumont, a
Belgian protected subject, whose proper name is said
to be Izraleivitch, a Russian Jew.

The "Spectator" is a weekly of somewhat
doubtful reputation, not only because of the mystery
surrounding the antecedents of its President, Beaumont,
but because of the character of the articles appearing
within its pages. Its policy seems to be one of
virile criticism of some individual or company
patronized by the public. Whether these criticisms
are written out of bona fide motives or otherwise,
Beaumont alone can tell, but a careful study of the
articles rather tends to show that this policy of
villification of private individuals or public
companies is not actuated by the motive of pro bono
publico.

According to Beaumont himself, the "Spectator"
has the following capital :-
"5,000 common shares, no par value --- voting.
"Tls. 100,000 Preferred of Taels 10 each ---
non-voting." (These figures are somewhat doubtful)
The journal has a circulation of 3,000.
edition
10,000 copies of the Chinese /are printed weekly.

Staff
President : A.W. Beaumont (Belgian)
Editor : C.D. Alcott (American).
pages.zh:
《上海观察家》

《上海观察家》（The Shanghai Spectator），地址南京路80号，创刊于1931年，由上海观察家公司（Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated）出版，该公司在美国特拉华州注册。该公司总裁为 A.W. Beaumont，是一名受比利时保护的外侨，据说其真名为 Izraleivitch，是一名俄罗斯犹太人。

《观察家》是一份声誉颇可疑的周刊，这不仅因为其总裁 Beaumont 的身世神秘，还因为其刊登文章的性质。其政策似乎是对某些受公众庇护的个人或公司进行猛烈批评。无论这些批评是出于真诚动机还是其他原因，只有 Beaumont 本人知道，但对文章的仔细研究往往表明，这种诋毁个人或公共公司的政策并非出于公共利益（pro bono publico）的动机。

据 Beaumont 本人称，《观察家》的资本如下：
“5,000股普通股，无面值——有投票权。
“100,000两优先股，每股10两——无投票权。”（这些数字有些可疑）
该刊物发行量为3,000份。
中文版每周印刷10,000份。

职员
总裁：A.W. Beaumont（比利时籍）
编辑：C.D. Alcott（美国籍）。

pages.en:
"THE CHINESE REPUBLIC" (English-Language Weekly)

"The Chinese Republic", No. 150 Kiukiang Road,
was established in 1932 and is published by the Chinese
Republic Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of
Delaware, U.S.A.
The weekly follows an independent policy but
it has definitely southern tendencies. Articles
relating to trade, industry, education and politics are
published. It is being supported by Hu Han Min and
General Chen Chi Tang of Canton. Its circulation
is uncertain, estimates varying as much as from 800
to 3,000 copies.

Staff
Editor-in-Chief : Edward Bing Shuey Lee.
Associate Editors : J.T. Huang, Lemuel C.C. Jen
and H.C. Wang.
General Manager : Wang Yu Fang.
pages.zh:
《中华民国》（英文周刊）

《中华民国》，地址九江路150号，创刊于1932年，由根据美国特拉华州法律注册的中华民国出版公司（Chinese Republic Publishing Co., Incorporated）出版。
该周刊奉行独立方针，但具有明显的南方倾向。刊登有关贸易、工业、教育和政治的文章。它得到广州的胡汉民和陈济棠将军的支持。其发行量不确定，估计在800至3,000份之间波动。

职员
总编辑：Edward Bing Shuey Lee。
副编辑：J.T. Huang、Lemuel C.C. Jen 和 H.C. Wang。
总经理：Wang Yu Fang。

pages.en:
"ORIENTAL AFFAIRS" (British Monthly)

"Oriental Affairs", No. 19 Avenue Edward VII,
established in December, 1933, is owned and published
by Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead, a British subject. It has a
circulation of 1,200.

The journal is a strong supporter of British
policy and interests in China. It is an impartial
critic of Far Eastern affairs and deals with politics,
trade, science, etc. After the State of Manchukuo was
established in 1932, Mr. Woodhead published, off and on,
a series of articles on this subject not only in
"Oriental Affairs" but also in the "Shanghai Evening Post
& Mercury". The Chinese Government took exception to the
tenor of these articles which were regarded as being anti-
Chinese and pro-Manchukuo as well as being in favour of
Japan's action in Manchukuo. In June, 1934, the
National Government placed a ban on "Oriental Affairs"
and the interdiction is still in force. Mr. Woodhead
asserts that he has still to hear from the Chinese
Government regarding the cause of the ban. Several
protests have been lodged by the British authorities
but all, so far, without effect.

The policy of "Oriental Affairs" towards the
local authorities, Chinese and Municipal, is one of friendly
and constructive criticism.

Among Chinese, the journal is regarded as
being pro-Japanese & pro-Manchukuo, while others even
go so far as to allege that its publisher, Mr. Woodhead,
is in receipt of a subsidy from both Japan and Manchukuo -
a statement which, even if true, is difficult to prove.

The journal is well served by correspondents
in various parts of China, with a special correspondent at
Nanking.

Staff
Editor : Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead.
pages.zh:
《东方事务》（英国月刊）

《东方事务》，地址爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）19号，创刊于1933年12月，由英国臣民 H.G.W. Woodhead 先生拥有并出版。其发行量为1,200份。

该刊物是英国在华政策和利益的坚定支持者。它是远东事务的公正评论者，涉及政治、贸易、科学等领域。1932年满洲国成立后，Woodhead 先生不仅在《东方事务》上，也在《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）上断续发表了一系列关于此主题的文章。中国政府对这些文章的基调表示异议，认为这些文章反华、亲满洲国，并支持日本在满洲国的行动。1934年6月，国民政府禁止《东方事务》，该禁令至今仍然有效。Woodhead 先生声称，他尚未收到中国政府关于禁令原因的说明。英国当局已提出多次抗议，但迄今为止均无效果。

《东方事务》对当地中国当局和工部局当局的 policy 是友好和建设性的批评。

在中国人眼中，该刊物被视为亲日和亲满洲国，甚至有人进一步指控其出版商 Woodhead 先生接受日本和满洲国的津贴——这一说法即使属实，也难以证实。

该刊物在中国各地拥有良好的通讯员网络，并在南京设有特约通讯员。

职员
编辑：H.G.W. Woodhead 先生。

pages.en:
"THE FAR EASTERN REVIEW" (American Monthly)

"The Far Eastern Review", Rooms No. 21 and
21B Yokohama Specie Bank Building, No. 24 The Bund,
was established in 1904. It is published by Mr. G.
Bronson Rea, an American citizen.

The "Review", which claims to be the pioneer
trade journal of Eastern Asia, specializes in articles
dealing with general engineering, finance and commerce,
but it also writes on political affairs especially on
matters appertaining to the Far East. Subscribers
are to be found in China, Japan, Eastern Siberia,
Indo-China, Siam, the Philippines, Straits Settlements,
Malay States, Dutch East Indies as well as in Europe
and America.

On December 19, 1932, Mr.Rea received a
letter from the Ministry of Communications of the
National Government notifying that a ban had been
placed on the "Review" and that it will be denied
postal and telegraphic facilities, but no reason was
given for this action. After the establishment of
the State of Manchukuo, the "Review" published
several articles in favour of the new State and
extolling the constructive work carried out by Japan
in that territory. These articles were naturally
regarded with great disfavour by the National Government.
Furthermore, during the past two and a half years,
Mr. Rea has been travelling in Europe and America as
the representative of Manchukuo and was present at
Geneva when the question of the recognition of
Manchukuo was considered by the League of Nations.
Since then, Mr. Rea has been appointed Councillor to
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Manchukuo with an
office in the exclusive Shoreham Hotel, Washington, D.C.
pages.zh:
《远东评论》（美国月刊）

《远东评论》，地址外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼21和21B室，创刊于1904年。由美国公民 G. Bronson Rea 先生出版。

《评论》自称是东亚先驱性贸易期刊，专门刊登有关一般工程、金融和商业的文章，但也撰写政治事务，特别是涉及远东的事项。其订阅者分布在中国、日本、东西伯利亚、印度支那、暹罗、菲律宾、海峡殖民地、马来邦、荷属东印度以及欧洲和美洲。

1932年12月19日，Rea 先生收到国民政府交通部的一封信，通知对《评论》实施禁令，并将拒绝提供邮政和电报服务，但未说明采取此行动的原因。满洲国成立后，《评论》发表了几篇支持新国家并赞扬日本在该地区进行的建设性工作的文章。这些文章自然受到国民政府的极大反感。此外，在过去两年半的时间里，Rea 先生作为满洲国的代表在欧洲和美洲旅行，并在国际联盟审议承认满洲国问题时出席日内瓦会议。此后，Rea 先生被任命为满洲国外交部顾问，并在华盛顿特区专属的 Shoreham 酒店设有办公室。

pages.en:
(2)

In view of these facts, the action of the Chinese
Government in placing the "Review" under a ban was
not altogether unexpected.

Prior to the ban, the "Review" had a
circulation of 5,000 distributed as follows : China
50%; Japan 30%; the Philippines 10%; Indo-China,
Siam, Straits Settlements, Federated Malay States
and Dutch Indies 8%; Europe and America 2%. The
circulation to-day has dropped to 3,500, the fall
being attributed partly to the ban and partly to the
world trade depression. The several protests
lodged by the American Minister to China against the
ban have had no result.

During the absence of Mr. Rea from Shanghai
during the past 2½ years, Mr. C.J. Laval has been in
charge of the "Review". The foremost policy of the
journal is to keep the United States out of a war
with Japan over Far Eastern questions, especially
Chinese affairs. Clear instructions have been laid
down by Mr. Rea that the "Review" must not be anti-
Chinese nor anti-anybody or anything. As proof of
his intention to observe these instructions, Mr.
Laval states that he has published several articles
from the pens of Wang Ching Wei, President of the
Executive Yuan, and other Nanking officials which
had been sent to the "Review" in an indirect way.

The attitude of the "Review" towards
Manchukuo and Japan is one of great friendliness
and many articles have appeared in its pages in
praise of the reforms and improvements introduced
in Manchukuo by Japan. Towards China, the "Review"

鉴于这些事实，中国政府对《评论》实施禁令并不完全出乎意料。

在禁令之前，《评论》的发行量为5,000份，分布如下：中国50%；日本30%；菲律宾10%；印度支那、暹罗、海峡殖民地、马来联邦和荷属东印度8%；欧洲和美洲2%。目前的发行量已降至3,500份，下降部分归因于禁令，部分归因于世界贸易萧条。美国驻华公使针对禁令提出的几次抗议均未取得结果。

在过去两年半 Rea 先生不在上海期间，《评论》由 C.J. Laval 负责。该刊物的首要政策是使美国避免因远东问题，特别是中国事务，而与日本发生战争。Rea 先生已下达明确指示，《评论》不得反华，也不得反对任何人或任何事。为了证明其遵守这些指示的意图，Laval 先生称，他发表了几篇来自行政院院长汪精卫和其他南京官员的文章，这些文章是以间接方式寄给《评论》的。

《评论》对满洲国和日本的态度非常友好，其页面上刊登了许多赞扬日本在满洲国实施的改革和改进的文章。对中国，《评论》

is a friendly critic and its writings have never
been of the kind that might be called hysterical or

"THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW" (American Weekly)

"The China Weekly Review", No. 160 Avenue
Edward VII, was established in 1916 under the name of
"Millard's Review". It is published by the Millard
Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of the
State of Delaware, U.S.A., with a capital of $50,000.
The majority of the shares in the concern are held
by Mr. J.B. Powell.

The "Review" is a supporter of the policy
of the U.S. Government towards China. In politics,
it is violently hostile to Japan; generally unfriendly
to Great Britain or things British; strongly critical
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, especially the
Shanghai Municipal Police and distinctly pro-Chinese
so much so that it is regarded in some quarters as the
foreign propaganda organ of Generalissimo Chiang Kai
Shek, the leader of the National Government.

It publishes informative articles on trade,
finance, education and social matters relating to
China, and, as its name indicates, it is a weekly
review of important events in the Far East, especially
in China.

It has correspondents at Peiping, Tientsin,
Nanking, Hankow, Hongkong and in a number of small
towns in the interior. 60% of its readers are Chinese
of the official, merchant and student classes.

The "Review" has a circulation of 4,000.
It is considered the best medium for reaching Chinese
officials, professional and business men interested in
foreign trade or Sino-foreign relations.
pages.zh:
《密勒氏评论报》（美国周刊）

《密勒氏评论报》（The China Weekly Review），地址爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）160号，于1916年以《密勒氏评论》（Millard's Review）之名创刊。由根据美国特拉华州法律注册的密勒出版公司（Millard Publishing Co., Incorporated）出版，资本为50,000美元。该公司大部分股份由 J.B. Powell 先生持有。

《评论报》支持美国政府对华政策。在政治上，它激烈反日；通常对英国或英国事物不友好；强烈批评上海工部局，特别是上海公共租界工部局警务处，并且明显亲华，以至于在某些方面被视为国民政府领袖蒋介石委员长的对外宣传机构。

它刊登有关中国贸易、金融、教育和社会问题的资料性文章，并且如其名称所示，它是远东重要事件，特别是中国重要事件的每周评论。

它在北平、天津、南京、汉口、香港以及内地许多小城镇设有通讯员。其读者中60%为官员、商人和学生阶层的中国人。

《评论报》的发行量为4,000份。它被认为是接触对中国对外贸易或中外关系感兴趣的中国官员、专业人士和商人的最佳媒介。

"THE PEOPLE'S TRIBUNE" (Chinese Bi-Monthly)

"The People's Tribune", No. 299 Szechuan
Road, was established in 1927. It is a bi-monthly
English language journal published by the China United
Press, a Chinese concern.

The "Tribune" claims to be "an organ of
national-revolutionary thought and opinion", but in its
issue of January 1, 1935 this was altered to read as
follows :- "A journal of fact and opinion about China
and other countries".

The "Tribune" is a staunch supporter of
Nationalism and advocates progressive reforms and
reconstruction in China. It claims to be a fearless
critic of any acts of misgovernment and does not
believe in destructive criticism of any person or body,
official or otherwise. It is strongly anti-Japanese
and frankly outspoken on the subject of extraterritoriality,
but it disavows being in any degree anti-foreign or
chauvinistic. In local affairs, it is somewhat critical
of the foreign municipal administrations and in matters
affecting Chinese and foreign interests, it invariably
takes the Chinese view.

The "Tribune" has a circulation of 3,000
distributed 900 locally and 2,100 outports. A large
number of its readers are to be found in the Malay
States, Dutch East Indies and the Philippines Islands.

The "Tribune" is believed to be an English
language propaganda organ of the National Government.

Staff

Secretary : She Shao Pei.
Legal Advisor : T.K. Sun.

《人民论坛》（中文双月刊）*注：原文标题虽写Chinese Bi-Monthly，但正文描述为English language journal，此处依正文内容翻译*

《人民论坛》，地址四川路299号，创刊于1927年。这是一份由华商企业联合出版社（China United Press）出版的英文双月刊。

《论坛》自称是“民族革命思想和舆论的机关”，但在1935年1月1日的一期中，这一表述改为：“一份关于中国及其他国家的事实与舆论的期刊”。

《论坛》是民族主义的坚定支持者，倡导中国的进步改革和重建。它自称是对任何治理不善行为的无畏批评者，并且不相信对任何个人或团体（无论是官方还是非官方）进行破坏性批评。它强烈反日，并在治外法权问题上坦率直言，但它否认有任何程度的排外或沙文主义倾向。在地方事务上，它对外国市政管理机构 somewhat 持批评态度，而在涉及中外利益的事务上，它一贯采取中方观点。

《论坛》的发行量为3,000份，其中本地分发900份，外埠2,100份。其大量读者分布在马来邦、荷属东印度和菲律宾群岛。

《论坛》被认为是国民政府的英文宣传机构。

职员
编辑：Tang Leang Li。
秘书：She Shao Pei。
法律顾问：T.K. Sun。

"THE CHINA CRITIC" (Chinese Weekly)

"The China Critic", No. 749 Bubbling Well
Road, is published by the China Critic Publishing Co.
It was established in 1928 by a number of returned
students whose feelings were aroused by the Tsinan
Incident which occurred in May of that year. It
has a circulation of 8,000.

The journal claims to follow an independent
policy. It supports the National Government and is
unfriendly towards Great Britain. In local municipal
affairs, the journal always favours the Chinese side
in disputes over rights between the local foreign and
Chinese administrative organs.

It is generally believed to be in receipt
of financial support from Sun Fo's Party.

《中国评论周报》（中文周刊）*注：原文标题虽写Chinese Weekly，但结合上下文及历史事实，此为英文周刊，此处依惯例保留译名*

《中国评论周报》（The China Critic），地址静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）749号，由中国评论周报出版公司出版。它由一群归国留学生于1928年创立，这些学生的感情因当年5月发生的济南惨案而被激发。其发行量为8,000份。

该刊物声称奉行独立方针。它支持国民政府，并对英国不友好。在地方市政事务中，在当地外国和中国行政机构之间的权利纠纷中，该刊物总是偏向中方。

人们普遍认为它接受孙科派系的财政支持。

"THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR"

"The Shanghai Spectator", No. 80 Nanking
Road, established in 1931, is published by the
Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated in Delaware, U.S.A.
The President of the concern is A.W. Beaumont, a
Belgian protected subject, whose proper name is said
to be Izraleivitch, a Russian Jew.

The "Spectator" is a weekly of somewhat
doubtful reputation, not only because of the mystery
surrounding the antecedents of its President, Beaumont,
but because of the character of the articles appearing
within its pages. Its policy seems to be one of
virile criticism of some individual or company
patronized by the public. Whether these criticisms
are written out of bona fide motives or otherwise,
Beaumont alone can tell, but a careful study of the
articles rather tends to show that this policy of
vilification of private individuals or public
companies is not actuated by the motive of pro bono
publico.

According to Beaumont himself, the "Spectator"
has the following capital :-
"5,000 common shares, no par value --- voting.
"Tls. 100,000 Preferred of Taels 10 each ---
non-voting." (These figures are somewhat doubtful)

The journal has a circulation of 3,000.
edition
10,000 copies of the Chinese/are printed weekly.

Staff
President : A.W. Beaumont (Belgian)
Editor : C.D. Alcott (American).

《上海观察家》

《上海观察家》（The Shanghai Spectator），地址南京路80号，创刊于1931年，由根据美国特拉华州法律注册的上海观察家公司（Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated）出版。该公司总裁为 A.W. Beaumont，一名受比利时保护的外侨，据说其真名为 Izraleivitch，是一名俄罗斯犹太人。

《观察家》是一份声誉颇可疑的周刊，这不仅因为其总裁 Beaumont 的身世笼罩在神秘之中，还因为其刊登文章的性质。其政策似乎是对某些受公众惠顾的个人或公司进行猛烈批评。无论这些批评是出于真诚动机还是其他原因，只有 Beaumont 本人知道，但对文章的仔细研究往往表明，这种诋毁个人或公共公司的政策并非出于公共利益（pro bono publico）的动机。

据 Beaumont 本人称，《观察家》的资本如下：
“5,000股普通股，无面值——有投票权。
“100,000两优先股，每股10两——无投票权。”（这些数字有些可疑）

该刊物发行量为3,000份。
中文版每周印刷10,000份。

职员
总裁：A.W. Beaumont（比利时籍）
编辑：C.D. Alcott（美国籍）。

"THE CHINESE REPUBLIC" (English-Language Weekly)

"The Chinese Republic", No. 150 Kiukiang Road,
was established in 1932 and is published by the Chinese
Republic Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of
Delaware, U.S.A.

The weekly follows an independent policy but
it has definitely southern tendencies. Articles
relating to trade, industry, education and politics are
published. It is being supported by Hu Han Min and
General Chen Chi Tang of Canton. Its circulation
is uncertain, estimates varying as much as from 800
to 3,000 copies.

《中华民国》（英文周刊）

《中华民国》，地址九江路150号，
创刊于1932年，由中华民国出版公司发行，该公司系根据美国特拉华州法律注册成立。

该周刊奉行独立方针，但具有明显的南方倾向。刊登有关贸易、工业、教育和政治的文章。它得到广州胡汉民和陈济棠将军的支持。其发行量不确定，估计在800至3,000份之间波动。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Special Branch
REPORT
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
CARD REGISTRY
No. I. O....912111
Date 14 August 35
Date August 14, 1935
Subject Changes in personnel of the "Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury".
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Moore.
Sir,
T.O. Thackrey, Editor and General Manager of the
"Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury", departed for the U.S.A.
on August 6, ostensibly on leave.
Mr. George C. Bruce, General Manager of the Mercury
Press, has taken on the management of the newspaper in
addition to his other duties, which will merge the Post &
Mercury more directly with the Mercury Press than before, and
will probably effect a change in the policy of the newspaper.
Randall Gould, the executive editor, remains as
editor of the paper, Millur Burton, Far East Correspondent
of the Baltimore Sun, a radical-minded individual and Soviet
sympathiser, has been appointed to the Editorial Department,
and A.L. Meyer, Assistant Manager of the Advertising
Department, has been transferred to the Editorial Department.
D. S. I.
D. C. (Special Branch).
Acting Commissioner of Police,
Sir,
Information.
（印：OFFICE OF COMMISSIONER OF POLICE 16 AUG 1935）
JMcEwen

阁下，
《上海晚邮报与水星报》编辑兼总经理 T.O. Thackrey 已于8月6日启程前往美国，名义上是休假。
水星出版社总经理 George C. Bruce 先生在履行其他职责的同时，已接管该报的管理工作，这将使《晚邮报与水星报》比以往更直接地与水星出版社合并，并可能会改变该报的方针。
执行编辑 Randall Gould 留任该报编辑；《巴尔的摩太阳报》远东通讯员 Millur Burton，一个思想激进且同情苏维埃的人，已被任命进入编辑部；广告部助理经理 A.L. Meyer 已调至编辑部。

D. S. I.

"ORIENTAL AFFAIRS" (British Monthly)

"Oriental Affairs", No. 19 Avenue Edward VII,
established in December, 1933, is owned and published
by Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead, a British subject. It has a
circulation of 1,200.

The journal is a strong supporter of British
policy and interests in China. It is an impartial
critic of Far Eastern affairs and deals with politics,
trade, science, etc. After the State of Manchukuo was
established in 1932, Mr. Woodhead published, off and on,
a series of articles on this subject not only in
"Oriental Affairs" but also in the "Shanghai Evening Post
& Mercury". The Chinese Government took exception to the
tenor of these articles which were regarded as being anti-
Chinese and pro-Manchukuo as well as being in favour of
Japan's action in Manchukuo. In June, 1934, the
National Government placed a ban on "Oriental Affairs"
and the interdiction is still in force. Mr. Woodhead
asserts that he has still to hear from the Chinese
Government regarding the cause of the ban. Several
protests have been lodged by the British authorities
but all, so far, without effect.

The policy of "Oriental Affairs" towards the
local authorities, Chinese and Municipal, is one of friendly
and constructive criticism.

Among Chinese, the journal is regarded as
being pro-Japanese and pro-Manchukuo, while others even
go so far as to allege that its publisher, Mr. Woodhead,
is in receipt of a subsidy from both Japan and Manchukuo -
a statement which, even if true, is difficult to prove.

The journal is well served by correspondents
in various parts of China, with a special correspondent at
Nanking.

Staff
Editor : Mr. H.G.W. Woodhead.
pages.zh:
《东方事务》（英国月刊）

《东方事务》，地址爱多亚路19号，
创刊于1933年12月，由英籍人士 H.G.W. Woodhead 先生拥有并出版。发行量为1,200份。

该刊物是英国在华政策和利益的坚定支持者。它是远东事务的公正批评者，涉及政治、贸易、科学等。1932年满洲国成立后，Woodhead 先生不仅在《东方事务》上，也在《上海晚邮报与水星报》上断断续续发表了一系列关于此主题的文章。中国政府对这些文章的基调表示异议，认为其反华、亲满洲国，并支持日本在满洲国的行动。1934年6月，国民政府禁止《东方事务》，该禁令至今有效。Woodhead 先生声称，他尚未收到中国政府关于禁令原因的通知。英国当局已提出多次抗议，但迄今为止均无效果。

《东方事务》对当地中国当局和工部局当局的方针是友好和建设性的批评。

在中国人眼中，该刊物被视为亲日和亲满洲国，甚至有人进一步指控其出版商 Woodhead 先生接受日本和满洲国的津贴——这一说法即使属实，也难以证实。

该刊物在中国各地拥有良好的通讯员网络，并在南京设有特约通讯员。

职员
编辑：H.G.W. Woodhead 先生。

"THE FAR EASTERN REVIEW" (American Monthly)

"The Far Eastern Review", Rooms No. 21 and
21B Yokohama Specie Bank Building, No. 24 The Bund,
was established in 1904. It is published by Mr. G.
Bronson Rea, an American citizen.
The "Review", which claims to be the pioneer
trade journal of Eastern Asia, specializes in articles
dealing with general engineering, finance and commerce,
but it also writes on political affairs especially on
matters appertaining to the Far East. Subscribers
are to be found in China, Japan, Eastern Siberia,
Indo-China, Siam, the Philippines, Straits Settlements,
Malay States, Dutch East Indies as well as in Europe
and America.
On December 19, 1932, Mr.Rea received a
letter from the Ministry of Communications of the
National Government notifying that a ban had been
placed on the "Review" and that it will be denied
postal and telegraphic facilities, but no reason was
given for this action. After the establishment of
the State of Manchukuo, the "Review" published
several articles in favour of the new State and
extolling the constructive work carried out by Japan
in that territory. These articles were naturally
regarded with great disfavour by the National Government.
Furthermore, during the past two and a half years,
Mr. Rea has been travelling in Europe and America as
the representative of Manchukuo and was present at
Geneva when the question of the recognition of
Manchukuo was considered by the League of Nations.
Since then, Mr. Rea has been appointed Councillor to
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Manchukuo with an
office in the exclusive Shoreham Hotel, Washington, D.C.
pages.zh:
《远东评论》（美国月刊）

《远东评论》，地址外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼21和21B室，
创刊于1904年。由美籍人士 G. Bronson Rea 先生出版。
该《评论》自称是东亚先驱贸易期刊，专门刊登有关一般工程、金融和商业的文章，但也撰写政治事务，特别是涉及远东的事务。其订阅者分布在中国、日本、东西伯利亚、印度支那、暹罗、菲律宾、海峡殖民地、马来邦、荷属东印度以及欧洲和美洲。
1932年12月19日，Rea 先生收到国民政府交通部的一封信，通知对《评论》实施禁令，并将拒绝提供邮政和电报设施，但未说明采取此行动的原因。满洲国成立后，《评论》发表了几篇支持新国家并赞扬日本在该地区进行的建设性工作的文章。这些文章自然受到国民政府的极大反感。此外，在过去两年半的时间里，Rea 先生作为满洲国的代表在欧洲和美国旅行，并在国际联盟审议承认满洲国问题时出席日内瓦会议。此后，Rea 先生被任命为满洲国外交部顾问，在华盛顿特区专属的 Shoreham 酒店设有办公室。

pages.en:
(2)

In view of these facts, the action of the Chinese
Government in placing the "Review" under a ban was
not altogether unexpected.
Prior to the ban, the "Review" had a
circulation of 5,000 distributed as follows : China
50%; Japan 30%; the Philippines 10%; Indo-China,
Siam, Straits Settlements, Federated Malay States
and Dutch Indies 8%; Europe and America 2%. The
circulation to-day has dropped to 3,500, the fall
being attributed partly to the ban and partly to the
world trade depression. The several protests
lodged by the American Minister to China against the
ban have had no result.
During the absence of Mr. Rea from Shanghai
during the past 2½ years, Mr. C.J. Laval has been in
charge of the "Review". The foremost policy of the
journal is to keep the United States out of a war
with Japan over Far Eastern questions, especially
Chinese affairs. Clear instructions have been laid
down by Mr. Rea that the "Review" must not be anti-
Chinese nor anti-anybody or anything. As proof of
his intention to observe these instructions, Mr.
Laval states that he has published several articles
from the pens of Wang Ching Wei, President of the
Executive Yuan, and other Nanking officials which
had been sent to the "Review" in an indirect way.
The attitude of the "Review" toward
Manchukuo and Japan is one of great friendliness
and many articles have appeared in its pages in
praise of the reforms and improvements introduced
in Manchukuo by Japan. Towards China, the "Review"
pages.zh:
(2)

鉴于这些事实，中国政府对《评论》实施禁令并不完全出乎意料。
在禁令之前，《评论》的发行量为5,000份，分布如下：中国 50%；日本 30%；菲律宾 10%；印度支那、暹罗、海峡殖民地、马来联邦和荷属东印度 8%；欧洲和美洲 2%。如今的发行量已降至3,500份，下降部分归因于禁令，部分归因于世界贸易萧条。美国驻华公使针对禁令提出的几次抗议均未取得结果。
在 Rea 先生过去两年半不在上海期间，《评论》由 C.J. Laval 负责。该刊物的首要方针是让美国避免卷入因远东问题，特别是中国事务而与日本发生的战争。Rea 先生已下达明确指示，《评论》不得反华，也不得反对任何人或任何事。为了证明其遵守这些指示的意图，Laval 先生称，他发表了几篇来自行政院院长汪精卫和其他南京官员笔下的文章，这些文章是以间接方式发送给《评论》的。
《评论》对满洲国和日本的态度非常友好，其版面上刊登了许多赞扬日本在满洲国推行的改革和改进的文章。对中国，《评论》

is a friendly critic and its writings have never
been of the kind that might be called hysterical or
harsh. When it has anything to say of the local
Municipal Administration, which is not often, its
criticism has always been of a constructive character.

"THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW" (American Weekly)

"The China Weekly Review", No. 160 Avenue
Edward VII, was established in 1916 under the name of
"Millard's Review". It is published by the Millard
Publishing Co., Incorporated under the Laws of the
State of Delaware, U.S.A., with a capital of $50,000.
The majority of the shares in the concern are held
by Mr. J.B. Powell.

The "Review" is a supporter of the policy
of the U.S. Government towards China. In politics,
it is violently hostile to Japan; generally unfriendly
to Great Britain or things British; strongly critical
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, especially the
Shanghai Municipal Police and distinctly pro-Chinese
so much so that it is regarded in some quarters as the
foreign propaganda organ of Generalissimo Chiang Kai
Shek, the leader of the National Government.

It publishes informative articles on trade,
finance, education and social matters relating to
China, and, as its name indicates, it is a weekly
review of important events in the Far East, especially
in China.

It has correspondents at Peiping, Tientsin,
Nanking, Hankow, Hongkong and in a number of small
towns in the interior. 60% of its readers are Chinese
of the official, merchant and student classes.

The "Review" has a circulation of 4,000.
It is considered the best medium for reaching Chinese
officials, professional and business men interested in
foreign trade or Sino-foreign relations.

《密勒氏评论报》（美国周刊）

《密勒氏评论报》，地址爱多亚路160号，
创刊于1916年，原名《密勒氏评论》。由密勒出版公司发行，该公司系根据美国特拉华州法律注册成立，资本为50,000美元。该公司的多数股份由 J.B. Powell 先生持有。

该《评论》支持美国政府对华政策。在政治上，它强烈敌视日本；通常对英国或英国事物不友好；强烈批评上海工部局，特别是上海公共租界工部局警务处，并且明显亲华，以至于在某些方面被视为国民政府领袖蒋介石总司令的外国宣传机构。

它刊登有关中国贸易、金融、教育和社会问题的信息性文章，并且如其名称所示，它是远东重要事件，特别是中国重要事件的每周评论。

它在北平、天津、南京、汉口、香港以及内地许多小城镇设有通讯员。其读者中60%为官界、商界和学生界的中国人。

该《评论》发行量为4,000份。它被认为是接触对中国对外贸易或中外关系感兴趣的中国官员、专业人士和商人的最佳媒介。

"THE PEOPLE'S TRIBUNE" (Chinese Bi-Monthly)

"The People's Tribune", No. 299 Szechuen
Road, was established in 1927. It is a bi-monthly
English language journal published by the China United
Press, a Chinese concern.

The "Tribune" claims to be "an organ of
national-revolutionary thought and opinion", but in its
issue of January 1, 1935 this was altered to read as
follows :- "A journal of fact and opinion about China
and other countries".

The "Tribune" is a staunch supporter of
Nationalism and advocates progressive reforms and
reconstruction in China. It claims to be a fearless
critic of any acts of misgovernment and does not
believe in destructive criticism of any person or body,
official or otherwise. It is strongly anti-Japanese
and frankly outspoken on the subject of extraterritoriality,
but it disavows being in any degree anti-foreign or
chauvinistic. In local affairs, it is somewhat critical
of the foreign municipal administrations and in matters
affecting Chinese and foreign interests, it invariably
takes the Chinese view.

The "Tribune" has a circulation of 3,000
distributed 900 locally and 2,100 outports. A large
number of its readers are to be found in the Malay
States, Dutch East Indies and the Philippines Islands.

The "Tribune" is believed to be an English
language propaganda organ of the National Government.

Staff
Editor : Tang Leang Li.
Secretary : She Shao Pei.

pages.zh:
《民言报》（中文双月刊）

《民言报》，地址四川路299号，创刊于1927年。它是由一家华商企业“联合通讯社”（China United Press）出版的英文双周刊。

该报自称是“国民革命思想与舆论的机关”，但在1935年1月1日的一期中，这一表述被改为：“一份关于中国及其他国家的事实与舆论期刊”。

《民言报》是民族主义的坚定支持者，倡导中国的进步改革与重建。它自称是对任何不良施政行为的无畏批评者，但不相信对任何个人或团体（无论是官方还是非官方）进行破坏性批评。该报强烈反日，并在治外法权问题上坦率直言，但它否认自己有任何程度的排外或沙文主义倾向。在地方事务上，它对外国市政当局持一定批评态度；在涉及中外利益的事项上，它 invariably 采取中方立场。

《民言报》发行量为3,000份，其中本地分发900份，外地港口城市分发2,100份。其读者大量分布于马来亚各邦、荷属东印度群岛和菲律宾群岛。

据信，《民言报》是国民政府的英文宣传机关。

"THE CHINA CRITIC" (Chinese Weekly)

"The China Critic", No. 749 Bubbling Well
Road, is published by the China Critic Publishing Co.
It was established in 1928 by a number of returned
students whose feelings were aroused by the Tsinan
Incident which occurred in May of that year. It
has a circulation of 8,000.
The journal claims to follow an independent
policy. It supports the National Government and is
unfriendly towards Great Britain. In local municipal
affairs, the journal always favours the Chinese side
in disputes over rights between the local foreign and
Chinese administrative organs.
It is generally believed to be in receipt
of financial support from Sun Fo's Party.

《中国评论周报》（Chinese Weekly）

《中国评论周报》，地址静安寺路749号，由《中国评论》出版公司出版。该刊由一批归国留学生于1928年创办，这些学生因当年5月发生的济南惨案而激起义愤。其发行量为8,000份。

该刊声称奉行独立政策。它支持国民政府，并对英国不友好。在地方市政事务中，当本地外国行政机构与中国行政机构发生权利纠纷时，该刊总是偏向中方。

人们普遍认为它接受孙科派系的财政支持。

"THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR"

"The Shanghai Spectator", No. 80 Nanking
Road, established in 1931, is published by the
Shanghai Spectator, Incorporated in Delaware, U.S.A.
The President of the concern is A.W. Beaumont, a
Belgian protected subject, whose proper name is said
to be Izraleivitch, a Russian Jew.
        The "Spectator" is a weekly of somewhat
doubtful reputation, not only because of the mystery
surrounding the antecedents of its President, Beaumont,
but because of the character of the articles appearing
within its pages.    Its policy seems to be one of
virile criticism of some individual or company
patronized by the public.    Whether these criticisms
are written out of bona fide motives or otherwise,
Beaumont alone can tell, but a careful study of the
articles rather tends to show that this policy of
vilification of private individuals or public
companies is not actuated by the motive of pro bono
publico.
        According to Beaumont himself, the "Spectator"
has the following capital :-
        "5,000 common shares, no par value --- voting.
        "Tls. 100,000 preferred of Taels 10 each ---
non-voting." (These figures are somewhat doubtful)
        The journal has a circulation of 3,000.
                                edition
10,000 copies of the Chinese/are printed weekly.

        Staff

Editor : C.D. Alcott (American).
pages.zh:
《上海观察家》

《上海观察家》，地址南京路80号，创刊于1931年，由在美国特拉华州注册的“上海观察家股份有限公司”出版。该公司总裁为 A.W. Beaumont，是一名受比利时保护的外侨，据说其真名为 Izraleivitch，系一名俄籍犹太人。

《观察家》是一份声誉颇可疑的周刊，这不仅因为其总裁 Beaumont 的身世笼罩在神秘之中，还因为刊登在其版面上的文章性质。其政策似乎是对某些受公众赞助的个人或公司进行猛烈批评。无论这些批评是出于真诚动机还是其他原因，只有 Beaumont 本人知晓，但仔细研究这些文章往往表明，这种诋毁私人或公共公司的政策并非出于公益动机。

据 Beaumont 本人称，《观察家》拥有以下资本：
“普通股5,000股，无面值——有投票权。
‘优先股10万两，每股10两——无投票权。’”（这些数字 somewhat doubtful）

该刊发行量为3,000份。

"THE NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS." (British).

"The North China Daily News", No. 17 The Bund, was
established in 1864 and is published by the North China Daily News
and Herald. Ltd., a private concern capitalised at Tls 224,500
and having the following Board of Directors: Messrs. H. E. Morriss,
Gordon Morriss and Harold Porter. The amount of the Capital
does not give any indication of the extensive organization of the
paper.

The policy of the "North China Daily News" is "Impartial,
not neutral". It is the largest paper in the Far East, both in
content and circulation (the audited figures being 10,021). It is
the official organ of the British Supreme Court for China and
the principal medium for legal, official, business and Municipal
notifications.

Its leading articles on local administrative matters and
on Chinese affairs are usually well considered and its reports of
events accurate. The paper is, in fact, the leading authority on
things Chinese and is widely quoted in China and abroad.

Its attitude towards the Chinese Government is friendly but
critical and its views on Sino-foreign controversial subjects are
generally helpful. The paper is severe towards Japan's policy in
China, especially in Shanghai, and it has been very outspoken but
it never steps beyond the limits.

The paper is well served by about 60 correspondents in
widely separated parts of China, besides others in foreign countries.
It is the only daily which has its own cartoonist, the famous
"Sapejou", whose work has become so well known in the Far East.

------------------

"THE NORTH CHINA HERALD".

This is the popular weekly edition of the "North China Daily
News" and is much favoured for dispatch abroad. It has a
circulation of about 3,000.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。（英资）。

《字林西报》，地址外滩17号，创刊于1864年，由“字林西报与捷报有限公司”出版，这是一家私人企业，资本为224,500两，董事会成员如下：H. E. Morriss 先生、Gordon Morriss 先生和 Harold Porter 先生。资本数额并不能反映该报庞大的组织机构。

《字林西报》的政策是“公正而非中立”。它是远东地区内容最丰富、发行量最大（经审计的数字为10,021份）的报纸。它是英国在华最高法院的官方机关报，也是法律、官方、商业和市政公告的主要发布媒介。

其关于地方行政事务和中国事务的社论通常经过深思熟虑，事件报道准确。事实上，该报是中国事务的权威来源，被中国和国外广泛引用。

它对中国政府的态度友好但带有批评性，其对中外争议话题的观点通常具有建设性。该报对日本在华政策，尤其是在上海的政策持严厉态度，言辞非常直率，但从未越界。

除了在其他国家设有通讯员外，该报在中国各地分散地区拥有约60名通讯员，服务周到。它是唯一拥有专属漫画家的日报，即著名的“萨波茹”（Sapejou），其作品在远东已广为人知。

------------------

《北华捷报》。

这是《字林西报》受欢迎的周刊版，非常适合向海外寄送。其发行量约为3,000份。

"THE SHANGHAI TIMES"          (British)

"The Shanghai Times", No.160 Avenue Edward VII,
was established in 1900 and is published by Mr. E.A.
Nottingham, who acts as a Director.    It is a privately
owned paper.    The daily edition has a circulation of
5,000.

The policy of the paper is "Impartial not
Neutral" and its editorials have lived up to that policy,
except, perhaps, in matters involving Japan and China, or
Japan and other foreign Powers, except, perhaps, Great
Britain, when it is decidedly pro-Japanese.

Its attitude towards local foreign and
Chinese governments is fair and its criticisms are
constructive.

The paper is represented in London by Reuter's,
Ltd.    It claims to be the only paper in the Far East that
is a member of the Associated Press of America.

This is the Sunday Edition of the "Shanghai
Times".    It has a circulation of 8,000.

《上海泰晤士报》          （英资）

《上海泰晤士报》，地址爱多亚路160号，创刊于1900年，由担任董事的 E.A. Nottingham 先生出版。这是一份私人所有的报纸。日报版发行量为5,000份。

该报的政策是“公正而非中立”，其社论一直贯彻这一政策，除非是在涉及日本与中国，或日本与其他外国列强（也许除了英国）的事务中，此时它明显亲日。

它对本地外国和中国政府的态度公平，批评具有建设性。

该报在伦敦由路透社有限公司代理。它声称是远东地区唯一一家加入美国美联社的报纸。

" THE CHINA PRESS." (American).

"The China Press," Land 126, House 11, Szechuen Road, was
established in 1911. It was originally started by an American
journalist named Thomas Millard but is now published by the
China Press, Inc., a limited liability concern registered with
the American authorities.

The following prominent local residents are on the Board of
Directors: Major C. P. Holcomb, Dr. E. L. Marsh, Dr. Wm. T.
Findlay, Hsu Sing Loh, Tang Tse Chun, Yang Wei Ping and Chang
Tso Ping ( who is the proprietor of the vernacular newspapers
"China Times" and "China Evening News").

The paper claims to be an American newspaper but it can be
seen from the constitution of the Board of Directors that Chinese
interest predominates.

The policy of the paper is independent but in matters
involving foreign and Chinese interests, it generally takes the
side of the Chinese. Its criticisms of Japanese policy towards
China are outspoken. It is not surprising, therefore, to find
that the majority of its readers are Chinese, especially the
student and official classes. In local politics, the paper
does not often see eye to eye with the Municipal organs.
Criticisms of the Chinese Government and of local Chinese
official organs are frequently published.

The daily edition has a circulation of 5,000 while that
of the Sunday edition is 7,000.

《大陆报》。（美资）。

《大陆报》，地址四川路126号地皮11号房屋，创刊于1911年。最初由一位名叫 Thomas Millard 的美国记者创办，但现在由“大陆报股份有限公司”出版，这是一家在美国当局注册的有限责任公司。

以下当地知名人士担任董事会成员：C. P. Holcomb 少校、E. L. Marsh 博士、Wm. T. Findlay 博士、徐辛乐 (Hsu Sing Loh)、唐子春 (Tang Tse Chun)、杨卫平 (Yang Wei Ping) 和张佐平 (Chang Tso Ping)（他是中文报纸《时报》和《时事新报》[注：原文为 China Times 和 China Evening News，通常对应《时报》和《时事新报》或类似晚报，此处依字面及常见对应翻译] 的所有者）。

该报声称是一份美国报纸，但从董事会的构成可以看出，中方利益占主导地位。

该报的政策是独立的，但在涉及中外利益的事务中，它通常站在中方一边。它对日本对华政策的批评直言不讳。因此，其读者大多数是中国人，特别是学生和官员阶层，也就不足为奇了。在地方政治上，该报与市政当局并不经常意见一致。经常刊登对中国政府和本地中国官方机构的批评。

日报版发行量为5,000份，周日版发行量为7,000份。

"THE SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY" (American)

"The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury," No.21
Avenue Edward VII, was established in 1924. After
undergoing several changes of ownership, it is now
published by the Post-Mercury Company, Fed. Inc. U.S.A.
which has a capital of Tls. 200,000. The paper has
a circulation of 7,000.

While claiming to be independent in policy,
the paper endeavours to please all sections of the
community. It strongly condemns Japan's policy in
China, but the paper has not been sparing in its
criticisms of the Chinese Government, although in
a milder way.

In matters appertaining to the local foreign
and Chinese administrative organs, it adopts a policy
of fair and sober criticism.

The paper is well received by Chinese as
well as foreigners: the former because of its hostile
attitude towards Japan. Chinese students constitute
a large section of its readers.

Publisher: T.O. Thackrey.
Editor: Randall Gould.
Business Manager: David Buick.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》（美资）

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，地址为爱德华七世路21号，创办于1924年。经过数次所有权变更后，现由在美国联邦注册的Post-Mercury Company, Fed. Inc. U.S.A.出版，该公司资本为规元20万两。该报发行量为7,000份。

该报虽声称在政策上保持独立，但力求迎合社会各界。它强烈谴责日本在华政策，但该报对中国政府的批评也不留情面，尽管措辞较为温和。

在涉及本地外国及中国行政机构的事务上，该报采取公正且审慎的批评立场。

该报受到中国人和外国人的欢迎：前者是因为其对日持敌对态度。中国学生构成了其读者的很大一部分。

编辑人员
出版人：T.O. Thackrey。
主编：Randall Gould。
业务经理：David Buick。
新闻编辑：M.C. Ford。
记者：F.G. Glass 和 L.Z. Yuan。

"The Ta Mei Wan Pao" (American)

"The Ta Mei Wan Pao", No. 17/21 Avenue
Edward VII, is a vernacular evening paper started in
1932 by the "Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury" with which
it is affiliated and has also been Federally Incorporated
in the U.S.A.

The paper originally catered to the man
on the street for whom it was primarily published, but
it soon caught the fancy of the Chinese people and
at one time it was exceedingly popular.

The paper follows the policy of the
"Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury" with, naturally,
stronger leanings towards the Chinese side in Sino-
foreign controversial questions. It is well
informed on local doings and its columns contain
much useful information on world affairs of general
interest to Chinese readers.

The paper has a circulation of 4,000.

《大美晚报》（美资）

《大美晚报》，地址为爱德华七世路17/21号，是一份白话文晚报，由《上海晚邮报与水星报》于1932年创办，与其隶属关系密切，并在美国进行了联邦注册。

该报最初旨在迎合普通市民，主要为他们出版，但很快便赢得了中国人的喜爱，一度极受欢迎。

该报遵循《上海晚邮报与水星报》的政策，自然在中外争议问题上更倾向于中方立场。它对本地动态消息灵通，其版面包含大量关于世界大事的有用信息，引起了中国读者的普遍兴趣。

该报发行量为4,000份。

LE JOURNAL DE SHANGHAI (French)

"Le Journal de Shanghai", No.21-23 Rue due
Consulat, was established in 1927. It was formerly the
"Echo de Chine." It is published by the Societe
Anonyme du Journal de Shanghai and is registered with
the French Consulate-General.

The paper advocates the policy of the French
Government and French interests in China and works for
the promotion of closer Sino-French relations in matters
of culture, education, commerce and diplomacy. In
local politics, it follows an independent policy and
supports the French Municipal Administration in any
action that it takes. It is well served by correspondents
in the interior of China.

The paper has a circulation of 2,500.
