《上海日报》（法资）

《上海日报》（Le Journal de Shanghai），地址为领事馆路21-23号，创办于1927年。其前身为《中国回声报》（Echo de Chine）。由上海日报股份有限公司（Societe Anonyme du Journal de Shanghai）出版，并在法国总领事馆注册。

该报倡导法国政府政策及法国在华利益，致力于在文化、教育、商业和外交事务上促进中法关系的紧密化。在本地政治方面，它奉行独立政策，并支持法国公董局采取的任何行动。它在中国内地拥有良好的通讯员网络。

"THE SHANGHAI NICHI-NICHI"    (Japanese)

"The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi," No.456 Chapoo
Road, was established in 1914.    It is published
by the Shanghai Nichi-Nichi Shimbun, Ltd. with
a capital of $60,000.
    The paper is a strong supporter of Japanese
policy in China.    It pays close attention to
Chinese affairs and its columns contain more
matter relating to Chinese doings than any
other Japanese paper in Shanghai.
    Its attitude towards the local Municipal
Administration is impartial, except in matters
affecting Japanese interests.    The paper has a
circulation of 3,000.

        Editorial Staff
Director:       K. Miyaji
General Manager & Chief Editor: G. Ishikawa
Reporters:      Y. Watanabe, G. Itoh, T. Kabashima
                and T. Suyenaga.
pages.zh:
《上海日日新闻》（日资）

《上海日日新闻》（The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi），地址为乍浦路456号，创办于1914年。由上海日日新闻有限公司出版，资本为60,000美元。

该报是日本在华政策的坚定支持者。它密切关注中国事务，其版面中关于中国动态的内容比上海其他任何日文报纸都多。

除涉及日本利益的事项外，该报对本地工部局的态度是公正的。该报发行量为3,000份。

编辑人员
董事：K. Miyaji
总经理兼总编辑：G. Ishikawa
记者：Y. Watanabe, G. Itoh, T. Kabashima 和 T. Suyenaga。

pages.en:
"THE SHANGHAI MAINICHI" (Japanese)

"The Shanghai Mainichi," no. 1 Thorne Road, was
established in 1903. It is published by the Shanghai
Mainichi Shimbun Ltd. with a capital of ¥70,000.

The paper is a staunch supporter of the Japanese
Government's policy in China. In local politics,
it sides with the Municipal Administration against
the Chinese Authorities, but against the Council in
municipal affairs affecting Japanese interests.

The paper has a circulation of 76,000.

Editorial Staff

Director & Chief Editor: S. Fukumachi.

Reporters: Y. Torisu, H. Oki, M. Tagami, J. Tashiro,
I. Takahashi, H. Sonoda, I. Nagosu,
M. Nakamura, D. Funakoshi, M. Sato,
O. Miyaki and S. Shimamura.

《上海每日新闻》（日资）

《上海每日新闻》（The Shanghai Mainichi），地址为汤姆生路1号，创办于1903年。由上海每日新闻有限公司出版，资本为70,000日元。

该报是日本政府在华政策的坚定支持者。在本地政治中，它在对抗中国当局时站在工部局一边，但在涉及日本利益的市政事务中则反对工部局董事会。

该报发行量为76,000份。

董事兼总编辑：S. Fukumachi。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI NIPPO* (JAPANESE)

"The Shanghai Nippo* No. 3/4
Barchet Road, was established in 1906. It is owned
by Mr. H. Hata and has a Capital of $50,000.
The paper is a strong supporter of
the local Japanese Consulate and the policy of the
Japanese government in China. It publishes much news
on official doings.
The paper has a circulation of 3,000.

Editorial Staff
Editor: K. Goto
Reporters: K. Yoshida, S. Hidaka, G. Miyake,

pages.zh:
《上海新报》*（日资）

《上海新报》*（The Shanghai Nippo*），地址为百老汇路3/4号，创办于1906年。由H. Hata先生所有，资本为50,000美元。

该报是本地日本领事馆及日本政府在华政策的坚定支持者。它刊登大量关于官方动态的新闻。

该报发行量为3,000份。

编辑人员
编辑：K. Goto
记者：K. Yoshida, S. Hidaka, G. Miyake, S. Moroishi。

pages.en:
The Shun Pao (申报), established in 1872,
is the oldest Chinese daily newspaper in Shanghai.
It is usually pro-Nanking but occasionally criticizes
the government and may be considered independent, as
it is not subsidized by the government or any particular
group. It is anti-Japanese but adopts an independent
attitude towards the policies of Great Britain and the
U.S.A. except that in all disputes between China and
Britain or China and the U.S.A., the Chinese point of
view is naturally emphasized. It is generally
considered to be authoritative and fair. The capital
of the paper is given at $1,500,000. 100,000
copies used to be printed daily but since the Sino-
Japanese hostilities, only 80,000 copies have been
printed. Chang Yun Woo (張和) is the chief
editor. Dr. Mr. Ying Liang (馬蔭良) is the
manager. After the murder of Sze Liang Zay(史量才),
the proprietor and managing-director, the family of
the victim has asked Chen Ching Han (陳景韓), who
was formerly an editor of the Shun Pao and is now an
advisor to General Chiang Kai Shek, to act as General
Manager of the paper, but the latter has not yet
accepted the offer.
pages.zh: 《申报》，创办于1872年，是上海历史最悠久的中文日报。它通常亲南京政府，但偶尔也会批评政府，可被视为独立报纸，因为它不接受政府或任何特定团体的资助。它反日，但对英国和美国的政策采取独立态度，只不过在中英或中美的一切争端中，自然强调中方观点。它通常被认为具有权威性和公正性。该报资本据称为1,500,000美元。过去每日印刷100,000份，但自中日敌对行动开始以来，仅印刷80,000份。张蕴和（Chang Yun Woo）是总编辑。马荫良（Ying Liang）博士是经理。在业主兼总经理史量才（Sze Liang Zay）被谋杀后，受害者家属曾请求曾任《申报》编辑、现任蒋介石将军顾问的陈景韩（Chen Ching Han）担任该报总经理，但后者尚未接受此提议。

pages.en:
The Sin Wan Pao (新闻报) is the most
influential Chinese daily newspaper in Shanghai.
It is regarded by the Chinese community as an
independent organ chiefly devoted to commerce and its
revenue is chiefly derived from advertisements. It is
anti-Japanese, but its attitude towards Britain and
the U.S.A. is for the most part impartial. It is
considered fair, authoritative and conservative.
Li Hao Zeu (李浩然) is the editor-in-chief. The
capital of this paper is given as $1,200,000 and
most of the shares are in the hands of the late Sze
Liang Zay family. About 120,000 copies are printed
daily of which 40,000 copies are distributed in
Shanghai. An evening edition of 10,000 copies is
also printed, but this is not in great demand and
free copies are distributed to the leading Chinese
hotels, etc.
pages.zh: 《新闻报》是上海最具影响力的中文日报。华人社区将其视为一家主要致力于商业的独立机构，其收入主要来自广告。它反日，但对英国和美国的态度大部分时间是公正的。它被认为公正、具有权威性且保守。李浩然（Li Hao Zeu）是总编辑。该报资本据称为1,200,000美元，大部分股份掌握在已故史量才（Sze Liang Zay）家族手中。每日印刷约120,000份，其中40,000份在上海分发。还印刷一份10,000份的晚报，但需求量不大，免费分发给各大华资酒店等。

pages.en:
The Shih Shih Hsin Pao (China Times)
(时事新报) is regarded by the Chinese community
as an independent progressive newspaper. It is anti-
Japanese and anti-foreign, not specifically anti-
Britain or anti-U.S.A. It is not considered
authoritative but sensational and mildly radical,
though fair in most of its articles. The editor
is Pen Kung Pi (潘公), a well known journalist.
The capital of the paper is $300,000 and the shares
are owned by a syndicate formed in 1930 by Chang
Tso Ping (張竹平) who is the Managing-Director
of the "China Press", a foreign daily newspaper and
the "China Evening News", a Chirese evening newspaper,
besides being Managing-Director of the Shih Shih Hsin
Pao. Dr. Wellington Koo (Chinese Minister to
France) is a member of the financial syndicate.
20,000 copies are printed daily.
pages.zh: 《时事新报》（China Times）被华人社区视为一家独立的进步报纸。它反日且排外，并非特指反英或反美。它不被认为具有权威性，而是耸人听闻且略带激进色彩，尽管其大多数文章是公正的。编辑是著名记者潘公弼（Pen Kung Pi）。该报资本为300,000美元，股份由一个辛迪加持有，该辛迪加由张竹平（Chang Tso Ping）于1930年成立，张竹平除了担任《时事新报》总经理外，还是外文日报《大陆报》（China Press）和中文晚报《大晚报》（China Evening News）的总经理。顾维钧博士（中国驻法国公使）是该金融辛迪加的成员。每日印刷20,000份。

pages.en:
The "Eastern Times" (時報), published at
No.194 Foochow Road, established in 1904, is a daily
newspaper. It has a sales office at No.302 Hankow Road.
The paper prints its articles in large type and does not
print many advertisements, although advertisement rates
form the chief source of the revenue of all newspapers.
The capital of the paper is $500,000. Waung Pah Wei
(黃伯惠), a returned student, who is a millionaire
and real estate owner, is the proprietor. Mr. Waung,
who is regarded by local journalists as an eccentric person,
often personally attends to the mechanical repairs of a
five-colour printing machine, which he bought for
Gold $150,000.
This paper publishes about 80,000 copies daily
with an evening edition of 30,000 copies. It is an
independent publishing organ but it has never published
editorials or brief comments. It is devoted to social
and sporting news only. This paper is popular among
students.
The administration of this paper is different
to all other leading newspapers. It has neither Editor-
in-Chief nor Manager. All reading matter is classified
into different sections and each section has an editor.
Koo Tse Oen (顧芷弇) is responsible for the Local
News Section while Tsai Yuin Soo (蔡行素) is Editor-
in-Charge of the Important News Section.
Waung Chi Loh (黃季樂) is the Chief of the
Business Department of the paper.
Registration Certificates Nos. 53 and 23
have been issued to the "Eastern Times" by the Ministry
of Home Affairs and the Central Propaganda Department
at Nanking.
pages.zh:
《时报》（Eastern Times），出版地址为福州路194号，创办于1904年，是一份日报。它在汉口路302号设有销售处。该报使用大号字体印刷文章，虽然广告费率是所有报纸的主要收入来源，但它刊登的广告并不多。该报资本为500,000美元。业主是黄伯惠（Waung Pah Wei），一位归国留学生，也是百万富翁和房地产商。黄先生被本地记者视为怪人，经常亲自修理他花费150,000金圆购买的一台五色印刷机。

该报每日出版约80,000份，另有30,000份晚报。它是一个独立的出版机构，但从未发表过社论或短评。它只刊登社会和体育新闻。该报在学生中很受欢迎。

该报的管理方式与其他主要报纸不同。它既没有总编辑也没有经理。所有阅读材料被分为不同版块，每个版块都有一名编辑。顾芷弇（Koo Tse Oen）负责本地新闻版，蔡行素（Tsai Yuin Soo）是要闻版的主编。

黄季乐（Waung Chi Loh）是该报营业部主任。

内政部和南京中央宣传部已向《时报》颁发了第53号和第23号登记证。

pages.en:
North China Daily News, 17, The Bund, Shanghai -
Daily paper, founded in 1864 issuing a weekly edition,
the North China Herald. Owned by the North China Daily
News and Herald Ltd., whose principal shareholders are
Mr. H. E. Morris and Mr. G. Morris. The largest daily
paper printed in English published in China, Japan
and the Straits. It has also the largest circulation,
subscription list and advertisement income, and is the
official organ for Consular, Municipal and legal notices.
Capital, 250,000 taels. General reputation, first class.
Circulation 5,000 to 6,000 daily. Caters for all
foreign and English-speaking residents of Shanghai, the
larger cities of the China coast, and the Yangtsze Valley,
and aims at maintaining and developing British trade in
the East. Has correspondents at Peking and in fifty
three other cities in China, who write on all phases
of Chinese trade, agriculture, politics, etc. Has also
correspondents in London, Edinburgh, Paris, Manila, Washington,
Vancouver, Montreal, Sydney, etc. In British politics
the present editor endeavours to favour the Conservative
party. The paper generally supports British interests.
The cosmopolitan nature of the community to which it
caters is nevertheless reflected in its articles which
appear to aim at upholding all foreign interests in China.
It is partial to France and the United States. It is very
critical when dealing with Chinese matters and to a
greater extent adopts the same attitude towards Japan.
The Chinese writer on its editorial staff, who is in the
pay of Chinese officials, carries on propaganda work on
their behalf in some of the articles which he contributes.
The best newspaper advertising medium in the East.
Proprietor : The North China Daily News & Herald Ltd.
Managing Director and Secretary : R. W. Davis
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，上海外滩17号——
日报，创刊于1864年，发行周刊版《北华捷报》。由《字林西报》及《捷报》有限公司（North China Daily News and Herald Ltd.）所有，其主要股东为H. E. Morris先生和G. Morris先生。这是在中国、日本和海峡殖民地出版的发行量最大的英文日报。它拥有最大的发行量、订阅名单和广告收入，是领事馆、工部局和法律公告的官方刊登机构。资本25万两白银。总体声誉一流。日发行量5,000至6,000份。面向上海、中国沿海较大城市以及长江流域的所有外籍人士和讲英语的居民，旨在维持和发展英国在东方的贸易。在北京及中国其他53个城市设有通讯员，撰写有关中国贸易、农业、政治等各方面的文章。在伦敦、爱丁堡、巴黎、马尼拉、华盛顿、温哥华、蒙特利尔、悉尼等地也设有通讯员。在英国政治方面，现任编辑力求偏向保守党。该报总体上支持英国利益。尽管如此，其所服务的社群具有国际性，这一特点反映在其文章中，这些文章似乎旨在维护所有外国在华利益。该报偏袒法国和美国。在处理中国事务时非常挑剔，并在更大程度上对日本采取相同的态度。其编辑部中有一位受中国官员薪俸的中国撰稿人，在他贡献的一些文章中代表他们进行宣传工作。是东方最好的报纸广告媒介。
所有者：《字林西报》及《捷报》有限公司
董事总经理兼秘书：R. W. Davis

pages.en:
THE NORTH CHINA HERALD AND SUPREME COURT AND CONSULAR GAZETTE.
(17, The Bund, Shanghai).- Weekly edition of the North China Daily
News (Shanghai). Founded, 1850. Owned by the North China Daily
News and Herald,-Ltd. Three supplements are issued with it: The
Municipal Gazette, The North China Herald Telegraphic Supplement,
and the North China Daily News and Herald, Ltd., Weekly Share
Supplement. Capital 250,000 taels. The sub-title is indicative
of its standing. Circulation, 1,800-2,000, which is larger than
that of any other weekly. Published specially for circulation in
the interior of China, where mails are comparatively infrequent,
and a bulky paper would entail heavy postage; at the same time
contains more news matter than other weeklies. It reaches practical-
ly all Consular, Customs, and Postal officials, business men and
missionaries in the interior. Under the same Directorship as, and
shares the Editorial Staff and Correspondents of the North China
Daily News. Its policy is British, and is aimed at establishing
British trade and interests in the Far East. The remarks about
the North China Daily News applies to its policy regarding Chinese
politics.
    A useful medium for advertisements likely to appeal to
foreigners and officials in the interior of China.
    For staff see North China Daily News (Shanghai).
pages.zh:
《北华捷报》暨《最高法院与领事公报》。
（上海外滩17号）。——《字林西报》（上海）的周刊版。创刊于1850年。由《字林西报》及《捷报》有限公司所有。随刊附发三份增刊：《工部局公报》、《北华捷报电讯增刊》和《字林西报》及《捷报》有限公司周报股票增刊。资本25万两白银。其副标题表明了它的地位。发行量1,800-2,000份，大于任何其他周刊。专门为中国内地发行而出版，那里邮路相对稀少， bulky 的报纸会导致沉重的邮资；同时包含的新闻内容比其他周刊更多。它实际上送达内地所有的领事、海关和邮政官员、商人和传教士手中。由与《字林西报》相同的董事会领导，并共享《字林西报》的编辑人员和通讯员。其政策是英国的，旨在确立英国在远东的贸易和利益。关于《字林西报》的评论适用于其对中国政治的政策。
    是一种有用的广告媒介，可能吸引中国内地的外国人和官员。
    员工见《字林西报》（上海）。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Times, 21 Museum Road, Shanghai, Daily Paper. Founded
about 1895. It is the property of a British subject, but its policy
appears to be controlled by Japanese. General reputation good.
Circulation 1250 except on Sundays when it reaches 3200. Caters for
a cosmopolitan public. Exchanges news with other papers. Has corres-
pondents throughout China and also in London, New York, etc. In
home politics hostile to Labour and inclined to be partial to
Liberalism. Its general attitude towards the officials and people
in China may be described as very cautious. It usually favours the
Northern Party and is very antagonistic to Dr. Sun Yat Sen and other
leaders holding radical views. It supports the interests of all
foreign nations, especially Great Britain and Japan. Its comments
nevertheless are very often unfavourable to France. A fairly useful
advertising medium, especially the Sunday Edition.
Proprietor and Director:- Edwin Arthur Nottingham.
Editor:- G. Burton - Sayer.
Staff:- Richard Hope, A. P. Finch, J. H. Lilley.
London agents:- Messrs. J. G. King & Sons, Fleet Street.
United States representatives:- Messrs. Roland Kay & Co. Chicago.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，上海博物馆路21号，日报。创刊于约1895年。其财产属于一位英国臣民，但其政策似乎受日本人控制。总体声誉良好。发行量1250份，除周日达到3200份。面向国际公众。与其他报纸交换新闻。在中国各地以及伦敦、纽约等地设有通讯员。在国内政治方面敌视工党，倾向于偏向自由主义。其对中国官员和民众的总体态度可描述为非常谨慎。它通常 favor 北方派系，并对孙中山博士及其他持有激进观点的领导人非常敌对。它支持所有外国国家的利益，特别是英国和日本。尽管如此，其评论往往对法国不利。是一种相当有用的广告媒介，尤其是周日版。
所有者兼董事：Edwin Arthur Nottingham
编辑：G. Burton - Sayer
员工：Richard Hope, A. P. Finch, J. H. Lilley
伦敦代理：J. G. King & Sons 公司，弗利特街
美国代表：Roland Kay & Co. 公司，芝加哥

pages.en:
The China Press, 14 Kiukiang Road, Shanghai. Daily paper (except
Mondays). Founded 1911. Published by the China Press Inc. a
company registered in Delaware, U. S. A. The capital consists of
10,000 shares of G.$5.00 each and the controlling interests is
held by Sopher & Co. British Jews, in their capacity as executors
of the Edward Ezra estate. Other important shareholders are Dr. Crane
a former American Minister to China, Rev. G. Castrillo, Spanish
Augustinian R. C. Mission and H. C. Norman, British. The circulation
is between 4000 and 5000. The paper caters for foreigners and
English reading Chinese. It receives news through all Reuter's
services as well as American, French, Italian and German wireless.
It obtains Chinese news through a Chinese member of the editorial
staff who appears to be well informed, and in addition has over 80
correspondents in the interior. In home politics it is non-partisan,
but supports American interests in China. It opposes the Japanese
chauvinist policy in China and the pretentions of that nation to
have special rights in this country. At present it appears to be
favourably disposed towards Great Britain. It is also partial to
progressive movements in China and has a large circulation among
English speaking Chinese officials, merchants and students in treaty
ports and the interior. It seems to be deferential to the opinions
of this section of its readers in matters affecting China. In spite
of its policy of neutrality in Chinese politics it publishes at
infrequent intervals propaganda favouring one or other of the Chinese
militarists in their quarrels with one another. American and British
editorials are contributed by J. B. Powell and R. Peyton-Griffin
respectively. It is a good advertising medium. The staff consist of:-
H. C. Norman, General Manager.
Herbert - Webb, Editor. His influence at present in the affairs of
the paper are negligible.
J. L. Butts, J. Hsu, L. Lehrbas, A. West, B. Kuhn, Mrs. B. Kuhn.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》（The China Press），上海九江路14号。日报（周一除外）。创刊于1911年。由《大美晚报》公司（China Press Inc.）出版，这是一家在美国特拉华州注册的公司。资本由10,000股组成，每股面值5.00美元，控股权由Sopher & Co. 持有，他们是英籍犹太人，作为Edward Ezra遗产的执行人。其他重要股东包括前美国驻华公使Crane博士、西班牙奥古斯丁罗马天主教传教团的G. Castrillo牧师以及英籍人士H. C. Norman。发行量在4000至5000之间。该报面向外国人和懂英语的中国人。它通过路透社的所有服务以及美国、法国、意大利和德国的无线电信号接收新闻。它通过编辑部中一位似乎消息灵通的中国成员获取中国新闻，此外在内陆还有80多名通讯员。在国内政治方面它是无党派的，但支持美国在华利益。它反对日本的沙文主义政策以及该国声称在中国拥有特殊权利的要求。目前它似乎对英国持友好态度。它也偏向中国的进步运动，在条约口岸和内陆的讲英语的中国官员、商人和学生中拥有大量读者。在涉及中国的事务上，它似乎尊重这部分读者的意见。尽管其在中国政治中保持中立政策，但它偶尔会刊登宣传文章，支持中国军阀在彼此争斗中的某一方。美英社论分别由J. B. Powell和R. Peyton-Griffin撰写。是一个良好的广告媒介。员工包括：
H. C. Norman，总经理。
Herbert - Webb，编辑。他目前在该报事务中的影响力微乎其微。
J. L. Butts, J. Hsu, L. Lehrbas, A. West, B. Kuhn, Mrs. B. Kuhn.

pages.en:
Evening News, No. 45-47 Peking Road -

Owned by two Americans named George S. Taell and C. J.
Lavell, but is generally believed to be subsidized by
Dr. Sun Yat Sen's party which it invariably supports.
The circulation is about 2,000. While antagonistic to
the Northern party, the paper seems very favourably
disposed towards Chinese and Chinese interests generally.
Its policy in regard to local foreigners and foreign
nations with the exception of Japan to which it is
antagonistic, seems to be governed by a desire to extend
its circulation among a cosmopolitan community. Efforts
will soon be made to have this paper registered under
the New China Trade Act as an American publication.

Editor : C. J. Lavell

Manager : George S. Taell
pages.zh:
《晚新闻》（Evening News），北京路45-47号——

由两名美国人George S. Taell和C. J. Lavell所有，但普遍被认为受到孙中山先生派系的资助，该报一贯支持该派系。发行量约为2,000份。虽然敌视北方派系，但该报似乎对中国及中国利益总体持非常友好的态度。除了对日本持敌对态度外，其关于当地外国人和外国的政策似乎受扩大其在国际社群中发行量的愿望所支配。不久将努力根据《新中国贸易法》将该报注册为美国出版物。

编辑：C. J. Lavell

经理：George S. Taell

pages.en:
Shanghai Mercury, 5 Hongkong Road, Shanghai.
Evening Daily paper, with which is incorporated the
Shanghai Courier. Founded 1879. Owned by the Shanghai
Mercury Ltd. The majority of the shares which are registered
in the name of a Briton, are held by Japanese who, it is
believed, are agents of the Japanese Government. The
proprietors issue a weekly edition of the paper as The
Celestial Empire (founded 1874). Authorised capital,
150,000 dollars; subscribed capital 146,200 dollars.
General reputation, highly respectable. Circulation
varies. Uses its own agencies, also some advertising
agencies in Europe and America. Rarely exchanges news.
In home politics, impartial. The paper pushes Japanese
interests in China. A fairly useful medium for trade
advertisements.
Proprietors : The Shanghai Mercury Ltd.
Managing Director and Secretary : W. J. Davey
Director : T. Sahara
Editorial Staff : W. A. Donaldson, Sam Hammond.
pages.zh:
《上海信使报》（Shanghai Mercury），上海香港路5号。
晚报日报，合并了《上海信使报》（Shanghai Courier）。创刊于1879年。由上海信使报有限公司（Shanghai Mercury Ltd.）所有。大部分股份登记在一位英国人名下，但由日本人持有，据信他们是日本政府的代理人。业主以《天朝帝国报》（The Celestial Empire，创刊于1874年）为名发行该报的周刊版。授权资本150,000美元；实缴资本146,200美元。总体声誉极高。发行量不定。使用自己的代理机构，也在欧洲和美国使用一些广告代理机构。很少交换新闻。在国内政治方面公正。该报推动日本在华利益。是商业广告的相当有用的媒介。
所有者：上海信使报有限公司
董事总经理兼秘书：W. J. Davey
董事：T. Sahara
编辑人员：W. A. Donaldson, Sam Hammond.

pages.en:
The Shun Pao (申報), established in 1872,
is the oldest Chinese daily newspaper in Shanghai.
It is usually pro-Nanking but occasionally criticizes
the government and may be considered independent, as
it is not subsidized by the government or any particular
group. It is anti-Japanese but adopts an independent
attitude towards the policies of Great Britain and the
U.S.A. except that in all disputes between China and
Britain or China and the U.S.A., the Chinese point of
view is naturally emphasized. It is generally considered
to be authoritative and fair. The capital of the paper
is given at $1,500,000. 100,000 copies used to be
printed daily but since the Sino-Japanese hostilities,
only 80,000 copies have been printed. Chang Yun Woo
(張蔭机) is the chief editor, and the proprietor.
and managing-director of the paper is Sze Liang Zay
(史量才), the chairman of the Nantao Municipal
Council. He is also connected with a number of
local public bodies and charitable institutions.
pages.zh:
《申报》，创刊于1872年，
是上海最古老的中文日报。
它通常亲南京政府，但偶尔批评政府，可被视为独立，因为它不受政府或任何特定团体的资助。它是反日的，但对英国和美国的政策采取独立态度，除非在中英或中美之间的所有争端中，自然强调中方观点。它通常被认为是权威和公正的。该报资本为1,500,000美元。过去每日印刷100,000份，但自中日敌对行动以来，仅印刷80,000份。张蔭机（音译）是主编，该报的所有者兼董事总经理是南市市政委员会主席史量才。他还与许多地方公共机构和慈善机构有关联。

pages.en:
Name SHUN PAO （申報）

Politics: Pro or anti Nanking Government or independent?
Pro-Nanking Government and independent.

Is it subsidized by Government or any group?
No.

What is its attitude towards the leading foreign countries,
i.e. Japan, Great Britain or United States?
Anti-Japan.

Reputation: Is it considered authoritative, fair,
sensational, conservative or radical?
Authoritative and fair.

Name of Editor: Chang Yun Woo （張蘊和）.

Owners: Any information regarding actual ownership or
control.
Limited concern.

Approximate average circulation per issue.
80,000 copies are printed daily.

名称 申报 （申報）

政治立场：亲南京政府、反南京政府还是独立？
亲南京政府且独立。

是否受政府或任何团体资助？
否。

它对主要外国（即日本、英国或美国）的态度如何？
反日。

声誉：被认为权威、公正、耸人听闻、保守还是激进？
权威且公正。

编辑姓名：张蘊和 （張蘊和）。

所有者：关于实际所有权或控制的任何信息。
有限公司。

每期大致平均发行量。
每日印刷80,000份。

pages.en:
The Sin Wan Pao (新聞報) is the most
influential Chinese daily newspaper in Shanghai.
It is regarded by the Chinese community as an indepen-
dent organ chiefly devoted to commerce and its revenue
is chiefly derived from advertisements. It is anti-
Japanese, but its attitude towards Britain and the
U.S.A. is for the most part impartial. It is considered
fair, authoritative and conservative. Li Hao Zeu
(李浩然) is the editor-in-chief. The capital of this
paper is given as $1,200,000 and most of the shares are
in the hands of Sze Liang Zay (史量才), managing
director of the Shun Pao (申報). About 120,000
copies are printed daily of which 40,000 copies are
distributed in Shanghai. An evening edition of 10,000
copies is also printed, but this is not in great demand
and free copies are distributed to the leading Chinese
hotels, etc.
pages.zh:
《新闻报》是上海最具影响力的中文日报。
它被华人社区视为一个独立机构，主要致力于商业，其收入主要来自广告。它是反日的，但对英国和美国的态度大部分是公正的。它被认为是公正、权威和保守的。李浩然（音译）是总编辑。该报资本为1,200,000美元，大部分股份掌握在《申报》董事总经理史量才手中。每日印刷约120,000份，其中40,000份在上海分发。还印刷10,000份晚报，但需求不大，免费分发给主要的中式旅馆等。

pages.en:
Name SHANGHAI SIN WEN PAO (新聞報)

Politics: Pro or anti Nanking Government or independent?
Independent.

Is it subsideded by Government or any group?
No.

What is its attitude towards the leading foreign countries,
i.e. Japan, Great Britain or United States?
Anti-Japan.

Reputation: Is it considered authoritative, fair,
sensational, conservative or radical?
Fair and conservative.

Name of Editor: Li Hao Zeu (李浩然).

Owners: Any information regarding actual ownership or
control.
Limited company, but most of the shares ~~the family of the late~~
are in the hands of Sze Liang Zay (史量才),
Managing Director of the Shun Pao.
Approximate average circulation per issue.
About 120,000 copies are printed daily.
pages.zh:
名称 上海新闻报 (新聞報)

政治立场：亲南京政府、反南京政府还是独立？
独立。

是否受政府或任何团体资助？
否。

它对主要外国（即日本、英国或美国）的态度如何？
反日。

声誉：被认为权威、公正、耸人听闻、保守还是激进？
公正且保守。

编辑姓名：李浩然 (李浩然)。

所有者：关于实际所有权或控制的任何信息。
有限公司，但大部分股份 ~~已故家族~~
掌握在《申报》董事总经理史量才 (史量才) 手中。
每期大致平均发行量。
每日印刷约120,000份。

pages.en:
The Shih Shih Hsin Pao (ChinaTimes 時事新報 )
is regarded by the Chinese community as an independent
progressive newspaper. It is anti-Japanese and anti-
foreign, not specifically anti-Britain or anti-U.S.A.
It is not considered authoritative but sensational and
mildly radical, though fair in most of its articles.
The editor is Pen Kung Pi ( 潘公展 ), a well known
journalist. The capital of the paper is $300,000
and the shares are owned by a syndicate formed in 1930
by Chang Tso Ping ( 張竹平 ) who is the Managing-
Director of the "China Press", a foreign daily news-
paper and the "China Evening News", a Chinese evening
newspaper, besides being Managing-Director of the
Shih Shih Hsin Pao. Dr. Wellington Koo (Chinese
Minister to France) is a member of the financial
syndicate. 20,000 copies are printed daily.
pages.zh: 《时事新报》（Shih Shih Hsin Pao，China Times）被华人社区视为一家独立的进步报纸。该报持反日及反外立场，但并非专门针对英国或美国。该报虽不被视为具有权威性，且风格耸动、略带激进色彩，但其大多数文章尚属公正。主编为著名记者潘公展（Pen Kung Pi）。该报资本为30万美元，股份由张竹平（Chang Tso Ping）于1930年组建的辛迪加持有。张竹平除担任《时事新报》总经理外，还兼任外文日报《大陆报》（China Press）及中文晚报《新闻报》（China Evening News）的总经理。顾维钧博士（中国驻法公使）是该金融辛迪加的成员。该报每日印刷量为2万份。

pages.en:
Name SHIH SHIH SIN PAO ( China Times 時事新報)

Politics: Pro or anti Nanking Government or independent?
Independent.

Is it subsidized by Government or any group?
No.

What is its attitude towards the leading foreign countries,
i.e. Japan, Great Britain or United States?
Anti-Japan.

Reputation: Is it considered authoritative, fair,
sensational, conservative or radical?
Fair.

Name of Editor: Pen Kung Pi (潘公展).

Owners: Any information regarding actual ownership or
control.
Limited concern.

名称：《时事新报》（SHIH SHIH SIN PAO，China Times）

政治立场：亲南京政府、反南京政府还是独立？
独立。

是否接受政府或任何团体的资助？
否。

其对主要外国（即日本、英国或美国）的态度如何？
反日。

声誉：被视为权威、公正、耸动、保守还是激进？
公正。

主编姓名：潘公展（Pen Kung Pi）。

所有者：关于实际所有权或控制权的任何信息。
有限公司。

每期平均发行量约为：
每日印刷2万份。

pages.en:
The "Eastern Times" (時報), published at
No. 194 Foochow Road, established in 1904, is a daily
newspaper. It has a sales office at No. 302 Hankow Road.
The paper prints its articles in large type and does not
print many advertisements, although advertisement rates
form the chief source of the revenue of all newspapers.
The capital of the paper is $500,000. Waung Pah-wei
(黃伯惠), a returned student, who is a millionaire and
real estate owner, is the proprietor. Mr. Waung, who is
regarded by local journalists as an eccentric person,
often personally attends to the mechanical repairs of
a five-colour printing machine, which he bought for
Gold $150,000.

This paper publishes about 80,000 copies daily
with an evening edition of 30,000 copies. It is an
independent publishing organ but it has never published
editorials or brief comments. It is devoted to social
and sporting news only. This paper is popular among
students.

The administration of this paper is different
to all other leading newspapers. It has neither Editor-
in-Chief nor Manager. All reading matter is classified
into different sections and each section has an editor.
Koo Tse-oen (顧芷年) is responsible for the Local News
Section while Tsai Yuin-soo (蔡行素) is Editor-in-
Charge of the Important News Section.

Waung Chi-loh (王季樂) is the Chief of the
Business Department of the paper.

Registration Certificates Nos. 53 and 23 have
been issued to the "Eastern Times" by the Ministry of
Home Affairs and the Central Propaganda Department at
Nanking.
pages.zh:
《时报》（Eastern Times），创刊于1904年，社址位于福州路194号，是一家日报。其在汉口路302号设有发行处。该报采用大号字体排版，刊登的广告不多，尽管广告费是所有报纸的主要收入来源。该报资本为50万美元。业主为黄伯惠（Waung Pah-wei），他是一位归国留学生、百万富翁及房地产商。黄先生被当地新闻界人士视为怪人，经常亲自修理他以15万金元购买的一台五色印刷机。

该报每日出版约8万份，晚刊3万份。它是一家独立的出版机构，但从未发表过社论或短评。该报仅致力于社会新闻和体育新闻。该报在学生中颇受欢迎。

该报的管理方式与其他主要报纸不同。它既没有总编辑，也没有经理。所有阅读材料被分为不同版块，每个版块设有一名编辑。顾芷年（Koo Tse-oen）负责本地新闻版，蔡行素（Tsai Yuin-soo）负责重要新闻版的主编工作。

王季乐（Waung Chi-loh）是该报营业部主任。

南京内政部及中央宣传部已向《时报》颁发第53号和第23号登记证。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, January 19, 1937
(2)
NO. 1. O...... 9/21
DATED... 4 2 37

Scores Of Papers
Published Here,
Manual Indicates

Chinese Language News
Sheets Roll Up Big
Local Score

NAMES COLORFUL

THAT Shanghai is the biggest newspaper city in China is amply evidenced by the 1937 edition of the Newspaper Directory of China, including Hongkong, and advertising manual published by Carl Crow, Inc. The manual, just off press, lists most of the Chinese and foreign-language papers in this country, and the list for Shanghai is an imposing one.

While every mosquito sheet in Shanghai is not listed here, a feat which is obviously impossible, the better known papers are included.

Post, Press, Times, News

Among the foreign-language newspapers, those published in the English language include the Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, published by the Post-Mercury Company Federal, Inc. (American), published every evening except Sunday—audited daily average circulation 7350; the China Press, published by the China Press, Inc. (Delaware)—audited daily average circulation 4840; the Shanghai Times, published by E. A. Nottingham (British), certified audited daily average circulation 6000; and the North China Daily News (British), audited daily average circulation 10,355.

The French language paper is Le Journal de Shanghai; the Japanese language dailies include the Shanghai Mainichi Shimbun, Shanghai Nichi Nichi Shimbun, Shanghai Nippo Sha; Russian language dailies include The New Trail, the Russian Daily News, the Shanghai Zaria, the Slovo; German language papers include the Ostasiatischer Lloyd, the China Dienst (a weekly), and the German Chamber of Commerce Journal (a fortnightly).

Many Chinese Dailies

There are a host of Chinese dailies in Shanghai. According to this listing, the Shun Pao and the Sin Wen Pao are neck and neck at the top with circulations of 150,000. Next is the Shih Sze Sin Pao (The China Times) with 100,000; next the Shin Pao (Eastern Times), with 80,000; and the Da Van Pao with 60,000. Other outstanding Chinese dailies include the National Herald, the China Daily News, The Great Daily News, the Hwa Mei Wan Pao (Chinese-American Evening News), the Min Pao, the Ta Kung Pao (L'Impartial), the Social Evening News, and the Ta Mei Wen Pao (Great American Evening Newspaper published by the Post-Mercury Company).

Shanghai supports a large number of Chinese daily tabloids, mostly with rather new organizations. These include the following colorfully-named papers: Morning News, the China Daily News, the Crystal, the Crystal Press, the Diamond, the Movie Life, Camera News, Star Daily News, Current Daily News, the Holmes, the Shanghai People's Daily News, the Shanghai Press, Petty News, World Morning News, Shanghai Commercial News, New Robinhood, Iron News, Theatre World, Social Daily News.

Semi-Weeklies

In addition, there are a large number of Chinese-language semi-weeklies which include Public News, Big News, News Press, Robin Hood, Social News, etc. Chinese language weeklies include Bankers' Weekly, Broadcast Weekly, Consumers' Weekly, the Chinese Student, China Weekly Herald, Public Life Weekly, Movie Weekly, English Weekly, Mutual Help, New People Weekly, Nice Weekly, People's Talk, Prosperous Year, Industrial and Commercial Advocate, Twinkling Rays, Weekly of the Chinese Institute of Engineers, Saturday, United Pictorial, Movietone, Chinese Christian Intelligencer, Pictorial Weekly, New Schoolmate, Weekly Critic, Radio Weekly, Amusing Weekly, Lady's Voice, Sports News, and People's Weekly.

The English-language weeklies listed in this volume are Capital and Trade, Catholic Review, China Critic, China Digest, China Weekly Review, China Outlook, Chinese Economic Bulletin, Chinese Nation, Chinese Republic, East, Finance and Commerce, North China Herald, Shanghai Sunday Times, Shanghai Woman, Shipping Review, Sporting World, Walla-Walla, etc.

Semi-Monthlies

There is a large group of Chinese language semi-monthlies here as well, which include Thousand Years, Children's World, Eastern Miscellany, New China Fortnightly, Economic Journal, Le Grand Shanghai, Analects, National Defence Forum, Social Mercury, Spring Color, Intelligence, World Knowledge, Ten-Day Magazine, Modern Children, etc.

Chinese language monthlies include Amateur Radio, Arts and Life, The Builder, Chinese Architect, Journal of Photography, Chin Fen Sports Monthly, Child Education, Chin Chin Movie Monthly, Chen Hwa Radio Magazine, China Radio, Medical Treatment Journal, Monthly Picture, Continental, Good Roads Monthly, China Pictorial, Central China, Construction, Red Cross Monthly, Juvenile Student, Mercy Monthly, Medical Questionnaire, Medical Journal, Happy Home, Anti-Opium Monthly, Yellow Flower, World Engineering News, Science, Public Welfare Monthly, Young Companion, China Traveler, National Weekly, Modern Cinema Pictorial, Modern Parents, Movie Punch, Sketch Pictorial, Modern Sketch, Oriental Punch, Philips Radio Magazine, Popular Radio Magazine, Radio Wave, Commercial Engineer, National Journal of Commerce, Commercial World, Modern Student, New Asia, New Inventions Miscellany, Life, Educational Review, True Light Review, Resister Pictorial, Women's Pictorial, Phenomena Monthly, Art Classics, Movie & Music Monthly, Green Year, Les Contemporains, Women's Message, and Women's Monthly.

English Monthlies

Among the English language monthlies are the American Women's Club Bulletin, British Women's Association Magazine, Cathay Magazine, Commercial Asia, China Highways, China Home and Art Journal, China Journal, Chinese Economic Journal, Chinese Recorder, Commercial Engineer, Far Eastern Hotel Industry, Far Eastern Review, Hexagon, Holy Trinity Cathedral, Israel's Messenger, Journal of the British Chamber of Commerce, Oriental Affairs, Shanghai Builder, Shanghai Screen Book, Shanghailander, Shanghai Police Gazette, Shanghai Woman, Tien Hsia, Totem, Town and Sportsman, Yankee Clipper, Y Spokesman, and a number of others.

The book also lists Agricultural Science, Kung Chen, Quarterly Journal of Economics and Tungchi Acta Medica as Chinese-language quarterlies, and the Commercial Directory of Shanghai as a Chinese-language annual. English-language annuals listed are the China Hong List, Credit Men's Business Directory, and Shanghai Dollar Directory.

It is very difficult to keep up with the times, and a number of these publications listed are no longer produced, whereas a number of others have not been included.

The directory, however, gives a general idea of Shanghai as a publishing center.

卡尔·克劳公司（Carl Crow, Inc.）出版的《中国报刊目录》（1937年版，含香港）及广告手册充分证明，上海是中国最大的报业城市。该手册刚刚付梓，列出了本国大多数中文和外文报纸，其中上海的名单令人瞩目。

虽然这里并未列出上海的每一份小报——这显然是不可能的任务——但较知名的报纸均被收录在内。

邮报、新闻报、时报、日报

在外文报纸中，英文报纸包括：由美资联邦邮报-水星报公司（Post-Mercury Company Federal, Inc.）出版的《上海晚邮报与水星报》，除周日外每晚出版——经审计的日均发行量为7350份；由特拉华州注册的《大陆报》公司（China Press, Inc.）出版的《大陆报》——经审计的日均发行量为4840份；由英籍人士E. A. Nottingham出版的《上海泰晤士报》（Shanghai Times），经认证的审计日均发行量为6000份；以及英资《字林西报》（North China Daily News），经审计的日均发行量为10,355份。

法文报纸为《上海日报》（Le Journal de Shanghai）；日文日报包括《上海每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi Shimbun）、《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nichi Nichi Shimbun）、《上海日本社》（Shanghai Nippo Sha）；俄文日报包括《新路报》（The New Trail）、《俄罗斯日报》（Russian Daily News）、《上海霞光报》（Shanghai Zaria）、《言论报》（Slovo）；德文报纸包括《东亚劳埃德报》（Ostasiatischer Lloyd）、《中国服务》（China Dienst，周刊）以及《德国商会期刊》（German Chamber of Commerce Journal，半月刊）。

众多中文日报

上海有大量的中文日报。根据此列表，《申报》和《新闻报》并驾齐驱，位居榜首，发行量均为15万份。其次是《时事新报》（The China Times），发行量为10万份；再次是《申包》（Shin Pao，即《时报》），发行量为8万份；以及《大晚报》（Da Van Pao），发行量为6万份。其他杰出的中文日报包括《国民导报》（National Herald）、《中华日报》（China Daily News）、《大公报》（The Great Daily News）、《华美晚报》（Hwa Mei Wan Pao）、《民报》（Min Pao）、《大公报》（Ta Kung Pao，L'Impartial）、《社会晚报》（Social Evening News）以及《大美晚报》（Ta Mei Wen Pao，由邮报-水星报公司出版的美资大型英文晚报[注：原文如此，实为中文晚报]）。

Sir,
The attached article on mosquito papers in Shanghai
appearing in the "China Press" on November 27, 1935 contains
quite accurate information.
During the Manchu regime the Chinese public paid
little attention to mosquito papers because most of the
reading matter contained in these papers relates to "sing
song" girls, Pekinese theatricals, love stories, etc.
To-day mosquito papers are being more and more favoured
by the general public.
Since the inauguration of the Republic, Yue Dah Yung
(余大雄), publisher of the now defunct "National Herald"
(神州日報), a Chinese daily newspaper, ceased the publication
of the "Herald" and started the "Crystal" (晶報), a three-
day mosquito paper. In addition to articles relating to
amusements, the paper contained short articles on political
and social affairs written in a serio-comic manner by well-
known newspapermen whom he had engaged. The "Crystal" soon
became very popular and attained a circulation of 30,000 copies
per issue.
Owing to the success of the "Crystal", other mosquito
papers such as the "Diamond" (金鋼鑽), the "Holmes" (福爾摩斯),
the "Shanghai Pao" (上海報), the "Petty News" (小日報), the
"Social Daily News" (社會日報), the "Modern Daily News"
(時代日報), the "Great Crystal" (大晶報), the "World Morning
News" (世界晨報), etc. were started. Subsequently all these
papers were converted into dailies.
The publishers of these papers are doing well and derive
much monthly revenue in the form of "hush-money" or subsidies

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 27, 1935    12568

New Journalistic Trend Seen
In Local Tabloids Following
Closing Of Mosquito Sheets

Tidy Editions Carry Compact, Lightly-Written
Summary Of Important And Unimportant
Local, World News; Moral Standards
Of Reporting Are Changing

By HAWTHORNE CHENG

The function of a Chinese news-paper is to entertain and inform in an entertaining way. Almost everything said and done in Chin-ese life here that carries a touch of humor, therefore, soon finds its way into Shanghai's many chroni-clers of events.

That has been the motto under which many new Chinese tabloid newspapers have sprung up like mushrooms in Shanghai in place of mosquito journals that have been suppressed by authorities. The substitution, however, marks a de-finite turn for the better in the development of China's "petty journalism" as far as the motto "to entertain" is concerned.

Take the Hsiao Chen Pao and Li Pao for instance. The former is an underling of the Chen Pao, the English name of which is Morning Post, while the latter was organiz-ed by a group of Chinese journ-alists and writers of considerable distinction as an independent daily.

A casual perusal will be con-vincing that both commendably testify to a new development, namely the decency in writing as compared to scandalism of their predecessors.

Marks Unique Trend

Especially the Little Morning Post, as it is published alongside the Morning Post, has marked a unique growth in the field of Chin-ese newspapers. The Sin Wan Pao, one of the oldest and leading Chin-ese dailies in Shanghai, publishes an evening edition, but there never has been a newspaper like the Chen Pao (Morning Post) that carries with it a tidy, little edition like the Hsiao Chen Pao (Little Morn-ing Post).

The Little Morning Post, as its name implies, is much smaller—only one full sheet folded into four pages—in size compared to its parent journal—a full-sized paper of 16 pages. Yet the smaller edition has to carry a skeleton of all the important news that appears in the large one, and to live up to its motto "to amuse," must write the news in a lighter vein. To serve these two irreconcilable purposes, the smallest of readable type has to be used in printing it.

The principle of "important news on front page" is observed. All the spot news of both a political and social nature have to be crowded into one page, the upper half of the front page being devoted to the former and lower half to the latter. Yet care has apparently been taken not to miss anything "hot" in its coverage. And this is done by "boiling down" copy that is turned in for publication.

In publishing crime news, words and phrases that sound "vulgar" or "dirty" from a Chinese stand-point are avoided as far as pos-sible. In writing his reports, how-ever, the crime reporter is told not to lose sight of purpose of the paper he is writing, which is ex-clusively to entertain. And under this motto, the principle of de-cency from the standpoint of Western journalism cannot be ob-served to the letter. For it is not indecent in a Chinese newspaper to elaborate in one's description of the circumstances and scenes in which an illegal couple have made love with each other before they are caught by the police.

Standards Change

Once, the Eastern Times carried a report saying that a man died with fatigue and exhaustion after making love to a woman. This way of reporting, however, has been, to a great extent, taken exception to by the Little Morning Post.

Nor does the Little Morning Post use the tactics of Yellow Journalism as does the Eastern Times. There is no "playing up" of news in the former with a view to sensation-alism.

The pages inside and on the back of the Little Morning Post are exclusively devoted to publica-tion of features and articles of an entertaining nature? There are several columnists, most of whom are Chinese writers of considerable standing, who write under different topics from day to day.

What has been said about the Little Morning Post is, for most part, also true with the Li Pao, which has apparently come into being due to the welcome that has greeted the publication of the Little Morning Post.

The Li Pao, however, excells by some very good cartoons that it occasionally prints. Yesterday's edition of Lih Pao, for instance, carries at the upper right hand corner of its front page a cartoon picture of Mr. Yin Ju-keng, as the person much in the limelight in connection with the autonomous conspiracy in North China. The cartoon by Mr. Lu Shao-fei, noted Chinese cartoonist, is very well done. It looks, in a very comical and sarcastic way, like the notori-ous Mr. Yin very much.

The Little Morning Post also prints cartoons, but much less fre-quently.

The Li Pao further distinguishes itself from its contemporary in another respect. It delves into the things that are suitable reading matter for the masses people, whereas some emphasis in discussions on Chinese literature and philosophy is being laid in the Little Morning Post, providing interesting reading for Chinese students with literary tastes. Under the heading entitled "Blood and Sweat," for instance, yesterday's edition of the Li Pao carried an article chatting about the dealers in sweet potatoes.

The Little Morning Post is more universal in its coverage both of news and features. Articles dealing with various aspects of development in foreign countries written in a lighter vein can be seen in this little paper everyday.

Both the Little Morning Post and the Li Pao publish no advertise-ments. They each depend on street sales and are sold for three coppers a copy.

《字林西报》，1935年11月27日，星期三    12568

随着小报被取缔，本地小开本报纸出现新闻业新趋势

版面整洁，简明扼要地刊登轻重不分的本地及世界新闻摘要；报道的道德标准正在发生变化

作者：HAWTHORNE CHENG

中文报纸的功能是以娱乐的方式提供信息和消遣。因此，这里中国人生活中几乎所有带有幽默色彩的言行，很快就会出现在上海众多记录事件的编年史中。

这已成为许多新的中文小开本报纸在上海如雨后春笋般涌现以取代被当局查禁的小报（mosquito journals）的座右铭。然而，就“提供娱乐”这一座右铭而言，这种替代标志着中国“小报新闻业”发展的一个明确好转。

以《小晨報》和《立報》为例。前者是《晨報》（英文名 Morning Post）的附属刊物，而后者则由一群颇具声望的中国记者和作家组织成立，作为一份独立的日报。

随意浏览即可令人信服地证明，这两份报纸都值得称赞地见证了一种新的发展，即与其前任热衷于丑闻相比，它们在写作上更为得体。

标志独特趋势

特别是《小晨報》，由于它与《晨報》一同出版，在中国报业领域标志着一种独特的增长。《新闻报》（Sin Wan Pao）是上海最古老且领先的中文日报之一，也出版晚刊，但从未有过像《晨報》（Morning Post）那样附带一份整洁的小版刊物如《小晨報》（Little Morning Post）的报纸。

顾名思义，《小晨報》的篇幅比其母报小得多——母报是一份16页的全幅报纸，而它只有一张全开纸折叠成四页。然而，这份较小的版次必须刊登大报上所有重要新闻的概要，并且为了践行其“提供娱乐”的座右铭，必须以较轻松的笔调撰写新闻。为了服务于这两个不可调和的目的，印刷时不得不使用最小的可读字体。

“头版刊登重要新闻”的原则得到了遵守。所有政治和社会性质的突发新闻都必须挤在一页上，头版的上半部分用于前者，下半部分用于后者。然而，显然已采取谨慎措施，确保在其报道中不漏掉任何“热点”。这是通过对提交的稿件进行“浓缩”来实现的。

在发布犯罪新闻时，尽可能避免使用从中文角度来看听起来“粗俗”或“肮脏”的词语和短语。然而，犯罪新闻记者被告知，在撰写报道时不要忽视其所供职报纸的宗旨，即专门提供娱乐。在这一座右铭下，西方新闻业视角下的体面原则无法被严格遵循。因为在中国报纸上，详细描述一对非法情侣在被警察抓获前发生性关系的情境和场景，并不被视为不雅。

标准改变

曾经，《时事新报》（Eastern Times）刊登过一篇报道，称一名男子在与一名女子发生性关系后因疲劳和衰竭而死。然而，《小晨報》在很大程度上对这种报道方式表示了异议。

《小晨報》也不像《时事新报》那样使用黄色新闻的策略。前者没有为了耸人听闻而“夸大”新闻。

《小晨報》的内页和背页专门用于刊登特写和娱乐性质的文章。有几位专栏作家，其中大多数是颇具地位的中国作家，他们每天就不同主题撰写文章。

关于《小晨報》所说的内容，大部分也适用于《立報》，该报显然是因《小晨報》出版后受到的欢迎而诞生的。

然而，《立報》因其偶尔刊登的一些非常优秀的漫画而更胜一筹。例如，昨天的《立報》（Lih Pao）在其头版右上角刊登了一幅殷汝耕（Yin Ju-keng）先生的漫画，他是华北自治阴谋中备受瞩目的人物。这幅由中国著名漫画家鲁少飞（Lu Shao-fei）创作的漫画做得非常好。它以非常滑稽和讽刺的方式，看起来很像那位臭名昭著的殷先生。

《小晨報》也刊登漫画，但频率低得多。

《立報》在另一个方面使其与同时代的报纸区别开来。它深入探讨适合大众阅读的内容，而《小晨報》则在讨论中国文学和哲学方面有所侧重，为具有文学趣味的中国学生提供有趣的读物。例如，在题为“血汗”的标题下，昨天的《立報》刊登了一篇闲聊红薯商贩的文章。

《小晨報》在新闻和特写的报道范围上更为广泛。在这份小报上，每天都可以看到以较轻松笔调撰写的关于外国各方面发展的文章。

《小晨報》和《立報》均不刊登广告。它们各自依赖街头零售，每份售价三个铜板。

$5

(C. & S. B.) Office Notes

REPORT ON CHINESE NEWS AGENCIES
AND
MOSQUITO NEWSPAPERS.
-------

Sir,
Attached is report on ChineseNews Agencies and
on mosquito newspapers.
As far as could be ascertained none of the
mosquito newspapers are in receipt of subsidies from
the National Government or from any political party,
but it is a well known fact that they derive most of their
income from extortion and such other unlawful
activities. One mosquito paper, the Crystal, has become
so influential that its owner has entry to the best
circles where he is favourably placed to hear of gossip
and scandals which he turns to his profit.
As regards the news agencies, they do not depend
on subscribers who take their service for their income.
but principally on subsidies from the Government or
some political party. The agencies charge from $10
to $15 per month for their news service, but as a rule
they are satisfied so long as they can find some paper
or commercial firm or private individual to accept their
service so that they can show their names on the list of
subscribers to enhance their repution. The only
respectable agency is the Kuo Wen and its service is
popular with the people.

Clerical Assistant.

D.C. (C. & B. B.)

(刑事 & 特科) 办公室笔记

关于中文通讯社
及
小报的报告。
-------

先生，
附件是关于中文通讯社
和小报的报告。
据查，没有任何
小报接受来自
国民政府或任何政党的补贴，
但众所周知的事实是，它们的大部分
收入来自勒索和其他此类非法
活动。有一家名为《晶报》（Crystal）的小报变得
如此具有影响力，以至于其所有者得以进入最高级的
社交圈，在那里他处于有利位置，可以听到八卦
和丑闻，并从中牟利。
至于通讯社，它们并不依赖
订阅其服务的客户来获得收入，
而是主要依靠政府或
某些政党的补贴。通讯社对其新闻服务
每月收费10至15美元，但通常
只要它们能找到某些报纸、商业公司或个人接受其
服务，以便将其名字列入订阅者名单以提升声誉，它们就感到满意。唯一
正派的通讯社是国闻通讯社（Kuo Wen），其服务
深受民众欢迎。

文书助理。

副总监（刑事 & 特科）

pages.en:
1.0. 9121

The Crystal ( 晶 报 ) was started about II years
ago by Yu Dah Yoong(徐大雄) who was then in charge of the National
Herald. It is the oldest mosquito newspaper and has the
largest circulation, the present figures being 20,000 copies.
It is published every three days. Owing to its popularity with
the Chinese, the paper has a certain amount of influence which its
owner turns to profitable account. The paper is located at
No. 161 Shantung Road. The present value of the paper is
estimated at $20,000 made up as follows: good will $12,000 ,
printing and composing materials, furniture etc. $8,000.

The Diamond ( 金剛鑽 ) was established about six
years ago by Sze Tsi Yung, who at one time was the Editor of the
World Book Co., a Chinese book shop on Foochow Road. The
paper was started as an opposition organ to the Crystal which
was criticizing a Chinese actor named Loh Mau Tai in a most unfair
manner. A number of friends of the actor conceived the idea
of forming a paper to deal with the Crystal. The Diamond soon
became popular with the public and next to the Crystal it is the
most influential mosquito paper in Shanghai. It has a circulation
of 12,000 copies. Like the Crystal it is also published every
three days. The present value of the Diamond is estimated at
about $15,000 of which $10,000 represents the value of the
good will. Address: 31 Ningpo Road.

The Shanghai Pao ( 上 海 报 ) was started on October 1,
1929. It is owned by a well known merchant by the name of Kwan
Zoong Meu who lives in Ho Ka Loong, Nantao. The paper is managed
by Kwan Zoong Wah, probably a relation of the owner. The paper
has a circulation of 10,000 copies. The Capital is $5,000. The
estimated income is $2,500 and expenses $2,300. It is published
every day. Address: 548 Foochow Road.
pages.zh:
1.0. 9121

《晶报》（The Crystal）大约于11年前由徐大雄（Yu Dah Yoong）创办，他当时负责《国民新闻报》（National Herald）。它是最老牌的“蚊子报”（小型八卦报刊），发行量最大，目前数字为20,000份。该报每三天出版一期。由于在中国人中颇受欢迎，该报具有一定的影响力，其所有者利用这一点牟利。该报社址位于山东路161号。该报目前的估值为20,000美元，构成如下：商誉12,000美元，印刷及排版材料、家具等8,000美元。

《金刚钻》（The Diamond）大约于六年前由施子庸（Sze Tsi Yung，音译）创办，他曾任福州路一家中文书店世界书局（World Book Co.）的编辑。创办该报是为了对抗《晶报》，因为《晶报》以一种极不公平的方式批评一位名叫罗茂泰（Loh Mau Tai，音译）的中国演员。这位演员的一些朋友萌生了创办一份报纸来对付《晶报》的想法。《金刚钻》很快受到公众欢迎，在上海，它是仅次于《晶报》的最具影响力的“蚊子报”。其发行量为12,000份。像《晶报》一样，它也是每三天出版一期。《金刚钻》目前的估值约为15,000美元，其中10,000美元代表商誉价值。地址：宁波路31号。

《上海报》（The Shanghai Pao）创办于1929年10月1日。其所有者是一位名为关宗梅（Kwan Zoong Meu，音译）的知名商人，他住在南市何家弄。该报由关宗华（Kwan Zoong Wah，音译）管理，可能是所有者的亲属。该报发行量为10,000份。资本为5,000美元。估计收入为2,500美元，支出为2,300美元。该报每日出版。地址：福州路548号。

pages.en:
-2-

The Shanghai Daily News ( 上海日报 ) was started
on May 16, 1930 by Kau Lan Sung. This man was formerly in the
employ of Kwan Zoong Meu of the Shanghai Pao, but it is alleged
that he left the service after a dispute had arisen over the
shortage of a large sum of money. Kao Lan Sung lives in Siao
Bee Loong, Nantao. The paper is capitalised at $2,000. Its
monthly income is estimated at $2100 and the expenses at $1900.
It has a circulation of 10,000 copies. It is published daily.
Address of paper: 812 Foochow Road.

The Keh Min Jih Pao ( 革命日报 ) was started in
July 1929. It is the organ of the Left Wing of the Kuomintang and
is against the Nanking Government. It supports Wang Tsing Wei.
One of its editors was the late Wang Loh Ping who was murdered
in a house in the French Concession early this year. The paper
was
used to have a circulation of 3000 copies. It published daily.
The name of the present editor cannot be ascertained. For obvious
reasons no information could be secured as to when it will be
published again.

The Great Crystal ( 大晶报 ) was established by Feng
Mong Yuen about 13 months ago. Its monthly expenses are estimated
at $600, its income is unknown. It has a circulation of 4,000
copies. It is published every 3 days. Address of paper: 311
Ningpo Road.

The Holmes ( 福尔摩斯 ) is a small but influential paper.
It was started by Wu Yong Fee with a capital of $150. It has a
circulation of 10,000 copies. The paper is published every 3 days.
The Manager's name is Yao Kee Kwang. Address of paper 169
Pakhoi Road.
pages.zh:
-2-

《上海日报》（The Shanghai Daily News）由高兰松（Kau Lan Sung，音译）于1930年5月16日创办。此人此前受雇于《上海报》的关宗梅，但据称他在因一大笔款项短缺发生争执后离职。高兰松住在南市小北门（Siao Bee Loong，音译）。该报资本为2,000美元。其月收入估计为2,100美元，支出为1,900美元。发行量为10,000份。每日出版。报社地址：福州路812号。

《革命日报》（The Keh Min Jih Pao）创办于1929年7月。它是国民党左派的机关报，反对南京政府。它支持汪精卫。其编辑之一是已故的王洛平（Wang Loh Ping，音译），他于今年早些时候在法租界的一所房屋内被谋杀。该报
曾拥有3,000份的发行量。每日出版。现任编辑的名字无法查明。出于显而易见的原因，无法获得关于其何时复刊的信息。

《大晶报》（The Great Crystal）由冯梦元（Feng Mong Yuen，音译）于大约13个月前创办。其每月支出估计为600美元，收入不详。发行量为4,000份。每3天出版一期。报社地址：宁波路311号。

《福尔摩斯》（The Holmes）是一份虽小但有影响力的报纸。由吴永费（Wu Yong Fee，音译）以150美元资本创办。发行量为10,000份。该报每3天出版一期。经理姓名为姚琪光（Yao Kee Kwang，音译）。报社地址：北河南路169号。

pages.en:
-3-

The New RobinHood ( 新罗宾汉 ) is a 3 day mosquito
paper. It was established 6 months ago by Cheng Sung Foong.
A few months later it was purchased by Huang Yu Tsar by whom it
is being managed. It has a circulation of 3,000 copies. Address
of paper: Dong An Lee off Hankow Road.

The Iron News ( 铁报 ) was established about a
year ago by Feng Moong Yu who was formerly a member of the Left
Wing of the Kuomintang , and is connected with the Great Crystal
(q.v.). It has a circulation of 9,000 copies. It is published
every 3 days. Address of paper: Tsung Yu Lee at the corner of
Ningpo Road and Lloyd Road.

The Life Weekly ( 生活 ) was established about
8 months ago by Huang Chen Ts and Sung Sing Ching. The latter
was formerly Chief of Provincial Educational Department during the
time of Marshal Sung Chun Fang, and is known by Chinese Newspaper
circles as the Mentor of Sz Liang Zai, the Manager of the Shun
Pao. This paper is well known in educational circles. It has
a circulation of 20,000 copies. It is capitalised at $2,000.
The Manager is Chow Ung Zag . Address: 442 Rue Lafayette,
French Concession.

The Tsing Yeu Ts Yeu ( 青年之友 ) is a paper
started by the clerical staff of the Commercial Press. It is
published under the auspices of the Chun Hwa Vocational
Educationists Association. No information could be secured
regarding its circulation, the name of the Editor, etc.
pages.zh:
-3-

《新罗宾汉》（The New RobinHood）是一份3日一期的“蚊子报”。它由程松风（Cheng Sung Foong，音译）于6个月前创办。几个月后，它被黄玉斋（Huang Yu Tsar，音译）收购并由其管理。发行量为3,000份。报社地址：汉口路附近的东安里（Dong An Lee，音译）。

《铁报》（The Iron News）由冯梦宇（Feng Moong Yu，音译）于大约一年前创办，他曾是国民党左派成员，并与《大晶报》（见上文）有关联。发行量为9,000份。每3天出版一期。报社地址：宁波路与劳合路（Lloyd Road）交界处的宗余里（Tsung Yu Lee，音译）。

《生活》周刊（The Life Weekly）由黄陈氏（Huang Chen Ts，音译）和宋星清（Sung Sing Ching，音译）于大约8个月前创办。后者曾在孙传芳元帅时期担任省教育厅厅长，并被中国新闻界称为《申报》经理史量才（Sz Liang Zai，音译）的导师。这份报纸在教育界很有名。发行量为20,000份。资本为2,000美元。经理为周仰扎（Chow Ung Zag，音译）。地址：法租界霞飞路442号。

《青年之友》（The Tsing Yeu Ts Yeu）是由商务印书馆职员创办的一份报纸。它在中华职业教育社的主持下出版。关于其发行量、编辑姓名等信息，未能获取。

pages.en:
The Chinese News Agency.

The Kuo Wen News Agency ( 國 聞 社 ) is the oldest
agency in Shanghai. It was started by Wu Chang Tsz, a member
of the Anfu Club of which Tsan Chi Jui is the President. The
Agency is subsidised not only by the Anfu Club but also by the
National Government because of its excellent service and its
influence with the Chinese public. The Agency has branches
at Tientsin, Peking and Nanking. The founder resides in
Tientsin. The Manager is Li Tsz Qwan who has a staff of 10 clerks
in Shanghai. Address of Agency: No. 22 Hankow Road.

The Kuo Min News Agency ( 國 民 社 ) was started by
Dang Teh Ming who is a member of the Propaganda Department of the
Shanghai Special District Kuomintang, who also acts as the
Manager of the Agency. It is in receipt of a subsidy from the
National Government. Address of Agency: North Soochow Road near
the Temple of the Queen of Heaven.

The Chun Hwa News Agency ( 中 華 社 ) was established
by Dr. Soume Chen who was at one time appointed President of the
Now defunct Shanghai Provisional Court. It is also in receipt
of a subsidy from the National Government. It has a staff of 6
clerks. Address of Agency: No. 33 Rue Amiral Courbet, French
Concession.

The Jih Jih News Agency ( 日 日 社 ) was started
by Ying Tsai Wei who lives at Nanking. He is also the Manager of
the Agency with a staff of 7 clerks. So far as can be
ascertained the paper has no political connections. Address of
Agency: No. 7 Shangtung Road.

中文通讯社。

国闻社（The Kuo Wen News Agency）是上海最老的通讯社。它由吴昌兹（Wu Chang Tsz，音译）创办，他是安福俱乐部的成员，该俱乐部主席为段祺瑞。该社不仅得到安福俱乐部的资助，还因其出色的服务及其在中国公众中的影响力而得到国民政府的资助。该社在天津、北京和南京设有分部。创始人居住在天津。经理为李子权（Li Tsz Qwan，音译），他在上海有10名职员。通讯社地址：汉口路22号。

国民社（The Kuo Min News Agency）由邓德明（Dang Teh Ming，音译）创办，他是国民党上海特别区宣传部的成员，同时也担任该社经理。它接受国民政府的资助。通讯社地址：天后宫附近的苏州北路。

中华社（The Chun Hwa News Agency）由陈硕美博士（Dr. Soume Chen，音译）创办，他曾被任命为现已撤销的上海临时法院院长。它也接受国民政府的资助。它有6名职员。通讯社地址：法租界古拔路（Rue Amiral Courbet）33号。

日日社（The Jih Jih News Agency）由应载伟（Ying Tsai Wei，音译）创办，他住在南京。他也是该社经理，下有7名职员。据查，该报没有政治背景。通讯社地址：山东路7号。

The Hsin Ming News Agency ( 新 民 社 ) was started
by Tsha Tiao Tu. It does not send out any articles and its
existence is purely nominal. Address of Agency: No. 576
Yunnan Road.

The Dah Chin News Agency ( 大 中 社 ) was started
by Pan Ching Ming, a well known Chinese journalist. He is a
partizan of Feng Yu-hsiang. In the latter half of 1929 when
Feng Yu-hsiang was held captive by General Yen Si Shan, the
News Agency was suspended. The Agency was formerly located
in Kiukiang Road.

The Tung Nan News Agency ( 東 南 社 ) was
established by Chen Ping Psh who lives at Nanking. The Agency
was suspended about a year ago; the cause cannot be ascertained.
The Agency used to be located in Shantung Road.

新民社（The Hsin Ming News Agency）由查调图（Tsha Tiao Tu，音译）创办。它不发送任何稿件，其存在纯属名义上的。通讯社地址：云南路576号。

大中社（The Dah Chin News Agency）由知名中国记者潘景明（Pan Ching Ming，音译）创办。他是冯玉祥的党羽。1929年下半年，当冯玉祥被阎锡山将军扣押时，该通讯社停止运作。该社原址位于九江路。

东南社（The Tung Nan News Agency）由陈平石（Chen Ping Psh，音译）创办，他住在南京。该社大约在一年前停止运作；原因无法查明。该社原址位于山东路。

Dear Mr. Aiers,

With reference to our telephone
conversation of yesterday, I enclose a list of
Chinese newspapers and news agencies as to which

With apologies for troubling you,
Yours sincerely,

R. C. Aiers, Esquire,
Assistant Superintendent,

March 2, 1937. Afternoon Translation.
Eastern Daily News ( 東方日報 ):-
THE WHITE RUSSIAN NEWSPAPERS IN SHANGHAI
Some of the White Russians in Shanghai are formerly members of the Russian royal family. Many are land owners, wealthy business men, etc. They were forced to leave their country and seek shelter in other parts of the world on the outbreak of the revolution in Russia. A great number of them are to be found in Shanghai.
These emigrants are hostile to the Soviet Union and publish papers in Shanghai strongly criticising the present Russian government.
Following the conclusion of the Franco-Soviet Pact, several Russian papers in the local French Concession have been ordered not to publish articles against the Soviet Union. It is reported that some of the papers have suspended publication.

1937年3月2日. 下午译文.
《东方日报》:-
上海的白俄报纸
上海的一些白俄以前是俄国皇室成员。许多人是地主、富商等。俄国革命爆发时，他们被迫离开祖国，在世界其他地方寻求庇护。其中大量的人可以在上海找到。
这些移民敌视苏联，并在上海出版强烈批评现俄罗斯政府的报纸。
随着《法苏互助条约》的签订，当地法租界的几家俄文报纸被命令不得发表反对苏联的文章。据报道，一些报纸已停刊。

S. I. REGISTRY.
No. D/o. 9121/41
Date 1 / 3 / 37
March 1, 1937.
Morning Translation
Lih Pao :-
RUSSIAN EMIGRANTS AND THEIR NEWSPAPERS IN SHANGHAI
Since the revolution in Russia, Shanghai has become a haven for White Russians in the Far East. There are between 20,000 and 30,000 Russian emigrants in Shanghai.
Shanghai has four Russian daily papers and one evening paper. The total circulation of these papers is about 5,000 copies.
The four daily newspapers are: the "Shanghai Zaria", the "Russian Daily News", the "Novy Poot" and the "Slovo"; the evening paper is called the "Zaria Evening News." Of these papers, the "Shanghai Zaria," which was established in 1925 by Mr. Lenbich, is the largest and enjoys the greatest circulation. Its office is located at No. 774 Avenue Joffre. The circulation is about 1,300 copies, while that of the evening edition is about 500.
The "Russian Daily News," No.620 Avenue Foch, comes next. Its founder is Mr. V. Chilikin and its circulation is about 1,000 copies.
The "Novy Poot," address No. 1, Lane 607, Avenue Joffre, ranks as third. This paper suspended publication temporarily on February 27.
The "Slovo" is the smallest. It is published by the Slovo Publishing Company and its office is situated at No. 238 Avenue du Roi Albert. Mr. Altadouroff is the manager of this paper. Its daily circulation is 600 copies.
Two of these papers employ Chinese labourers. Nevertheless, all these papers maintain a common attitude towards the Soviet Union; they leave out as much as possible anything that is said in praise of the good administration of the Soviet Union and express all the Union's faults. For this reason, the Soviet authorities in Shanghai are highly displeased with them.
It is reported in various newspapers that the "Novy Poot" has been banned for criticising Bolshevism and that it has failed to pay $600, the wages of Yang Shao Yung (楊兆熊) and 20 employees. According to reliable information received by this paper, the "Novy Poot" did not suspend its publication on this account but because of financial reasons. Although the said paper is against the Soviet, yet it cannot be said to be the bitterest of all the papers towards the Soviet. It was founded about one and half years ago with a capital of about $26,000. Originally it was a weekly publication but later it was converted into a daily paper. Its editor-in-chief is Mr. Ballod.
It has now suspended publication for the time being.
Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:
EXCHANGE SHOPS AND COPPER COINS
The Bureau of Social Affairs of the Shanghai City Government to-day will hold an informal meeting with representatives of various cigarette and exchange shops to discuss the plot of traitorous merchants to raise the value of copper coins.

上午译文
《立报》:-
上海的俄国移民及其报纸
自俄国革命以来，上海已成为远东白俄的避难所。上海有20,000至30,000名俄国移民。
上海有四家俄文日报和一家晚报。这些报纸的总发行量约为5,000份。
这四家日报是：《上海柴拉报》（Shanghai Zaria）、《俄罗斯日报》（Russian Daily News）、《新路报》（Novy Poot）和《言论报》（Slovo）；晚报名为《柴拉晚报》（Zaria Evening News）。在这些报纸中，由伦比奇先生（Mr. Lenbich）于1925年创办的《上海柴拉报》规模最大，发行量最高。其办事处位于霞飞路774号。发行量约为1,300份，而晚版的发行量约为500份。
《俄罗斯日报》，地址福煦路620号，位居其次。其创始人为V. 奇利金先生（Mr. V. Chilikin），发行量约为1,000份。
《新路报》，地址霞飞路607弄1号，排名第三。该报于2月27日暂时停刊。
《言论报》规模最小。它由言论出版公司（Slovo Publishing Company）出版，办事处位于阿尔贝特国王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）238号。阿尔塔杜罗夫先生（Mr. Altadouroff）是该报经理。其日发行量为600份。
这些报纸中有两家雇佣中国工人。尽管如此，所有这些报纸对苏联都保持着共同的态度；它们尽可能省略任何赞扬苏联良好治理的内容，并揭露联盟的所有缺点。因此，苏联驻上海当局对它们非常不满。
各报报道，《新路报》因批评布尔什维克主义而被禁，且未支付杨兆熊（Yang Shao Yung）及20名员工的工资600美元。根据本报收到的可靠消息，《新路报》并非因此停刊，而是出于财务原因。虽然该报反对苏联，但不能说它是所有报纸中对苏联最激烈的。它成立于约一年半前，资本约为26,000美元。最初是周刊，后来改为日报。其主编为巴洛德先生（Mr. Ballod）。
目前它已暂时停刊。
《大公报》及其他本地报纸：
兑换店与铜元
上海市政府社会局今日将与各家烟纸店和兑换店的代表举行非正式会议，讨论奸商抬高铜元价值的阴谋。

Russian Newspapers and Periodicals

The following alterations in Russian publications
and change of editors took place in Shanghai during the
month of August, 1931 : -
"The Commercial Bulletin" ceased publication.
The Weekly newspaper "Golos" which usually appear-
ed weekly, made its appearance only twice during the
month.
M.C. Lambitch owner and publisher of "Shanghai
Zaria" and "Vechernee Vremia" (Evening Times) has
changed editors of both these newspapers. Mr. A.M.
Dmitrieff is appointed to replace Mr. L. Arnoldoff
who was given two months sick leave, and Mr. A.B.
Petroff has replaced Mr. B. Soovorin who was compel-
led to resign on August 1, 1931.
pages.zh:
1931年8月9日。

俄文报纸与期刊

1931年8月期间，上海俄文出版物发生以下变更及编辑人员变动：-
《商业公报》（The Commercial Bulletin）停刊。
通常每周出版的周报《声音》（Golos），本月仅出版了两期。
《上海朝霞》（Shanghai Zaria）和《晚报》（Vechernee Vremia，即 Evening Times）的所有者兼出版商 M.C. Lambitch 已更换这两份报纸的编辑。任命 A.M. Dmitrieff 先生接替休两个月病假的 L. Arnoldoff 先生；A.B. Petroff 先生接替了被迫于1931年8月1日辞职的 B. Soovorin 先生。

1/8/31.

Russian Newspapers and Periodicals

The following is a correct list and particulars of the
Russian newspapers published in Shanghai at present : -
Daily:
1. "Shanghai Zaria" (Estd. 1925) 551 Avenue Joffre
Editor L.B. Arnoldoff. Publisher & owner M.C. Lembitch.
2. "Slovo" (Estd. 1928) 238 Avenue Du Roi Albert.
Editor P.I. Zaitseff. Owner Mr. Altaduckoff.
3. "Vechernee Vremia" (Evening Time) 117-119 Av. Du Roi Albert.
Editor B.A. Seuvorin. Owner M.C. Lembitch & Coy.
4. "Commercial Bulletin" (1931) 72 Route Vayren App. 4
Editor N.P. Stepanoff. Publishers C. Stepanoff & Coy.
Weekly :
1."Golos" (The Voice) (1931) 118 Route Vallen app. 17
Editor N.P. Malinovsky. Owner Publishing Co. "Golos"
Two Russian Magazines are published and on sale in Shanghai
namely: "Blue Diamond" and "SUB-SENTINEL" a military monthly.

Variations:

The following alterations in Russian Publications took
place during the month of July 1931 : -
"The Evening Zaria" and the morning paper "Vremia" (Time)
ceased publication on July 3rd 1931 and became amalgamated
and commenced a new evening edition called the "Vechernee
Vremia" (The Evening Times) which appeared on the same date.
(Translation of the Editorial's notice is attached herewith).
On July 16, 1931 a new Russian paper appeared in Shanghai
called the "Commercial Bulletin" which is published daily and
devotes itself exclusively to advertisement purposes. It is
being distributed free of charge. Judging on its first issue
this publication comes under the category of "mosquito" type.

1931年8月1日。

以下为目前在上海出版的俄文报纸的正确清单及详情：-
日报：

3. 《晚报》（Vechernee Vremia，即 Evening Time）阿尔伯特国王路117-119号
   编辑 B.A. Seuvorin。所有者 M.C. Lembitch 公司。
4. 《商业公报》（Commercial Bulletin）（1931年）华伦路72号4室
   编辑 N.P. Stepanoff。出版商 C. Stepanoff 公司。
周刊：
1. 《声音》（Golos，即 The Voice）（1931年）瓦伦路118号17室
   编辑 N.P. Malinovsky。所有者“声音”出版公司

上海出版并销售两种俄文杂志，即：《蓝钻》（Blue Diamond）和《副哨兵》（SUB-SENTINEL），后者为军事月刊。

变动情况：

1931年7月期间，俄文出版物发生以下变更：-
《晚朝霞》（The Evening Zaria）和晨报《时报》（Vremia，即 Time）于1931年7月3日停刊，合并后开始发行新的晚刊，名为《晚报》（Vechernee Vremia，即 The Evening Times），并于同日创刊。
（社论公告译文附后）。
1931年7月16日，上海出现了一份新的俄文报纸，名为《商业公报》（Commercial Bulletin），该报每日出版，专用于刊登广告。免费分发。从其首期来看，该出版物属于“蚊子”类小报。

pages.en:
- 2 -

The Russian "Hong List" appeared on sale in Shanghai du-
ring last month. It is published by the Union of Russian
Invalides and the work is very comprehensive and is useful
source of information.

All the above mentioned Russian newspapers pursue an
anti-communist policy and have no other particular politi-
cal tendency, with the exception of "Golos" which professes
republican-democratic sentiments and is edited by one of the
members of the so called "Peasants Party" whose headquarters
is in Prague, Zsechoslovakia.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

上月，俄文《鸿名册》（Hong List）在上海上市销售。该名录由俄国伤残军人联合会出版，内容非常详尽，是有用的信息来源。

上述所有俄文报纸均奉行反共政策，无其他特定政治倾向，但《声音》（Golos）除外，该报宣称持有共和民主情感，其编辑为所谓“农民党”成员之一，该党总部设在捷克斯洛伐克布拉格。

We announce herewith that commencing from Friday July 3rd
1931 the publication of the "Evening Zaria" will be dis-
continued. Simultaneously the morning paper "Vremia" (Times)

The paper will make its first appearance on the above

Supplementing the report on local Russian newspapers,
dated February 11, 1930, attached herewith, three other
Russian publications have since made their appearance in
Shanghai, i.e. the "Dain," "Vremya" and "Armia and Flot."
All of these papers were published previously, but
ceased publication for various reasons, particularly,
political.
The "Dain" (The Day). Some 200 copies of this
publication are printed, but not all are sold. The paper,
a yellow sheet, is published weekly and edited by S.M.
Ogonezeff, who is reported to be supporting the Russian
Facists. He served formerly in Harbin as one of the many
assistants to the Manager of the "Wagon Lits Co.," is
reported to be fairly well off and is looked upon with
a certain amount of suspicion by the other local Russian
editors. The paper cannot be considered as popular and
resembles very much the "Showdown" in the English language,
as it makes certain personal sensational disclosures verging
almost, in some cases, on slander. Ogonezeff possesses his
own printing establishment at 59 Rue Moliere, and has his
editorial office at 21 Moulmein Road. The expenses in
connection with the printing of the "Dain" are not considerable.
The "Rossia" (Russia) was formerly a daily publication
but now appears periodically on Sundays. The editor, Mr.
N.V. Kolesnikoff, a former Colonel of the Russian General
staff, is subsidized by the Japanese Military Clique and
the re-appearance of this paper as also the "Armia and Flot"
(Army & Fleet) also edited and published by Kolesnikoff at
the present moment points to the desire on the part of the

The local editor is Mr. Lev Arnoldov who has been connected
with the paper since its first appearance in Shanghai. The
proof of the popularity of the "Zaria" is to be seen in the
fact that although two other emigre newspapers have made their
appearance here in Shanghai (the "Slovo" and the "Vremya")
within the past year, they have not affected the Zaria's
circulation nor have they caused the management to lower
their advertising and subscription rates.
The political inclinations of the "Zaria" continue to
be the same, namely anti-Bolshevist, pro-Slav, recognizing

platform of common-sense democracy. The "Zaria" tactically
avoids mud-slinging, one of the most ardent passions indulged
in by Russian editors.
The "Slovo" can be classed as a "catch-the-penny" newspaper.
It has been in existence about a year. Its subscription and
advertising rates are exactly half those of the "Zaria."

are anti-Soviet, anti-Jewish, anti-masonic. It opposes Russian

definite object of the restoration of the old Russian Monarchy.
It has close connections with the Monarchist and military
Russian emigre groups in Paris, particularly with the
organization headed by General Koutinoff, who, it is alleged,
has just recently been kidnapped. It is suspected that this
paper receives funds from the Jesuits and it is likewise
asserted that two loans have been provided by the China

《Slovo》模仿 Lembitch 的报纸，并通过俄国漫画家“Sarajou”（即北华捷讯报的 Sarojnikoff）来博取人气。董事会成员包括 Altadukoff、Sarojnikoff、Levitin（Levitsky）和 D. Scherbin 先生，后者曾是道胜银行（Dalbank）的官方经纪人，并于1929年9月在该报资金枯竭时提供财政援助。Levitin 先生是经理，Zaitseff 先生是编辑，他根据 Levitin 的指示偶尔进行人身攻击。该报的政策是吹捧 Grosse 先生。

《Vremya》是上海的白俄君主派出版物。由 Boris Souvorin 先生编辑，他偶尔也进行人身攻击。该报的政治倾向是反苏维埃、反犹太、反共济会。它反对俄国民族主义，极度亲军事，并以恢复旧俄国君主制为明确目标。它与巴黎的君主派和军事俄国流亡群体有着密切联系，特别是与据称最近刚被绑架的 Koutinoff 将军领导的组织。有人怀疑该报从耶稣会士那里获得资金，同样也有人声称中国金融公司提供了两笔贷款。
